chapters.title: Chapter 1701: Avalon
paragraphs: From the start of the battle, Kent knew Elina wasn’t used to her abilities just yet. The power of the Nine Tribulation Dragon wasn’t something that could be mastered easily.
However, to think she was able to hold her own for 30 minutes, Kent realised something wasn’t right. He knew Elina better than anyone.

When they met during the Primordial Era and became friends, Chaos, being sceptical about humans, made it his mission to study her and capture everything he could about her. This led him to know all about Elina’s battle style.
What she had displayed now wasn’t something the old Elina could do. This made him wonder if it had something to do with the star tattoo that he knew was linked to the mysterious Avalon.
But first...
Kent let go of Elina, taking away his dagger while a smile remained on his lips.
"Nice battle, Elina. It’s just that I am too monstrous for your current mastery and control of your power. Perhaps, after you get the hang of your new powers, we can spar again."
She nodded, unsummoning her weapon and armour.

She then jumped into Kent’s arms and locked him into a fierce kiss, one that lasted for ten good minutes. The kiss contained her happiness, gratitude, and a promise to treasure the gift Kent had given her.
She had always wanted to become a dragon, and now, Kent had made her dream come true.
After having had enough of his lips, Elina simply hugged Kent for another ten minutes before pulling away, her cheeks red like a tomato.
"I have dragon horns now," she said, pointing at them.
Kent smiled and nodded. "I can see that, Elina. They look cute, just like you."
She blushed and turned to face Vexthra, Pandora, Yukiko, and Umai.
"I am a dragon now, sisters."
"Congratulations, Elina. You deserve the best."
They smiled and hugged her, making sure she understood how happy they were to see her happy, too.
After sharing a long and heartfelt hug with her sisters, Kent went straight to the point.
"Elina, my love, what can you tell me about the star tattoo on your forehead?"
Elina instinctively reached up to touch the star tattoo on her forehead.
"This... It is the Mark of Avalon."
Kent furrowed his brow.
"Mark of Avalon. Is Avalon a person or a place?" he asked.
However, Elina shook her head.
"I do not know."
Kent was a bit disappointed she wasn’t able to provide any tangible detail. However, before he could say anything else, Pandora asked a question.
"How did you get it?"
The question made Kent turn back to Elina, whose body visibly trembled, almost as if she had recalled something terrifying.
"What is wrong, Elina? Are you alright?" Kent asked, wrapping an arm around her shoulders.
Elina took a deep breath, then exhaled before replying.
"I am fine. It’s just that I felt a bit scared when Big Sister asked that question. The truth is, I would rather forget how I obtained this star mark because it was terrifying."
She exhaled again and, noticing that Kent wanted to know, continued.
"During the last moments of my transformation, my consciousness was taken to a place of absolute darkness. I had no idea where I was or why I had been brought there.

For what felt like an eternity, I was just floating there. However, a few seconds before I returned to my body, I saw the most terrifying sight. A reddish-gold eye opened within the darkness, and when I met its gaze, I felt something open inside my body...
Then I returned to my body with all this knowledge of how to wield the Nine Tribulation Dragon, fight with the glaive, and use many other terrifying techniques."
Elina’s body trembled again.
However, to Kent’s absolute shock, Pandora’s body trembled as well, fear appearing in her eyes.
"Huh, you too?"
Kent was shaken by the sight.
Naturally, Elina’s reaction was normal. After all, she was fragile by nature, and she was also much weaker and younger than Pandora, so being scared was natural to her.
But he never expected the Queen of Evil, who had already stepped into the Primordial Stage, to show such a reaction.
But she did, and that told Kent something.

Whoever Avalon was, they were scary. He was torn between whether Avalon was a person or a place. Now, he knew Avalon was a person, perhaps even a beast, and judging by Pandora’s reaction, even a Primordial was scared of them.
"Pandora, have you met this Avalon before?" Kent asked, and she nodded.

"When I first arrived in this universe, the first thing I saw was that eye and a warning. I didn’t know he was called Avalon. However, he warned me not to dare harm this universe, or else I wouldn’t know how I died.
Later, we met again when I was about to transcend to the Primordial Stage. He gave me a technique that, had it not been for it, I would have died during the ascension ritual.
I always wondered who he might be, but I came up empty." She sighed and looked at the tattoo on Elina’s forehead.
"I don’t know who this Avalon is, but I know they are far stronger than a Primordial. Perhaps you should hold off on investigating them for now."
Kent nodded, but he wasn’t satisfied with just this.
He recognised that Avalon was stronger, far stronger than anything or anyone he had met so far.
However, if that was the case, what did any of this mean? Was Avalon a threat or an ally? Most importantly, why had he given Elina the techniques and his mark?
So many questions remained unanswered, causing Kent to grit his teeth and sigh. He would find out more about Avalon when he got to the Cult of Wisdom.
If there was a place where he could learn something about such an entity, it would be the Cult of Wisdom. Kent decided to push everything to the back of his mind for now.
For today, celebrating Elina’s transformation into a true dragon was the most important thing.
"We should celebrate," Kent suggested, and his wives nodded, every last one of them up for a good celebration.
"MmmmhhHH."
"AaaHHHH."

Some time later, they were all inside the Love House, Elina’s body bathed in sweat as Kent thrust his dick in and out of her. When it came to Kent and his wives, celebrating usually meant a sex marathon.
They had basically everything they would ever need at the moment, so sex seemed like the most important decision any of them could ever come to an agreement on.
Of course, Kent decided to give Elina extra attention today since it was her day. So after thrusting for two hours, he came, filling her with his dragon juice.
He then moved on to Umai, who, up until the moment she and Kent had their first sex, had never expected that one day she would be in bed with the legendary Primordial Chaos Dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 1703: Dreaming the Same Dream
paragraphs: "Sage, you know, this time I feel like I won’t be returning from this battle," a young man with short blue hair and blue eyes said, his expression helpless.
Judging by the coldness around him and the fact that he has an ice tattoo on his forehead, it was clear that his understanding of the ice element is very high.
He grabbed his jug and gulped down the entire contents.
Seated across from him, a handsome half-elf with flowing green hair, a lean physique, and a pair of round eyeglasses resting on his face smiled and also drank his wine.

"That is not the way to start the day, Sahir," Sage said with a smile. "You are one of the best mages in the universe. If anything, you should be worried about the heroic welcome you will receive after you dispose of those Ice Demons."

Sahir smiled and shook his head. "Easy for you to say, Sage. You are the smartest man in the world, and on top of that, you are also a legendary alchemist. But we both know that is merely a front for who you really are, Kevin Sage."
Sahir narrowed his eyes at the half-elf and added, "You are the legendary White Knight, an existence that even the greatest warriors of this era couldn’t measure up to."

Sage smiled and shook his head. "And you are Sahir, the greatest Ice Mage I have ever met. You are a legend, dude, in case you are not aware. You are also a Celestial Supreme and the wielder of a sacred ice. If anything, you will be proving to the Ice Demons what kind of monster you really are."
Sahir smiled and nodded after hearing what his friend said.

To the rest of the universe, Kevin Sage claimed he was merely an alchemist and the smartest man alive, but Sahir knew a different side of him—one that even Pill Celestial Zathoriel Prime had no idea about, until Kevin’s final moment.

During the Ice Age, when the Ice Demons invaded the universe, a legendary knight known as the White Knight, named after the color of his armor, stood at the vanguard, protecting the universe from all kinds of dangers.
In fact, he was the greatest warrior of that era, and Sahir was his best friend, the one to whom Kevin had revealed almost everything about himself.
They shared a deep bond, one that transcended mere friendship.
"You know what, Sage? I think we should become sworn brothers. I long ago promised to fight by your side, and if I had to die to ensure your quest succeeds, I wouldn’t bat an eye.
"However, what would make me sad is dying without having a real brother. So let’s become sworn brothers in blood, and if we return alive, I will convince my sister to marry you."
Sahir said with a smile, causing Kevin Sage to smirk.
"Still very shameless, huh?" Kevin laughed, but then he proceeded to slash his palm, drawing blood. Sahir did the same, and they shook hands.

Kevin Sage spoke some strange words, and their blood mixed, forming the tattoo of a spider on each other’s arms. "In the next life, I will look for you, Sahir. Just make sure you die in a dignified way."
Sahir nodded with a smile. When nobody believed he could ever become a mage, Pill Celestial Kevin Sage did, and that led him to become one of the best.
Years later, during the climax of the battle, to kill two Pseudo-Primordial Ice Demon Generals, Sahir burned his soul and life force, unleashing the greatest spell the universe had ever seen.
"Ice Emperor’s Descent."
That technique not only killed two Pseudo-Primordials but also bought Kevin Sage enough time to push back the remaining Ice Demon Generals and seal the Ice Gate.
Sahir, or as they call him to this day, the Ice Emperor, was the sole reason the Ice Age survived. He sacrificed his life to save everyone.
On his dying breath, he smiled and muttered, "Being one of the good guys is indeed terrible."
A young man with short blue hair jolted awake from his sleep, his brow soaked in sweat.
"No, that dream again," he muttered, moving his body to sit at the edge of his bed.
He used his right hand to wipe the sweat off his brow and sighed. Then he turned and looked at a black-and-white uniform hanging on the wall and smirked.
"Why do I still have that hanging there, taking up space? It’s not like I would ever become a mage."
He threw another smirk at the uniform as though its presence was a constant reminder of his failure to join one of the mage sects on Planet Dormaa.
He tried several times, but he was always met with the same sentence:
"Your affinity for ice is the lowest I have ever seen."
And with such a response, rejection inevitably followed.
After several tries and failures, he gave up and took a job as a server at a prominent restaurant, where he worked his ass off for a few spirit stones.

After freshening up, he quickly made his way out and, after a twenty-minute trek, arrived at the Everyday Inn Restaurant. He quickly fixed his appearance and started serving customers and taking orders.
Two hours into his shift, the gate opened, and a group of youngsters walked in—three males and three females—causing the look on Sahir’s face to change.
He recognized them, and knowing the kind of trouble they were, he frowned.
After all, he had once tried to join the Grand Arcane Mage Sect alongside them, only to be rejected.

And he wasn’t the only one affected by the sudden appearance of the six disciples. The other servers also frowned, some retreating to other tables. They had no plans of dealing with the overprivileged kids today.
In the end, it was Sahir who approached them, and with the smile expected of a waiter, he spoke.
"Welcome to Everyday Inn. What would you like to order today?"
The six youngsters looked at Sahir, and for a moment, they said nothing.
Then, out of nowhere, they burst into resounding laughter.
"If it isn’t our overly confident waiter who thinks becoming a mage is as simple as serving food."
One of the young men, Cole, blurted out, drawing many diners’ attention.
Some of them sympathized with Sahir, while others merely smiled and shook their heads. They knew Sahir was a nobody, so being teased was, in a way, normal.
Sahir kept his composure and even managed a small smile.
He was being humiliated, but the last thing he wanted was to offend any of them. All six youngsters were Six-Circle Mages, or as they were commonly called, High Mages.
So offending them was the last thing he wanted.
"Such is the world of the strong. They get to do whatever they want without consequences," a man seated with two ladies muttered before returning to his food.
Meanwhile, Cole and his squad continued to tease Sahir for a good ten minutes before finally ordering their meals.
Sahir took their order, the professional that he was, and went to fetch their food.
"What a loser," Fiona muttered, brushing the back of Cole’s hand.
"Hey, why don’t we play a game?" Gideon suddenly suggested, causing his friends to turn toward him.
"What kind of game?" Steven asked, already interested even though he hadn’t heard the details yet.
"It’s simple. How much do you think it would cost to convince the owner to make that loser our personal dessert table?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1704: Humiliation
paragraphs: Sahir may live in an Immortal world, but he was only a Root Ascension Stage cultivator. He hadn’t even formed his Core yet, so naturally, going against Immortal Lords was far beyond his level.
He had suffered to get this job, and so despite the daily verbal abuse he received from customers who came to dine at the Everyday Inn Restaurant, he never dreamt of quitting.
He knew it would be hard for a mortal like him to find another decent job like this.
Customers came and went, many unleashing loads of insults on him before leaving.
But he endured it all like a man until today, when he was being forced to go down on all fours so his back could serve as a table to hold the dishes the six youngsters had ordered.

All six of them were core disciples of the Grand Arcane Mage Sect, so they held some power. The sect was their backer, and knowing their reputation, it wouldn’t be too far-fetched if they ordered the demolition of the restaurant.
So the owner, despite the unreasonable request they had made, had no choice but to oblige.

"Sahir, just do as they say, and it will be over soon," Lady Abba said, her expression showing how sorry she was for ordering one of her workers, perhaps her favorite, to become a table for the unreasonable High Mages.
"You heard the woman. Go down on your knees and become our table. We are willing to throw in 10,000 Spirit Stones as a tip for your hard work," Cole said, wearing a mocking expression.

"Don’t be an ungrateful brat. Our offer is one-of-a-kind. A mere mortal like you doesn’t even qualify to stand before us, so you should be thankful we are willing to put your miserable life to good use."
Fanicia, one of the best High Mages in the Grand Arcane Mage Sect, shouted at Sahir, who stood his ground, not budging despite the dozens of eyes on him.
He just wouldn’t do it, and that could be seen in his eyes.
He could endure all kinds of humiliation, but this had crossed his bottom line. He would not become a table, and that could be seen and sensed from him.
"I am sorry, Lady Abba. I appreciate you employing me, but I suppose today is the day I quit," he sighed, then turned away and started to walk off.
Many who were disgusted by the behavior of the six High Mages sighed and smiled at Sahir’s resolve. They even gave him a thumbs-up for not allowing himself to be humiliated.

However, perhaps they shouldn’t have celebrated so early. Just when Sahir had taken his fifth step, a spell circle appeared beneath his feet, and chains burst out, grabbing hold of his legs, hands, and neck.
In an instant, Sahir’s body was locked down.
"Who said you could leave, bastard?" Fanicia shouted, her arms moving in a graceful arc as thousands of ice needles formed and pointed at Sahir’s head.

He was completely locked down, unable to even lift a finger. As a mortal, facing an Immortal Lord meant death, and Sahir knew that. However, instead of trying to break free, he remained calm, his eyes closed.
He had accepted his fate, and if he were to be frank with himself, death at this point was the easiest way out. Life had been cruel to him, and so death would at least end it all.
Cole, Steven, Fiona, Gideon, and Dina smiled as they watched Fanicia lock Sahir down.
"Please, kindly spare him. He is just a kid who doesn’t know how to appreciate the kindness of his seniors." Lady Abba pleaded, her body trembling as she looked at the coldness in Fanicia’s eyes.
The young lady smirked at Lady Abba and then waved her hand, pulling Sahir back and causing his body to slam into a chair beside her. His head struck the knob of the chair, drawing blood.
Sahir clutched his head as pain from the impact traveled through his body.
Lady Abba staggered back, her expression pale as she stared at the sight of Sahir bleeding. Tears fell from her eyes. She was a nobody, even if she owned a restaurant.
Just like Sahir, she was also a failed mage who wanted to live for herself. So, with the little she had, she opened a restaurant, and thanks to her good menu, it became popular rather quickly.
Later, she employed people just like her—people whose dreams had been cut short because they couldn’t meet the standards of the cultivation world.
Sahir was one of her best workers, but now, as he lay at the mercy of the High Mage, all she could do was helplessly stare at him.
Tears rolled down her face, and when their gazes met, she silently conveyed how sorry she was to Sahir.
"I am sorry, kid," she muttered.

"Bastard, I gave you a chance, but you clearly don’t appreciate my kindness. Now, I will teach you a lesson," Fanicia waved her hand, and the needles she had formed moved, aiming to cripple Sahir for good.

However, just before the needles could get within four inches of Sahir, a cold breeze swept past everyone, and the needles shattered. Then a voice, cold and deadly, spoke, instantly filling the restaurant with an overwhelming killing intent.
"There are always those who, against all odds, choose to court death."
BANG!
The restaurant’s door exploded inward, and Kent walked through, his steps leaving a trail of ice on the floor. Every step he took caused the restaurant to tremble.

The six High Mages froze in place, their expressions turning pale as Kent approached them. They felt a heavy pressure descend upon their shoulders, the kind they could not shrug off, no matter how hard they tried.
Unfortunately for them, Kent had no intention of letting them leave today. With every step he took, the pressure pressing down on them multiplied.
By the time he stopped beside Sahir, all six of them were on the ground, their bodies pressed flat against the tiled floor.
Kent gazed down at Fanicia, whose expression had turned pale white.
"You dare hurt my brother?" he muttered coldly, and with a wave of his hand, a spear shot forward and pierced her head, killing her instantly.
He then turned and looked at the five remaining High Mages, a faint smirk appearing on his face.
He crouched down and looked at Sahir.
A smile appeared on Kent’s face when their gazes met.
"Life hasn’t been good to you, huh, buddy?" Kent asked.
Despite having no idea who Kent was, Sahir nodded.
It was only after he nodded that he realized what he had done, but by then it was already too late. This made him become confused.

Kent smirked and said, "Same here, buddy. I lived a miserable life for thirty-two years before everything finally turned around for me. Now, I am living the best time of my life and soon, you’ll too."
He reached forward and offered his hand to Sahir, who, once again, accepted it without knowing why.
It was as though he could trust Kent completely despite this being their first meeting.
Kent pulled him to his feet, and then, with a wave of his hand, a chain flew toward them. He placed it in Sahir’s hands.
"I am proud of you, buddy. You refused to be humiliated any further. That shows character, and I admire that.
"However, for daring to humiliate my brother, I, Kent Madson, will kill all of you. And whoever dares come seeking revenge will be dealt with accordingly."
Kent waved his hand, and five spears appeared.
Before anyone could plead on behalf of the five High Mages, the spears shot forward.
The five of them felt a sharp pain flash through their minds as the spears pierced their heads.
A moment later, five lifeless bodies collapsed onto the floor.

chapters.title: Chapter 1705: Bond Between Brothers
paragraphs: Nobody expected things to get bloody in an instant.
To many who witnessed the start of it all, they knew Sahir was done for, and that conclusion was reached because he was merely a mortal, while the six High Mages were Immortals.
However, in what appeared to be the most unexpected turn of events, Kent killed all six of them without batting an eye.
In that instant, everyone knew what would follow.
A sect values its core disciples so much that their lives are tied to the Life Crystal Hall, a relic within the sect.
As long as a crystal remains whole, it means the one whose life was tied to it was still alive. However, the moment it cracks, it signifies either death or grave danger.

Today, the one in charge of monitoring the Life Crystals in the Grand Arcane Mage Sect suddenly turned pale when a Life Crystal shattered. His body froze, and for a moment, he doubted what he had just seen.
However, a few seconds later, after five more shattered, he was forced to accept reality, sending him running out of the room.
He crossed the 30-kilometre distance in less than five seconds, bursting through the door leading to the Grand Hall, where the Sect Master and six high-ranking elders usually gathered.
"Who dares disturb us?" Elder Haneul shouted, veins bulging on his forehead. A terrible pressure descended upon the Life Crystal Guardian, forcing him to his knees.
"Relax, Haneul. Let’s hear what he has to say," Sect Master Kaidrenn stated, causing Elder Haneul to withdraw the pressure.
"Speak," Elder Haneul shouted.
"They... They shattered," the Life Crystal Guardian muttered. He caught his breath before adding more context. "The Life Crystals of six disciples shattered."
"What?"
Sect Master Kaidrenn and the six elders with him exclaimed, their expressions turning grim. He waved his hand, and all of them vanished from the room, appearing inside the Life Crystal Storage Hall.
When their gazes landed on the shattered Life Crystals, their expressions darkened. Every last one of them became so enraged that the room trembled.
"Who dares kill disciples of my Grand Arcane Mage Sect?" Sect Master Kaidrenn shouted, his voice spreading throughout the sect.
DONG! DONG! DONG!
Bells rang from every corner of the sect, and disciples and elders alike started gathering at a clearing. Whenever bells like these rang, it meant the sect was under attack, so they came running.
However, when they arrived, they saw no battle. Instead, they met the sight of the Sect Master and the six Grand Elders working together to open the Grand Arcane Gate.
Most importantly, they saw a flicker of a soul hovering before the gate.
Most recognised who the soul belonged to.
This caused them to widen their eyes since the only way this soul would be out is if the owner is in danger..
"Isn’t that Big Sister Fiona’s soul?" a disciple asked his friends, who looked wide-eyed.
"It is her soul. But why is she here, though? Shouldn’t she be contained within a Life Crystal or whatever they call it?"
His question went unanswered when the Sect Master spoke.
"All inner and outer disciples, channel your energy into the Arcane Gate. Core disciples, maintain its stability, and sect elders, follow me inside."
It is well known that the Grand Arcane Mage Sect possesses a method of travelling between planets using a tremendous amount of soul energy.
With enough soul power, they can tear holes through the void and travel to any planet within mere seconds.

Today, using Fiona’s soul as a conduit, they decided to hunt down the one who dared kill their disciples. Since the victims had been slain, the killer would bear their resentful marks, making it easy to track him down.
The moment the gate opened, Sect Master Kaidrenn jumped in, followed by the elders and Grand Elders.
Back on Planet Dormaa, after slaughtering the six High Mages, Kent turned and looked at Sahir.
"Sorry for coming too late, brother." Kent apologised.
After all, when he received the quest to find Sahir a couple of weeks ago, he should have immediately dispatched the shadow fiends. Instead, he waited a little longer before doing so.
As a result, he had nearly arrived too late.
Had he been only a few minutes later, perhaps Sahir would have suffered an even graver fate. Fortunately, he arrived just as things were about to escalate.
Even so, he was still pissed to find his sworn brother standing at death’s door.
"Young man, you have to run now before they arrive," Lady Abba said, shivering from the horrific incident that had unfolded inside her restaurant.
She knew she was finished. After all, six High Mages had died in her establishment.
That was not good, and as someone who knew just how unreasonable Immortals could be, she began to panic.
"Take Sahir with you and run."

Kent turned and looked at the woman he had originally intended to kill, but later changed his mind about. It turned out that teleporting to the location of his shadow fiends takes more time than teleporting to his wives or legion, especially the farther away they were from him.
So, while on his way, he witnessed how Lady Abba initially tried to convince Sahir to comply with the High Mages’ demands. However, he also saw how she later pleaded on his behalf.
Right now, hearing her warn him despite knowing that when those people arrived, she would likely be the first to die, made Kent forgive her.
However, he was not about to leave.
"They are coming, huh? Better. They would save me the headache of going to them myself."
Of course, he had no plans to go after the Grand Arcane Mage Sect. He came for Sahir, not to cause unnecessary trouble.
However, since they were coming to him, he would wait and make sure his fame spread even further.
"Relax, Sahir. Once everything is over, I will take you back home and make sure every weakness you’re feeling now becomes a thing of the past."
Sahir nodded, and once again, he wondered why he did so. A part of him felt at ease knowing Kent had his back. However, he kept wondering why he trusted him.
Of course, he had heard Kent’s name before.
Who hadn’t?
However, this was their first meeting. That meant they had never met before, so how could they be brothers? As far as he could recall, his late parents had never told him he had another sibling.
So why was Kent calling him brother?
He tried to make sense of everything but came up empty.

Kent could tell Sahir was struggling to understand what was happening. Judging by the look on his face, he was struggling greatly. Even so, Kent said nothing, knowing that everything would make sense soon.
The quest that helped him locate Sahir Came with rewards that would restore Sahir to his previous peak state.

Suddenly, the clouds outside churned violently, prompting everyone inside the restaurant to rush out. Many people outside also sensed the terrifying pressure emanating from the heavens and immediately started running.
BOOOOOM
Suddenly, a bolt of lightning descended from the clouds, blasting a hole through the restaurant’s roof.
Inside, Kent waved his hand, creating a shield around himself. Sahir, Lady Abba, and a few others chose to remain.
"The one who dared kill disciples of my Grand Arcane Mage Sect should come out now and accept his punishment."
Sect Master Kaidrenn’s voice descended from the clouds, shaking the entire planet.
"Why don’t you come instead? I’m too lazy to walk right now."
Kent responded, and another bolt blasted the roof clean off this time.

sentences.text: Nobody expected things to get bloody in an instant.
To many who witnessed the start of it all, they knew Sahir was done for, and that conclusion was reached because he was merely a mortal, while the six High Mages were Immortals.
However, in what appeared to be the most unexpected turn of events, Kent killed all six of them without batting an eye.
In that instant, everyone knew what would follow.
A sect values its core disciples so much that their lives are tied to the Life Crystal Hall, a relic within the sect.
As long as a crystal remains whole, it means the one whose life was tied to it was still alive.
However, the moment it cracks, it signifies either death or grave danger.
Today, the one in charge of monitoring the Life Crystals in the Grand Arcane Mage Sect suddenly turned pale when a Life Crystal shattered.
His body froze, and for a moment, he doubted what he had just seen.
However, a few seconds later, after five more shattered, he was forced to accept reality, sending him running out of the room.
He crossed the 30-kilometre distance in less than five seconds, bursting through the door leading to the Grand Hall, where the Sect Master and six high-ranking elders usually gathered.
"Who dares disturb us?" Elder Haneul shouted, veins bulging on his forehead.
A terrible pressure descended upon the Life Crystal Guardian, forcing him to his knees.
"Relax, Haneul.
Let’s hear what he has to say," Sect Master Kaidrenn stated, causing Elder Haneul to withdraw the pressure.
"Speak," Elder Haneul shouted.
"They...
They shattered," the Life Crystal Guardian muttered.
He caught his breath before adding more context.
"The Life Crystals of six disciples shattered."
"What?"
Sect Master Kaidrenn and the six elders with him exclaimed, their expressions turning grim.
He waved his hand, and all of them vanished from the room, appearing inside the Life Crystal Storage Hall.
When their gazes landed on the shattered Life Crystals, their expressions darkened.
Every last one of them became so enraged that the room trembled.
"Who dares kill disciples of my Grand Arcane Mage Sect?" Sect Master Kaidrenn shouted, his voice spreading throughout the sect.
DONG!
DONG!
DONG!
Bells rang from every corner of the sect, and disciples and elders alike started gathering at a clearing.
Whenever bells like these rang, it meant the sect was under attack, so they came running.
However, when they arrived, they saw no battle.
Instead, they met the sight of the Sect Master and the six Grand Elders working together to open the Grand Arcane Gate.
Most importantly, they saw a flicker of a soul hovering before the gate.
Most recognised who the soul belonged to.
This caused them to widen their eyes since the only way this soul would be out is if the owner is in danger..
"Isn’t that Big Sister Fiona’s soul?" a disciple asked his friends, who looked wide-eyed.
"It is her soul.
But why is she here, though?
Shouldn’t she be contained within a Life Crystal or whatever they call it?"
His question went unanswered when the Sect Master spoke.
"All inner and outer disciples, channel your energy into the Arcane Gate.
Core disciples, maintain its stability, and sect elders, follow me inside."
It is well known that the Grand Arcane Mage Sect possesses a method of travelling between planets using a tremendous amount of soul energy.
With enough soul power, they can tear holes through the void and travel to any planet within mere seconds.
Today, using Fiona’s soul as a conduit, they decided to hunt down the one who dared kill their disciples.
Since the victims had been slain, the killer would bear their resentful marks, making it easy to track him down.
The moment the gate opened, Sect Master Kaidrenn jumped in, followed by the elders and Grand Elders.
Back on Planet Dormaa, after slaughtering the six High Mages, Kent turned and looked at Sahir.
"Sorry for coming too late, brother." Kent apologised.
After all, when he received the quest to find Sahir a couple of weeks ago, he should have immediately dispatched the shadow fiends.
Instead, he waited a little longer before doing so.
As a result, he had nearly arrived too late.
Had he been only a few minutes later, perhaps Sahir would have suffered an even graver fate.
Fortunately, he arrived just as things were about to escalate.
Even so, he was still pissed to find his sworn brother standing at death’s door.
"Young man, you have to run now before they arrive," Lady Abba said, shivering from the horrific incident that had unfolded inside her restaurant.
She knew she was finished.
After all, six High Mages had died in her establishment.
That was not good, and as someone who knew just how unreasonable Immortals could be, she began to panic.
"Take Sahir with you and run."
Kent turned and looked at the woman he had originally intended to kill, but later changed his mind about.
It turned out that teleporting to the location of his shadow fiends takes more time than teleporting to his wives or legion, especially the farther away they were from him.
So, while on his way, he witnessed how Lady Abba initially tried to convince Sahir to comply with the High Mages’ demands.
However, he also saw how she later pleaded on his behalf.
Right now, hearing her warn him despite knowing that when those people arrived, she would likely be the first to die, made Kent forgive her.
However, he was not about to leave.
"They are coming, huh?
Better.
They would save me the headache of going to them myself."
Of course, he had no plans to go after the Grand Arcane Mage Sect.
He came for Sahir, not to cause unnecessary trouble.
However, since they were coming to him, he would wait and make sure his fame spread even further.
"Relax, Sahir.
Once everything is over, I will take you back home and make sure every weakness you’re feeling now becomes a thing of the past."
Sahir nodded, and once again, he wondered why he did so.
A part of him felt at ease knowing Kent had his back.
However, he kept wondering why he trusted him.
Of course, he had heard Kent’s name before.
Who hadn’t?
However, this was their first meeting.
That meant they had never met before, so how could they be brothers?
As far as he could recall, his late parents had never told him he had another sibling.
So why was Kent calling him brother?
He tried to make sense of everything but came up empty.
Kent could tell Sahir was struggling to understand what was happening.
Judging by the look on his face, he was struggling greatly.
Even so, Kent said nothing, knowing that everything would make sense soon.
The quest that helped him locate Sahir Came with rewards that would restore Sahir to his previous peak state.
Suddenly, the clouds outside churned violently, prompting everyone inside the restaurant to rush out.
Many people outside also sensed the terrifying pressure emanating from the heavens and immediately started running.
BOOOOOM
Suddenly, a bolt of lightning descended from the clouds, blasting a hole through the restaurant’s roof.
Inside, Kent waved his hand, creating a shield around himself.
Sahir, Lady Abba, and a few others chose to remain.
"The one who dared kill disciples of my Grand Arcane Mage Sect should come out now and accept his punishment."
Sect Master Kaidrenn’s voice descended from the clouds, shaking the entire planet.
"Why don’t you come instead?
I’m too lazy to walk right now."
Kent responded, and another bolt blasted the roof clean off this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 1706: An Angry Dragon is a Dangerous Dragon
paragraphs: The clouds churned violently as though a heavenly tribulation were about to descend upon everyone. Clearly, Kent’s response to Sect master Kaidrenn’s command had angered them, and they were determined to show him who was in charge.
RUMBLE
BOOOOOM
Another bolt of lightning struck the restaurant, destroying it this time. Many people in the distance gasped as they watched the walls crumble.
Many of them had dined at this restaurant before. However, it had now been reduced to rubble. While the foundation remained intact, it would no longer be serving anyone food.
However, despite the lightning possessing enough power to destroy even Immortal Lords, Kent and the people inside the restaurant remained unharmed.
Kent had ensured their safety by shielding them within an ice dome.
The moment the building collapsed, the clouds parted, revealing Sect Master Kaidrenn and twelve elders. Their expressions were dark as they stared at Kent, who sat with his legs crossed.
Compared to Sahir and the others, whose faces were filled with terror, Kent appeared completely relaxed.
"Identify yourself, brat. Are you the one who killed my disciples?" Sect Master Kaidrenn demanded, his expression grim.
He did not like what he was seeing, and that feeling only intensified at the sight of the six corpses with spears protruding from their heads.
Kent had deliberately left their bodies intact for their elders to see exactly how they had been killed.
Kent looked back at Sect Master Kaidrenn and smiled. "I go by Kent Madson, and yes, I was the one who killed them. As for why, it was because they looked down and hurt my brother."
The expressions of Sect Master Kaidrenn and the elders of the Grand Arcane Mage Sect changed the moment they heard Kent introduce himself.
Kent Madson was a being known throughout the universe, so his appearance here was unexpected. Even more shocking was the fact that he had killed six of their disciples.
If he had been anyone else, they would have attacked him already. However, Kent was different, and that made them hesitate.
"Kent Madson or not, that doesn’t give you the right to kill my disciples," Sect Master Kaidrenn said, his fists clenched.
"So, what are you going to do about it?" Kent asked, causing the thirteen individuals to frown even more deeply.
Seeing this, Kent smiled, stood up, and hovered a few meters above the ground.
"Do you losers have any idea who this young man is?" Kent asked, pointing at Sahir, who certainly had not expected to become the centre of attention when he woke up that morning.
Yet here he was.

"Let me open your eyes today, you scums. The person your uncultured disciples tried to humiliate and harm was once hailed as the greatest Ice Mage to ever walk this universe. His spells shook battlefields, and his presence gave hope to mages and warriors alike.
If not for him, this universe would not enjoy the peace it has today. If not for his sacrifice, none of this would exist. So you had better show him the respect he deserves before it is too late.
Trust me, it would be in your best interest to turn around and leave right now."

Sahir felt something stir within him for a moment, causing him to smile. However, just as it came, it vanished. Even so, while the others looked at Kent with doubtful eyes, he looked at him with belief.

"What kind of nonsense are you spewing, brat? So what if your name is Kent Madson? Do you think you can justify killing six core disciples of the Grand Arcane Mage Sect and fabricate a story to win public sympathy?" Elder Haneul shouted, pointing his mage staff at Kent.

He and the other five Grand Elders were Grand Mages, while the other six Elders were Master Mages. However, Sect Master Kaidrenn was an Archmage, one of the best and most highly respected Archmages in the Eastern Region.
So, for Kent to be treating them like children infuriated him.
Kent narrowed his eyes at the elder who spoke and then smirked.
"I don’t need anyone’s sympathy. I only said that because it is the truth. Also, the only reason you are still alive is that I have great respect for mages.
That said, if you thirteen don’t want to see me angry, turn around and leave before you provoke me. As you already know, the saying: "An angry dragon is a dangerous dragon."
The air around Kent began to shift.
Sect Master Kaidrenn immediately noticed the change, and as someone capable of casting up to sixty-five spell circles, he knew that fighting Kent was bad news.
However, if he left now without avenging his disciples, he would become a laughingstock among his peers.
He certainly could not leave without making sure this Kent Madson kid understood that there were consequences to one’s actions.
"Grand Arcane Formation."
His staff moved, and a fifty-four-layered spell circle appeared, causing a powerful pressure to descend upon Kent.
However, Kent merely stood there with his hands clasped behind his back.
"Reinforce the formation and make sure this bastard learns not to offend the Grand Arcane Mage Sect ever again."
The elders formed seals and then pointed at the formation.
It immediately became even more powerful. Seeing this, Kent used his Omniscient Jade Eyes to scan it and discovered that the core of the formation was being imbued with soul essence.
’So it’s a soul attack, huh? I want to see if it can even scratch my soul.’
He smiled and waited for the formation to fully take shape. Twelve seconds later, it completed itself and stabilised.

Kent saw that the core had become so saturated with energy that he felt an urge to attack and destroy it. However, recalling that his soul had already reached the peak of the Demigod Stage and that his Soul Universe had expanded once more, he stopped himself.
On top of that, he still possessed soul immunity.
Sect Master Kaidrenn wasted no time and gestured downward, his voice booming across the area.
"Soul Eraser!"
A purple beam fired from the formation and struck Kent’s body before, bathing him in a purple radiance.
Sahir and everyone watching gasped, not because Kent had been attacked, but because he made no effort to defend himself.
Even Sect Master Kaidrenn and the elders were stunned when they saw Kent simply standing there as the attack engulfed him.
Kent, however, smiled from within the Soul Eraser beam.

’Looks like this formation can kill a normal True God with a weak soul. Unfortunately, my soul is simply too vast and too energetic. Even two hundred more attacks like this wouldn’t make me feel a thing.’
He remained within the beam for as long as it lasted.
When the beam finally receded, and his flawless body was revealed, everyone gasped again, their eyes widening in disbelief.
Sect Master Kaidrenn and the twelve elders turned pale as they saw Kent standing there with a faint smile on his face.
"Told you it would be wise to turn around and leave. However, now that you’ve attacked me, it’s only fair that I do the same."
He grinned and raised his left hand.
"Don’t worry, I won’t kill you. But you’re going to wish I did."
"Underworld Soul River."
He muttered the words before snapping his fingers, manifesting the massive and terrifying Gates of the Underworld Soul River.
The thirteen mages turned completely pale.

chapters.title: Chapter 1707: Terror
paragraphs: So many changes had occurred since Kent last used the Underworld Soul River.

The first was his rise from a mortal to an immortal. This ascension had significantly boosted his strength, but it had also elevated his soul from a mortal one to an Immortal one, making him even more dangerous.
But while that ascension made his soul stronger, the Underworld Soul River had also become more powerful and, by extension, more horrifying.
He unlocked some of its abilities, and with the awakening of his Evil Qi, it had become something even more terrifying.
Inside his soul sea, even Lady Kenzie dared not come close to the colossal door that seemed to hold so much evil behind its giant gates.

The most chilling part was that when Kent awakened his Bone Lich Undead Emperor, the Underworld Soul River had started leaking a potent death qi, one that had covered a 200-kilometre radius of the door.

Today, as the giant gates appeared, the 13 elders found themselves within the range of that death qi. Aside from that, the natural soul suppression and evil qi surrounding it had taken hold of all 13 of them.
BOOOM
They fell from the sky and slammed into the ground, their bodies trembling in sheer terror. However, Kent ignored them, waved his hand, and shouted,
"Open."
CRACK

The gates moved, and as if giants were pushing them, they slowly parted, revealing a crimson river. The previous dark river seemed to have transformed after so many changes had happened to Kent’s soul.
This time, the river was crimson, and the most chilling part was that, the moment it was revealed, humming sounds began to come from beyond the gates.
To ordinary ears, or those not included within Kent’s attack range, the humming surprisingly sounded melodious.
However, to the 13 elders, the humming was like knives stabbing their souls.
"AAARRRGGHHHH..."
Their screams filled the space as they started rolling across the floor, some clawing at their faces.
It was as if someone or something had taken control of their bodies, making them do things they would not do naturally.
However, as blood started pouring from their scratched faces, noses, ears, and more, it became clear that they were experiencing something extremely evil.
"AARRGGHH... P-please... make it... arrgghhh... make it stop, please," Sect Master Kaidrenn pleaded, his face covered in scratch marks.
He had clawed his own face to the point that flesh could be seen sticking to his nails.
"You want me to stop, but you still aren’t apologising to my brother and me," Kent said with a smirk.

To the untrained and ordinary eye, what was happening seemed ordinary, but those who could see deeply saw millions of liches crawling across the bodies of the 13 elders, causing them to scratch themselves.
To them, they were being eaten alive by liches. However, all of this was merely a terrifying illusion ability that came from the Underworld Soul River.
If Kent wanted to, he could keep the Underworld Soul River active for a few more minutes. However, his soul soon began to feel the toll.
So, after a few more seconds, he deactivated the gates, freeing the 13 elders. Some collapsed, while others continued to scratch their bodies and roll on the ground like madmen.
Kent shook his head and laughed. "All high and mighty, but after a mere display of just one skill, none of you could stand. How pitiful."

He walked toward Sect Master Kaidrenn and muttered coldly, "I am letting you live today not because you deserve it, but because you have done nothing personally to my brother. You should be grateful for that.

The next time you dare point your weapons at him, or anyone present here, I will lay waste to your precious sect, and there is nothing you or anyone else can do to stop me. Trust me, when it comes to destroying things, I excel at the."
Kent smirked and walked back. "Now, get the hell out of my sight."
He waved his hand, and the bodies of the 13 elders were hurled upward. Before anyone could wonder what had happened, they entered the portal they had come through, and it closed behind them.
Back at the Grand Arcane Mage Sect, all 13 elders fell out of the formation, some snapping awake due to the impact, while others remained unconscious.
Every disciple in the sect became quiet, some rushing to the side of the elders who had just been released through the portal.
They never expected the same energetic elders who had left with revenge in their eyes to return broken and, judging by the looks on their faces, terrified.
"Take them inside," some of the core disciples instructed, and the disciples carried the elders away while the healer mages began treating them.
Thousands of disciples scrambled to ensure no threats came near the injured elders.
A few minutes after the elders returned, five white-bearded men appeared and, with a wave of their mage staffs, created a dome around the sect.
Even without personally seeing the sect master and the elders, they could sense the lingering evil intent surrounding them. This told them they had offended someone they should never have provoked.
So, with their combined strength, they formed a 24-layer formation around the sect. Even with Kent’s strength, breaking a Tier 24 formation would be extremely difficult.
In fact, he would not even try. A Tier 24 formation at full strength could kill even God Kings, so he would not take that risk.
Unbeknownst to them, Kent had no intention of pursuing the Elders or causing trouble for the Sect master Kaidrenn
Before arriving on Planet Dormaa, he was already aware that it was one of the 13 planets under the protection of the Grand Arcane Mage Sect.

This meant destroying the sect was akin to putting countless innocent people in danger. So he had no intention of destroying them. But scaring them was something he did intend to do, and now it seemed he had done it.
Kent turned and looked at Lady Abba as he descended from the sky.
"Thank you for providing my brother with a stable job and trying to defend him when he found himself in danger. As a reward, I will rebuild your restaurant and make it even better than before.
I will also ensure that nobody dares to trouble you again. Lastly, I will help you expand your reach to other planets and galaxies and, perhaps one day, even the God Realm."
Kent snapped his fingers, and Gaia appeared beside him.
"This is Gaia. She is good at building things. She and her friends will work together to rebuild your restaurant. For now, just relax and let them work."
As he said that, Akira, Dori, Li Hua, Yuna, and the rest of the Loli Gang arrived, their small bodies and cute appearances causing many people to wish they could play with them.
Kent had no idea how Gaia, Akira, and Dori had managed it, but it seemed that all the lolis who had joined their unofficial Loli legion had now become builders.
They no longer merely escorted the three Cosmic Lolis.
They now actively participated in construction and engineering projects.
Kent planned to find out what Gaia had done to them, but for now, he wanted them to focus on rebuilding the Everyday Inn Restaurant into one of the grandest restaurants on Planet Dormaa.
And just as he had done for Veth and Lady Wu, he would make sure that when it came to the restaurant business, Lady Abba would become uncontested.

He waved his hand, and the bodies of the 13 elders were hurled upward.
Before anyone could wonder what had happened, they entered the portal they had come through, and it closed behind them.
Back at the Grand Arcane Mage Sect, all 13 elders fell out of the formation, some snapping awake due to the impact, while others remained unconscious.
Every disciple in the sect became quiet, some rushing to the side of the elders who had just been released through the portal.
They never expected the same energetic elders who had left with revenge in their eyes to return broken and, judging by the looks on their faces, terrified.
"Take them inside," some of the core disciples instructed, and the disciples carried the elders away while the healer mages began treating them.
Thousands of disciples scrambled to ensure no threats came near the injured elders.
A few minutes after the elders returned, five white-bearded men appeared and, with a wave of their mage staffs, created a dome around the sect.
Even without personally seeing the sect master and the elders, they could sense the lingering evil intent surrounding them.
This told them they had offended someone they should never have provoked.
So, with their combined strength, they formed a 24-layer formation around the sect.
Even with Kent’s strength, breaking a Tier 24 formation would be extremely difficult.
In fact, he would not even try.
A Tier 24 formation at full strength could kill even God Kings, so he would not take that risk.
Unbeknownst to them, Kent had no intention of pursuing the Elders or causing trouble for the Sect master Kaidrenn
Before arriving on Planet Dormaa, he was already aware that it was one of the 13 planets under the protection of the Grand Arcane Mage Sect.
This meant destroying the sect was akin to putting countless innocent people in danger.
So he had no intention of destroying them.
But scaring them was something he did intend to do, and now it seemed he had done it.
Kent turned and looked at Lady Abba as he descended from the sky.
"Thank you for providing my brother with a stable job and trying to defend him when he found himself in danger.
As a reward, I will rebuild your restaurant and make it even better than before.
I will also ensure that nobody dares to trouble you again.
Lastly, I will help you expand your reach to other planets and galaxies and, perhaps one day, even the God Realm."
Kent snapped his fingers, and Gaia appeared beside him.
"This is Gaia.
She is good at building things.
She and her friends will work together to rebuild your restaurant.
For now, just relax and let them work."
As he said that, Akira, Dori, Li Hua, Yuna, and the rest of the Loli Gang arrived, their small bodies and cute appearances causing many people to wish they could play with them.
Kent had no idea how Gaia, Akira, and Dori had managed it, but it seemed that all the lolis who had joined their unofficial Loli legion had now become builders.
They no longer merely escorted the three Cosmic Lolis.
They now actively participated in construction and engineering projects.
Kent planned to find out what Gaia had done to them, but for now, he wanted them to focus on rebuilding the Everyday Inn Restaurant into one of the grandest restaurants on Planet Dormaa.
And just as he had done for Veth and Lady Wu, he would make sure that when it came to the restaurant business, Lady Abba would become uncontested.

chapters.title: Chapter 1708: The Ice Emperor’s Rebirth
paragraphs: Word of what had happened to the Grand Arcane Mage Sect spread throughout the Eastern Region, reaching as far as the wind could carry it.
Yet again, Kent’s name was associated with such a horrific event. It was as if, after his name appeared on the three Dao Tablets, his fame never seemed to die down.
Many who heard what had happened could only shake their heads and wonder if things could have gone any better.
Kent showed them all what he was capable of, and that alone proved to them that, just as he defeated the sect elders, he could just as easily defeat the entire sect and lay waste to everything.
This wake-up call prompted them all to become extra careful when dealing with him in the future.
Meanwhile, after ensuring Gaia and her team were properly introduced, Kent left with Sahir, travelling several light-years to a planet devoid of human life.
The planet was covered in ice, so freezing that, had it not been for Kent possessing Absolute Ice, they would have frozen to death the moment they came within 20 kilometres of it.

However, against all odds, he pushed forward, and after a few days traversing the frigid depths of the frozen planet, they arrived at a crystal clearing where, aside from giant crystal stones and walls, nothing else could be seen.
The structure looked like an ancient ritual ground. The arrangement seemed as though it had served a purpose a very long time ago.

Indeed, this place was sacred and once belonged to the Ice Emperor, but it was created by Kevin Sage. Back during the Ice Era, Kevin Sage set out one day to search for the core of a very powerful ice beast to use in alchemy.
During his search, he stumbled upon this Ice Planet.
Back then, a tribe of Ice Humans lived there.
When Kevin Sage arrived, he discovered that this tribe had been living on the frigid planet for as long as they could remember. They had no idea there were worlds and people beyond their own.

His arrival changed that and led him to Sahir, who was the tribal chief’s son at the time. Back then, the strongest member of the tribe was only a True Immortal. He was also a mage, with the strongest among them being a Master Mage.

Sahir was the useless son of the tribe chief. Even though he had managed to reach the Heavenly Ascension Stage, he was only able to cast a single spell circle, making him the least talented member of the tribe.
But when he met Kevin Sage, his story changed.
Kevin saw his true potential and, using the Ice Emperor Platform he had built for the tribe, he awakened his Bloodline and Physique, unleashing his talent upon the universe.
Today, he had brought him back to this very platform to unlock his memories and awaken his talent once again.
When they stepped onto the platform, it hummed, and spell circles began to manifest.
Sahir, who had always dreamed of being able to cast spells using spell circles, admired the sudden awakening, and for a moment, he smiled.

"Don’t worry. Very soon, you will become a Supreme Mage, one of the greatest in the entire universe. You once stood at the peak of the Mage World, commanding an army of over one hundred million ice mages.
In fact, you were one of the three Supreme Ice Mages back then, so relax. Soon, the universe will welcome you, just as I told you the last time."
Kent’s words caused Sahir to look at him and sigh.
"You keep speaking as if you know me from a life I never lived. Just who are you...?"
Kent smiled, walked closer to Sahir, and placed a hand on his shoulder.
"My name in this life is Kent Madson. However, a very long time ago, I was known as Kevin Sage. In that life, you were my sworn brother.

We fought many battles together and saved each other countless times. The day you died, you created the greatest spell the universe had ever seen. You, my friend, created the legendary Ice Emperor Descent, a spell formed from one hundred spell circles."
Sahir looked at Kent intently for a few seconds before bursting into resounding laughter.
"Please, if this is a dream, then it should end. I have been dreaming of this other Sahir for years, but it seems today’s dream is a bit out of hand."
Kent smirked and laughed as well.
"It is indeed out of hand, so why don’t you get your ass to the centre of the platform so we can start what we came here for?
Remember, you promised to beg your sister to marry me, so the faster we get this done, the faster I can become the husband of the Immortal Ice Maiden."
Kent laughed even louder and watched Sahir shake his head, smile, and then walk to the centre of the platform.

"Remember, when you wake up, you will become a completely different yet somehow the same person. Do well not to overexert your ice element unless you wish to kill me like you nearly did the last time."
Kent waved his hand, and a staff alongside a blue core appeared, radiating a rather unique aura.
When he received the quest and saw that the Grand Eternal Ice Staff and the Dominion of Life Core were the rewards, he had nearly cursed at the universe for showing favouritism.
The two items were both things that would restore Sahir to his peak state, and, based on his determination, he might even rise higher.

Kent wished he had received the same treatment as well. By now, he would have already become a Celestial. However, he understood that, unlike Sahir, who had lived only one life, he had lived thirteen different lives.
He couldn’t just use one of them to improve himself. He had to walk those paths again and slowly return to his peak.
So, with the items in hand, he channelled his energy into them, and a few seconds later, they transformed into beams of light and entered Sahir’s body.
He passed out immediately. Then a forest of ice cocooned around him, encasing him in its frigid embrace.
The moment he was encased, his rebirth ceremony began.
Kent stepped back and waited. At this point, all he could do was wait and watch what would happen.
Time soon passed, and before long, five days had gone by. Over those days, Kent could sense a powerful presence slowly growing inside the cocoon.
That was Sahir returning to his peak.
He continued to wait, knowing that the legendary Ice Emperor would soon return to the universe once more.
Three days later, the first crack appeared, and the universe rejoiced.

chapters.title: Chapter 1709: A Legend’s Return
paragraphs: "Sage, can you tell me more about the Law of Origin?" Sahir asked, seated at the edge of a cliff overlooking the vast world below. Seated beside him was the green-haired alchemist known for his good looks and intelligence.
Kevin Sage turned to Sahir and smiled. "Why do you want to know about the Law of Origin?" he asked.

"Because I want to be the first to create a 100-layered spell, and I think gaining some insight into it will help me greatly. I have already made some progress in the casting phase." Sahir replied, not hiding his ambition from Kevin Sage.

They were friends and, to some extent, brothers. Just as Kevin Sage had confided in him after he managed to comprehend some aspect of the Law of Origin, Sahir did the same, and as expected, Kevin Sage smiled.

"Why not? If you can comprehend the Law of Origin and become the first ice mage to touch the 100th Circle, wouldn’t that be a good thing?" Kevin Sage didn’t hesitate and transferred the knowledge he had acquired to his friend.
"I will not let you down, Sage," Sahir said, showing how grateful he was to Sage, who had just handed him something many would have gatekept for as long as they could.

A knight clad in white armor zoomed through thousands of ice demons, cutting them down as he went. Everywhere he passed, bodies fell. It was as if those closest to him had no choice but to die simply because he passed by.
The more he moved, the more ice demons came.

However, one could tell that warriors of different professions, shapes, sizes, and races were fighting to repel the millions, perhaps billions, of ice demons yet their efforts arent showing since there were just so many ice demons.
As the battle raged on, the man clad in white armor lifted his head and looked at the massive portal in the sky that kept spawning ice demons.

"I need to do something," the White Knight said to himself. Then he turned his gaze due east, where a blue-haired mage stood atop an ice dragon, moving about and casting one terrifying ice spell after another.
For a moment, the White Knight allowed himself to smile. Then his expression turned serious, and without any hesitation, he moved toward the ice mage.
A few minutes later, he stood a few meters away from him.
"Sahir, I think the only way we can win this is to close the gateway. However, it must be done from the inside."
"What are you trying to say, Sage?" Sahir asked, disregarding the fact that he had called Sage by his real name instead of his White Knight persona.

"I think you already know, Sahir. I need to enter the Ice Demon Realm and close the gate from there. I may never return, since closing it will take all of my power, but it must be done. So I guess this is goodbye."
Sahir paused mid-cast and locked eyes with Kevin Sage. "I guess this is goodbye then," he said with a smile, giving Sage a knowing look.
The two understood that sacrifices had to be made for the greater good. Knowing this, the moment Sage moved and entered the gateway, Sahir sighed and surveyed the battlefield.
A few minutes later, he appeared in a space occupied by over 20,000 Celestials and two Pseudo-Primordial Ice Demons. Knowing they were the greatest threat, Sahir sighed and closed his eyes.
"Ah, this is the end, I suppose." He grinned and commanded in an icy tone,
"ICE EMPEROR DESCENT!"
His staff moved, and for the first time ever, 100 spell circles appeared. Along with them, a majestic 20-kilometer-tall ice figure descended onto the battlefield.
"With ice as my conduit and this domain as my playground, I summon the Sword of External Damnation."
A giant sword materialized in the hands of the ice figure.
Then, with one sweeping slash, thousands of Celestials and even the two Pseudo-Primordials were killed, a feat that instantly changed the course of the battle.
However, with his soul and life force rapidly draining away, Sahir walked to a small stone and lay down.
In his final moments, he saw Kevin Sage smile back at him and ask, "So how does it feel to be one of the good guys?"
He smiled and weakly shook his head. Then he muttered under his breath, "Being one of the good guys is indeed terrible."
He closed his eyes, and everything turned dark.
Sahir snapped his eyes open, causing a terrifying chill to spread across the entire ice planet.
"This damn bastard."
Kent, who knew what was about to happen, had already made preparations. Cursing, he teleported and appeared 30 kilometers away from the planet.
"Damn it."
He had to retreat even farther because the moment he appeared outside the planet, another wave of ice qi surged from within, freezing the surrounding asteroids.

Kent pushed the Soul Map to its limit, moving as far as 1.2 million kilometers away before finally coming to a stop. Even from that distance, he could still sense the bone-chilling cold biting at his skin.
"Looks like he came back stronger than before," Kent said, a smile appearing on his face.
"Tower, is that Extreme-Rank Ice?" he asked.
[No, Master. Lord Sahir has stepped into the rank of Ultimate Ice. It seems the items used to restore his cultivation and other aspects were far more potent than we initially believed.]
"It seems so." Kent shook his head and sighed.
He was happy for Sahir, since this was something beneficial for both of them. With what was coming and what had already arrived, he would need every bit of help he could get.

Meanwhile, back on the Ice Planet, Sahir’s body hovered in the air, surrounded by fifteen crystallized blue shards. Each shard contained so much ice essence that if one were detonated, an entire planetary system would be frozen solid.
As they hovered around him, Sahir slowly absorbed their power, steadily increasing his strength.
His blue hair had grown longer, falling past his shoulders. He had also become more handsome, with his height increasing to 6’5", making him an inch taller than before.
He was clad in white robes decorated with red runes and adorned with various ornaments.
Beside him, the Grand Eternal Ice Staff hovered, releasing waves of ice essence.
Sahir had gone from an ordinary person to a Celestial. Aside from that, he had also become a Supreme Mage, meaning he could cast up to ninety-nine spell circles.
But if that wasn’t impressive enough, he had also awakened the Ice Emperor Body and the Genesis Ancient Ice Emperor Bloodline.
In his past life, the grade of his bloodline had been Supreme.

This time around, it was a Celestial-Grade Bloodline, and judging by the fact that his ice rank had also reached the Ultimate stage, he could already be counted among the ten greatest ice mages in the universe.
Slowly, Sahir opened his eyes and looked at his hands.
"I was supposed to be dead," he muttered.
He was about to scan his surroundings when memories from his current life flooded into his mind.
"So that’s was what happened, huh? Sage is here." He grinned and lifted his head, meeting the gaze of a very angry dragon.
"Interesting."
He took a single step and appeared before Kent, a wave of ice qi oozing from his body.
Perhaps if he had taken a moment to suppress his overflowing aura, he wouldn’t have done what happened when he arrived before Kent.

chapters.title: Chapter 1710: Crazy Bastard
paragraphs: Because Sahir was now a Celestial and also a Supreme Mage, his aura was on an entirely different level. Tapping into space and moving at such a speed was bound to generate a terrifying shockwave.
So the moment he moved and appeared before Kent, the resulting shockwave blasted the dragon backward, sending him flying through space and crashing through several asteroids.
On top of that, Kent’s body was instantly frozen, leaving him unable to stabilize himself.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Sahir, who immediately realized he had made a blunder, facepalmed and moved again, catching Kent before he could slam into a particularly massive asteroid.
COUGH! COUGH!
Kent coughed up blood, his body growing limp.
Kent was perhaps the strongest Immortal in the entire universe, but under the direct force of a Celestial, he was injured so severely that he seemed little different from a mortal.
"Sorry, buddy."
Sahir gently set Kent down on an asteroid and sat behind him, channeling his energy into Kent’s body.
Inside Kent’s soul sea, a very angry dragon roared at the cracked sky. It seems his robust soul was even injuried.
Several years ago, when he had performed the Ice Emperor Ritual and awakened Sahir’s bloodline, something similar had happened.
Back then, he had been frozen like an ice statue for two months.
Had it not been for possessing flame elements at the time, he would have frozen to death.
It was precisely why he had warned Sahir before initiating the ritual this time around.
In the end, however, things seemed still went out of the window and an even painful occurance happened today. Kent swore next time, he wouldn’t bring the bastard back...
Thanks to his monstrous healing abilities, Kent only needed about two days to recover from injuries that could have easily killed an Immortal Lord.
"You crazy bastard, I warned you not to try that again, but clearly, you didn’t listen," Kent said, glaring at Sahir, who held a smile on his face, very happy that his bro was fully healed.
Kent looked at that smile and smirked. He stood up and stretched his body a few times before turning back to Sahir.
"Don’t expect me to hug you, punk. I only hug women."
"Of course I know that," Sahir replied, already aware of this rule. Kevin Sage hated hugging people, especially men, so Sahir wasn’t looking for a hug. However, he would be happy if he got one.
Unfortunately for him, that chance went out the window when he sent Kent flying through asteroids. But he was a big boy, so he didn’t care much.
"So, reincarnation really does exist, huh?" he said, staring at Kent as if he’d seen a stranger, yet this stranger was his best friend and sworn brother.

"It does exist, and the fact that you and I are standing here now is all the proof you need. I reincarnated and was recovering my memories. I only recently recovered my memories of Kevin Sage, and that led me to you."
Sahir furrowed his brow and said in a questioning tone, "You make it sound like Kevin Sage was just one of your many lives."
Kent said nothing, which made Sahir widen his eyes. "Hold on a minute, are you saying what you speculated last time was true?"
Kent smiled and nodded. "Big time. It turns out I was badass in many lives before we met, but I just couldn’t recover my memories back then."
"Unbelievable." A shocked expression appeared on his face. "What kind of lives did you live before we met? And don’t tell me you were the incarnation of the Ruthless Bandit."
Kent grinned. "What if I were? In fact, what if I were the reincarnation of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, the legendary Lord Genesis, the Faceless Assassin, the Divine Beast Tamer, and many more?"
Sahir, who knew Kent well, realized he was subtly revealing the truth.
His eyes widened as shock crossed his face.
In the past, Kevin Sage always speculated that the reason he was better than everyone—and yes, Kevin was that arrogant—was because he believed he had lived previous lives that were influencing him.
Now, it appeared he wasn’t joking at all.
"That explains why you were able to help me tame Little White," Sahir said, a small smile playing on his lips. During the Ice Era, he had an ice dragon mount.
Thanks to this mount, he was able to traverse the starry skies and go places without having to move even a finger.

Of course, what he didn’t tell many people was that the first time he met Little White, he nearly died. That dragon came close to killing him. However, when he asked Kevin for aid, things went rather smoothly.
"Turns out you were the legendary Divine Beast Tamer. No wonder Little White liked you more than even me, his master."
Kent laughed, wondering whether or not that beautiful dragon was still alive.
"How do you feel now?" Kent asked after examining Sahir’s condition with his Omniscient Jade Eyes for a few seconds.
"I think I am stronger than before. Now, I can cast 100 spell circles without having to burn too much of my soul essence. It shows I am getting closer to a breakthrough."
"Good to hear that." Kent walked to the edge of the asteroid and stared down into the darkness below. Then he sighed and turned back to Sahir.
"So, what do you plan on doing next? You have just reincarnated, but you must know that while you were gone, a lot happened, some of it relating to you. What do you plan on doing next?"

Sahir thought for a moment and answered, "I will first return to the Celestial Realm and find out more about what happened to my family after I was gone. I will also use the time to catch up on events from over the years.
I may have been at the top back then, but years have passed, so I wouldn’t be surprised if I am no longer at the peak.
Once that is handled, I will venture into the Ice Abyss and search for Little White’s whereabouts while also training for when you will need my help."
Kent nodded and pressed his finger against Sahir’s forehead. "I have given you permission to access a secret world.
If you need help, come get me. Of course, if it weren’t for the fact that I have things to do, I would have escorted you for a while longer.
However, just like you, there are many others who once walked through thick and thin with me, so I must find their whereabouts and restore their strengths."
"I understand, Sage. I will be sure to stay in touch."
"That is great to hear, Sahir. Say hi to Azirah for me when you reunite with her."
"I will," Sahir said with a smile before extending his hand and summoning his staff. With a simple gesture, the void exploded open.
However, unlike the usual dark maw that opened whenever one wanted to travel through the void, this one manifested as a decorated gateway, its interior filled with icy mist.
"You must become stronger soon, Sage. The last time, we were forced to sacrifice our lives. This time around, I intend to kill every last one of them. So become stronger soon..."
"I will. However, you should also be careful out there. You may be a Supreme Mage, but there are others like you out there, and they would hate to see a rival."
Sahir smirked and stepped into the void gate. "They can try."
The void closed, and he was gone.
After he left, Kent smirked and sat down, taking a pill from his ring and swallowing it.
