chapters.title: Chapter 1711: Harem Missions (1)
paragraphs: [Moonfang City - Planet Sonoria]

Moonfang City is one of the four cities on Planet Sonoria. It is inhabited by a race of human variants known as Moon Humans. They share a direct connection with the moon, allowing them to harness its power.
Naturally, they are as good-looking as many other races fortunate enough to be favored by the Moon Goddess.
However, looks and character are two completely different things. This is especially true for the ruler of Moonfang City, Lord Vexor.
He is one of the biggest scumbags on Planet Sonoria.
His empire was built upon the suffering of the poor.

Just as many wealthy men go out of their way to ensure the poor remain poor, Lord Vexor had invested both time and money to make sure the people of Moonfang City understood the need to show appreciation.
There are about 300 million people in Moonfang City, and almost everyone fears him.
His slave trade business is the largest on Planet Sonoria. On top of that, he is affiliated with the Soul Temple, which sends aid whenever he finds himself in trouble.
In return for their assistance, he provides people whose souls and resentment are extracted by the Soul Temple to strengthen themselves.
This had been going on for years, and people are aware of it, but with thousands of immortals and dozens of demigods under his command, nobody dared stand against him.
...until today.
Inside a teleportation station, a ship landed, and three beautiful women stepped out.
Unity, alongside Dia and Lilian, walked out, instantly attracting attention. Unity’s dark hair flowed down her back, moving through the air as though every strand possessed a life of its own.

She was clad in an elegant outfit consisting of trousers and a gown that covered her shoulders. Of course, she merely wanted to appear regal while maintaining a fierce and imposing presence, so she concealed part of her armor beneath the gown, or perhaps it was more accurate to call it a cloak.
Now that she had become an Immortal King, her already stunning appearance had become even more breathtaking.

Already blessed with the Celestial-grade Amoris Astraea Bloodline, born from her nature as Artemis, the Goddess of the Hunt, and Amorin, the Goddess of Love, her beauty continued to grow as she gradually recovered the nature and power of her past lives.

Beside her, Lilian had chosen to go redheaded today by switching to her Flame Dragon side. Her crimson dragon horns, paired with her fiery red hair and scarlet eyes, made her look dangerous and, surprisingly, even more attractive.
As the saying goes, men are drawn to dangerous women. Lilian had become the very embodiment of that appeal.

Just like Unity, she had also reached the Peak Immortal King Stage. And with both her Flame and Ice at the Absolute Rank under her command, who was to say that the legendary Dual Dragon Mage wouldn’t reduce Moonfang City to ashes before noon?
Then came Dia, one of the most mysteriously terrifying women in Kent’s harem. She was Kent’s heart demon in 13 lives, yet she was also her own person.

After making peace with herself, she had begun to grow rapidly. As a result, even though she had yet to awaken her bloodline, she had become one of the few women in the harem to reach the Immortal Monarch Stage.
She stood 6’2" tall, making her two inches taller than her sister, Unity. Even with her bloodline still dormant and no True Name having been bestowed upon her, her beauty was evident to all.
She had silver hair, unlike her sister, but aside from that, her athletic physique and the scythe she wielded made her appear more like a warrior than a beauty to be admired.

As they walked away, many men turned to look at them, some even feeling the urge to approach. However, for reasons they couldn’t understand, whenever such thoughts surfaced, they were forced to erase them from their minds.
If only they knew their pitiful lives had been spared because they chose not to approach.
But it was only a matter of time before those foolish enough to ignore the obvious would decide to court death.

A couple of hours later, Unity and her sisters found themselves in a private room, seated around a table and drinking tea. The first thing they had done after arriving in Moonfang City was gather information about their target, Lord Vexor.
After all, they had come for his head. They intended to make sure he would die soon so they could claim their rewards and move on to the next mission.
Just like every team harem, they were competing against one another.

Unity’s team wasn’t the only one out there. With three women in each team, more than a dozen teams were already operating across different regions, handling the missions Kent had received from the Tower and the Quest Pool.
"What are your findings?" Unity asked, taking a sip of her tea.

"Just as the mission stated, he is heavily protected," Dia said, revealing her findings to her sisters. "During my scouting, I discovered that he has over ten thousand immortal guards, with close to one thousand of them being Immortal Lords.
"Aside from them, he also has about twenty-four demigod guards. However, most of them are stationed outside his mansion, so if we can slip through their defenses, killing him won’t be a problem."
"What Dia discovered is the same as what I found," Lilian revealed. "He is indeed very well protected. However, if we can get close to him, killing him will be as simple as a single dragon breath."
Lilian smiled, already fantasizing about how she would barbecue the poor bastard.
Unity merely shook her head, fully aware that after Kent had awakened Lilian’s True Name, her personality had changed as well.
Because she possessed both ice and fire, her ice form was calm, quiet, and composed. However, when she switched to her flame form, all hell would break loose.
"Unfortunately for you, there will be no breath attacks on the target today," Unity said.
Lilian pouted. However, knowing how intelligent Unity was, she said nothing and instead listened to the plan.
"So here’s the plan..."
A while later, they left the restaurant and headed toward the location where the mission would begin.
Meanwhile, inside a luxurious mansion, a Moon Human man with short dark hair and a muscular build sat upon a throne-like chair, surrounded by half-naked women massaging his body.
A few meters away, a demigod guard stood at attention, delivering his report.
"My Lord, I have discovered the location where the three new arrivals are staying. General Tengis has already made arrangements to send men over this evening.
"By tomorrow, all three of them will be in your bed, my lord."
The ruler of all Moonfang City, Lord Vexor, smiled.
"Good job, Torghud. You can take the day off and return tomorrow evening."

Torghud nodded and turned to leave, his expression brightening slightly. However, just as he opened the main door and was about to step outside, a loud dragon roar echoed across the sky, turning it crimson.
Then, from the clouds, a massive dragon emerged, its wings beating against the air as the ground began to tremble.
DONG! DONG! DONG!
Alarm bells rang throughout the Mansion, and powerful immortals and demigods scrambled to their feet, unsheathing their weapons.

chapters.title: Chapter 1712: Harem Missions (2)
paragraphs: The plan Unity cooked up was rather simple; Lilian would do what she does best: rain fire upon the mansion, creating a grim atmosphere and chaos beyond measure while also killing as many immortals as she could.
So the moment Lilian made her presence known, she nosedived, her wings spread wide and flames burning around her.
"ROARRRRRR"
Her roar shook the entire mansion and even the city.
"BOOOOM"
Then, in a devastating collision, the ground shattered, large craters formed, and some mansions came crashing down.
In just one deadly impact, Lilian destroyed almost half of the mansions, and over a thousand immortal guards died, with many others sustaining injuries.
However, that wasn’t all. The moment she landed, thousands of fireballs started to rain down, filling the entire mansion with chaos—the very same chaos Unity had asked for.
While the fireballs were doing their thing, Lilian took to the air again and clashed with ten demigods.
Perhaps that was what they wanted, so they ignored the destruction around them and went after her. She, of course, led them into the clouds, where they would be out of sight.

But with them gone and over 70% of the immortals dead from the collision and fireballs, when Unity made her appearance known, she was met with only a few immortals and about ten demigods, leaving only four demigods unaccounted for.
Unity walked through the gate like she owned the place, her hair tied into a ponytail, her body covered in leather armor, her bow firmly in her hand.
"I would like to think you guys are innocent, and as such, I would spare you. However, if you attack me, I will be forced to kill you all," she warned, but her words fell on deaf ears.

A demigod zipped through space, his spear pointed at Unity’s neck. However, just before he could get within two meters of her, a dark-clothed figure appeared behind him, her scythe moving like a blur.
The demigod saw the attack coming, but before he could make any attempt to evade, Dia’s scythe sliced through his neck, ending his life.
"Well, my sister would kill you all." Unity smiled and winked at Dia, who smirked, having forgotten just how annoying Unity—or Artemis—could be sometimes.
"Unity, go now and make sure that bastard dies with three arrows through his head," Dia said, and Unity nodded.
"Be careful, Big Sister. These bastards aren’t that weak, but they’re not that strong either."
Unity took a step forward, and she vanished from sight.
The demigods who saw what Dia did became alarmed, some trying to run toward the mansion where they believed Unity had gone. However, before they could move, Dia activated her trump card.
"Heart Demon Realm."
The space around them turned cold, and then, as though they had been possessed, they all screamed loudly, and hell broke loose.
Dia moved like the wind, her scythe meeting the staff of a demigod mage. Soon, they became blurs, exchanging thousands of blows in mere seconds.
Her Heart Demon Realm allowed her to plant heart demons within the hearts of opponents whose soul strength was lower than hers.
Her soul was already comparable to that of demigods, so she was able to implant heart demons into eight of the nine remaining demigods.
Now, all of them were fighting their heart demons. However, given how fiercely they were attacking one another, it was clear that their heart demons had taken each other’s forms.
The only one who wasn’t affected was the mage, who possessed a rather robust soul. But even so, with just one of her, it was only a matter of time before Dia cut her down.
Meanwhile, Unity stopped 2 km away from where Dia was fighting the demigods and bit her lip. Her sister had been the most loving and caring person she knew during the Primordial Era.
However, after spending thirteen lifetimes as a heart demon, she had become so twisted at heart that her core nature had completely changed.

Seeing the resentment coming from the direction of her battle, Unity realized that the sister she knew had long since died, and the one fighting now was the unknown person Ainna had said had lost both her soul and destiny.
She was her sister, but her true nature had long been stolen, leaving her cursed. While she could harness some of the curse, she always feels agonizing pains due to it.

Unity had wanted her not to come on the mission, but when all her sisters left, she stubbornly insisted that she would come too. Now, while she was dominating the battlefield, she was also in great pain.
"Don’t worry, Big Sister, we will get your fate and destiny back one day."
With a sigh and an angry expression, Unity released an arrow through the main gate, revealing a large hall where five demigods stood, ready to kill whoever walked through the gate.
When Unity stepped through, Lord Vexor ordered his four demigod guards to attack. However, Unity didn’t stand idle either.
An arrow flew from her bow and arrived before Lord Vexor, but she was also attacked from the side. However, instead of defending, Unity allowed the sword to strike her body.
"CLANG"
The demigod who attacked her widened his eyes.
"Indestructible Body, bitch."

Unity’s foot moved and landed on the demigod’s face. Then her bow glowed, and three arrows appeared on the string. With a deadly pull, she unleashed three terrifying arrows, each of which landed on its mark.
The mansion shook, and then it exploded, revealing Unity locked in battle with the five demigods, including her target, Lord Vexor.
Once the mansion was reduced to rubble and the space widened, Unity smiled and teleported away. The next second, the sky turned golden, and arrows started to rain down.
"Activate the defensive formations!" Lord Vexor, who chose to stay and fight, believing that victory was within his reach, turned pale, his body trembling as he issued the order.
"Formations or not, you are dying today, you evil bastard." Unity intensified her assault.

She knew that before she could get to her target, she first had to deal with the four demigods, who weren’t any weaker than some of the beasts she had fought and killed while inside the Planet Killer Dungeon.
However, humans were crafty, so she was careful as well. This was all so that when she got to her target, she would find it easier.
Inside the clouds, Lilian too was locked in battle with the ten demigods, and the same was true for Dia, who was getting closer to killing her second demigod.
Meanwhile, 7 km away from the mansion, a formation gate opened, and three demigods clad in bone-like armor, each wielding a bone-like weapon, stepped out.
The aura of blood clung to them, showing that they are blood cultivators like many others. However, their appearance alone was enough to tell that they weren’t friendly.

"I wonder who is bold enough to attack a City Lord who is under the soul temple protection," one of them said, a smirk forming on his pale face. He had four sets of eyes, making him look both dangerous and evil.
"I don’t care who dares do that. What I know is that I will be getting fresh blood to drink."
They laughed and moved toward the mansion, where Lord Vexor was being attacked by Unity and her two sisters, Dia and Lilian.
However, they had moved only 800 meters before coming to a stop. One hundred meters away from them, a purple-haired dragon man sat with his eyes closed, a smile playing on his face.
"Gentlemen, how about we watch instead?" Kent said.
Then, as though the heavens themselves were falling, all three agents of the Soul Temple dropped to their knees, their bones breaking instantly.

sentences.text: The plan Unity cooked up was rather simple; Lilian would do what she does best: rain fire upon the mansion, creating a grim atmosphere and chaos beyond measure while also killing as many immortals as she could.
So the moment Lilian made her presence known, she nosedived, her wings spread wide and flames burning around her.
"ROARRRRRR"
Her roar shook the entire mansion and even the city.
"BOOOOM"
Then, in a devastating collision, the ground shattered, large craters formed, and some mansions came crashing down.
In just one deadly impact, Lilian destroyed almost half of the mansions, and over a thousand immortal guards died, with many others sustaining injuries.
However, that wasn’t all.
The moment she landed, thousands of fireballs started to rain down, filling the entire mansion with chaos—the very same chaos Unity had asked for.
While the fireballs were doing their thing, Lilian took to the air again and clashed with ten demigods.
Perhaps that was what they wanted, so they ignored the destruction around them and went after her.
She, of course, led them into the clouds, where they would be out of sight.

But with them gone and over 70% of the immortals dead from the collision and fireballs, when Unity made her appearance known, she was met with only a few immortals and about ten demigods, leaving only four demigods unaccounted for.
Unity walked through the gate like she owned the place, her hair tied into a ponytail, her body covered in leather armor, her bow firmly in her hand.
"I would like to think you guys are innocent, and as such, I would spare you.
However, if you attack me, I will be forced to kill you all," she warned, but her words fell on deaf ears.
A demigod zipped through space, his spear pointed at Unity’s neck.
However, just before he could get within two meters of her, a dark-clothed figure appeared behind him, her scythe moving like a blur.
The demigod saw the attack coming, but before he could make any attempt to evade, Dia’s scythe sliced through his neck, ending his life.
"Well, my sister would kill you all." Unity smiled and winked at Dia, who smirked, having forgotten just how annoying Unity—or Artemis—could be sometimes.
"Unity, go now and make sure that bastard dies with three arrows through his head," Dia said, and Unity nodded.
"Be careful, Big Sister.
These bastards aren’t that weak, but they’re not that strong either."
Unity took a step forward, and she vanished from sight.
The demigods who saw what Dia did became alarmed, some trying to run toward the mansion where they believed Unity had gone.
However, before they could move, Dia activated her trump card.
"Heart Demon Realm."
The space around them turned cold, and then, as though they had been possessed, they all screamed loudly, and hell broke loose.
Dia moved like the wind, her scythe meeting the staff of a demigod mage.
Soon, they became blurs, exchanging thousands of blows in mere seconds.
Her Heart Demon Realm allowed her to plant heart demons within the hearts of opponents whose soul strength was lower than hers.
Her soul was already comparable to that of demigods, so she was able to implant heart demons into eight of the nine remaining demigods.
Now, all of them were fighting their heart demons.
However, given how fiercely they were attacking one another, it was clear that their heart demons had taken each other’s forms.
The only one who wasn’t affected was the mage, who possessed a rather robust soul.
But even so, with just one of her, it was only a matter of time before Dia cut her down.
Meanwhile, Unity stopped 2 km away from where Dia was fighting the demigods and bit her lip.
Her sister had been the most loving and caring person she knew during the Primordial Era.
However, after spending thirteen lifetimes as a heart demon, she had become so twisted at heart that her core nature had completely changed.

Seeing the resentment coming from the direction of her battle, Unity realized that the sister she knew had long since died, and the one fighting now was the unknown person Ainna had said had lost both her soul and destiny.
She was her sister, but her true nature had long been stolen, leaving her cursed.
While she could harness some of the curse, she always feels agonizing pains due to it.
Unity had wanted her not to come on the mission, but when all her sisters left, she stubbornly insisted that she would come too.
Now, while she was dominating the battlefield, she was also in great pain.
"Don’t worry, Big Sister, we will get your fate and destiny back one day."
With a sigh and an angry expression, Unity released an arrow through the main gate, revealing a large hall where five demigods stood, ready to kill whoever walked through the gate.
When Unity stepped through, Lord Vexor ordered his four demigod guards to attack.
However, Unity didn’t stand idle either.
An arrow flew from her bow and arrived before Lord Vexor, but she was also attacked from the side.
However, instead of defending, Unity allowed the sword to strike her body.
"CLANG"
The demigod who attacked her widened his eyes.
"Indestructible Body, bitch."
Unity’s foot moved and landed on the demigod’s face.
Then her bow glowed, and three arrows appeared on the string.
With a deadly pull, she unleashed three terrifying arrows, each of which landed on its mark.
The mansion shook, and then it exploded, revealing Unity locked in battle with the five demigods, including her target, Lord Vexor.
Once the mansion was reduced to rubble and the space widened, Unity smiled and teleported away.
The next second, the sky turned golden, and arrows started to rain down.
"Activate the defensive formations!" Lord Vexor, who chose to stay and fight, believing that victory was within his reach, turned pale, his body trembling as he issued the order.
"Formations or not, you are dying today, you evil bastard." Unity intensified her assault.

She knew that before she could get to her target, she first had to deal with the four demigods, who weren’t any weaker than some of the beasts she had fought and killed while inside the Planet Killer Dungeon.
However, humans were crafty, so she was careful as well.
This was all so that when she got to her target, she would find it easier.
Inside the clouds, Lilian too was locked in battle with the ten demigods, and the same was true for Dia, who was getting closer to killing her second demigod.
Meanwhile, 7 km away from the mansion, a formation gate opened, and three demigods clad in bone-like armor, each wielding a bone-like weapon, stepped out.
The aura of blood clung to them, showing that they are blood cultivators like many others.
However, their appearance alone was enough to tell that they weren’t friendly.

However, they had moved only 800 meters before coming to a stop.
One hundred meters away from them, a purple-haired dragon man sat with his eyes closed, a smile playing on his face.
"Gentlemen, how about we watch instead?" Kent said.
Then, as though the heavens themselves were falling, all three agents of the Soul Temple dropped to their knees, their bones breaking instantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1713: Harem Missions (3)
paragraphs: "CLANG!"
A spear met Unity’s bow, forcing both of them to take several steps back.

Then she moved, and the sole of her boot slammed into the demigod’s face, pushing him back. However, as if he wasn’t humiliated enough, her other hand moved, and a slap landed across his face, sending his head snapping backward.
Unity wasted no time and unleashed an arrow at point-blank range, sending the demigod flying backward as an arrow burst through his chest.
With the demigod incapacitated, she locked her gaze onto Lord Vexor.
She had already severely injured three of the demigods, and now the fourth had been added to the list. So the moment she fixed her gaze on Lord Vexor, the poor bastard knew he was done for.
"Everlasting Beam."
Unity wasted no time and unleashed an arrow that streaked across the sky, locking onto Lord Vexor, who was trying to make a run for it.
Unfortunately for him, Unity never missed her targets.
Lord Vexor’s face turned pale as death finally came for him. He had expected today to go in his favor. He even fantasized about having these three beauties in his bed by tomorrow morning.
However, from the moment he was attacked, everything became clear to him—death had finally arrived at his doorstep.
The moment the golden arrow locked onto him, he felt as though fate itself had marked him for execution.
"Stop it! Stop that arrow!"
He roared and threw out dozens of defensive and life-saving artifacts.
Shields, barriers, talismans, and formations appeared one after another, creating layer upon layer of protection around him, shielding him from death—or at least, that was what he thought.
Unfortunately for him, the golden arrow didn’t slow down.
It pierced through the first barrier.
Then the second.
Then the third.
Every defensive measure exploded upon contact.
"BOOM!" "BOOM!" "BOOM!"
Lord Vexor turned pale, his body shuddering as though cold water had been poured on his pride. By the time the last life-saving treasure was destroyed, one of his legs had already given out.
The arrow arrived before him and was only inches away when a beam descended from the sky, blasting it away. However, the impact also sent Lord Vexor flying backward.
In his place stood a man who looked to be around fifty-five years old, clad in robes and holding a magic brush. At first glance, his posture, with his hands behind his back, resembled that of a monk.
However, his pink beard defeated the entire purpose of such an impression, and the fact that he wasn’t bald further proved he was no monk.
"Little one, how about we talk this over and see if we can arrive at a mutual agreement?" he said, a smile appearing on his face.
One kilometer away, Lord Vexor slowly rose to his feet, a smile forming on his otherwise pale and injured face.
Unity, ever perceptive, saw the smile and instantly knew this man wasn’t here for any noble cause. However, she decided to play along.
"Who are you, and what makes you think there can ever be a justification for colluding with the Soul Temple and engaging in slave trading?"
The expression on the man’s face didn’t change. However, the aura around him began to grow.
"My name is Lord Riven, and I am the guardian of this city. As for your accusations, I don’t know where you heard them from, but under my guardianship, none of what you said is true.
I would have found out if Vexor dared to collude with the Soul Temple," he said with a smile before adding,
"As for the slave trade, I can assure you that only criminals were sold. No innocent people were targeted."
"Is that so?" Unity asked, her expression surprisingly calm.
Seeing this, Riven thought she believed him, so he nodded and let out a fake laugh.
The next words Unity spoke, however, wiped the smile off his face and forced him to take a serious demeanor.
"I guess you have eyes, but you cannot see. Since that is the case, allow me to blind you for good."
RUMBLE!
Unity’s body erupted with golden lightning, arcs of crackling energy dancing across her skin.
With a single deadly step, she appeared right in front of Riven.
Before the so-called city guardian could create any distance between them, two beams shot from Unity’s eyes and landed directly on his own.
"AAARRGGGGHHHH!"
His screams filled the sky, traveling for miles, sending chills down the spines of everyone who heard him.
"There you go. Now I won’t blame you if you can’t see the rot right before your eyes."
Unity followed up with a slap across Riven’s face, sending him hurtling through the air.
"Now, give me your life, bastard."
Her hand moved, and ten arrows streaked through the sky, each finding its mark on Lord Vexor. The force pushed him backward, raising a massive cloud of dust.
When the dust finally settled, a scene that sent chills down the spines of the demigods, barely clinging to their lives, was revealed.
Lord Vexor had been skewered to the wall of his mansion.
Lightning arrows pinned his hands, legs, and neck firmly against the wall.
He didn’t even have time to cry out for help before he died.
Unity sighed and turned away from him, directing her gaze toward Dia.
Seeing that her sister had everything under control, she looked up and discovered that Lilian was also doing better than she had expected.
After making sure her two sisters were fine, she turned back toward the four demigods.

"Leaving you four alive would be like freeing four maniacs from their master and setting them loose upon the world. You are a danger to society, so I cannot let you go. However, I also don’t feel like killing you, so what should I do with the four of you?"
The four immediately dropped to their knees.
"Please, fairy, spare us, and we promise never to harm the innocent again."
"Yes, please! We will never dare hurt anyone ever again."
"Please spare us, and we promise to fight for the innocent from now on."
"Hmmm..."
Unity hummed as her thoughts shifted.
By nature, she wasn’t a killer.
She had lived for forty-three years in her incarnation as Artemis, and her entire incarnation as the Goddess of Love had been spent helping people find their happy endings.
While Neomi, the Mother of Killers, would have slaughtered these four demigods without a second thought, Unity was genuinely considering letting them go.
None of her sisters hated her for being soft.
In fact, they admired that part of her because she was the only one among them who could still see a trace of good even in the worst kind of people.
Perhaps that was why Vexthra, the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment, liked her more than the rest of their sisters.
"You are a good person, Unity. Never lose that."
A familiar voice suddenly echoed inside her mind.
Turning slightly, she saw Kent walking toward her.
Three warriors clad in bone-like armor hovered behind him, their bodies completely immobilized.
"Kent!" Unity called out, her face lit up with joy.
The moment he got close enough, she leaped into his arms, completely forgetting that she was in the process of deciding the fate of four demigods only moments ago.
Kent looked at her bright smile and couldn’t help but shake his head inwardly.
Perhaps if Artemis hadn’t died so young, she would have come to understand the true hardships of the vast universe and developed a far stronger mentality.
Then again, none of that really mattered.
As long as she was happy, everything was fine.
The four demigods felt their bodies stiffen when they met Kent’s gaze.
In that instant, they knew their deaths were inevitable.
They could sense it clearly.
Kent was the complete opposite of Unity.

chapters.title: Chapter 1714: Arriving in The Dead World
paragraphs: It took Lilian and Dia 30 more minutes to handle their side of the battle.
As expected, Dia killed all 10 demigods. Well, she personally killed only six of them, since the other four died fighting their own teammates, whom they thought were their heart demons.
But the most important thing was, unlike her sister Unity, she didn’t blink when killing her opponents.

Lilian also killed her opponents, but she sustained some injuries. Even so, considering how inconsequential those injuries were, it could be said that with just her Peak-Rank Immortal King cultivation base, she was able to kill demigods.
That was impressive in many ways.
Kent could do it because he was Kent. But for someone like Lilian, who wasn’t even close to the Immortal Lord stage, doing the same thing was commendable.

After they were done, Kent gathered all the dead bodies and stored them inside the Legion Tower. Once Veera returned, she would use them to improve her undead warriors. As for the demigods Unity fought and the three agents from the Soul Temple, he would reserve them for Sylara.
She would use their blood essence to draw more Blood Tattoos.
"You all have done well," Kent said, seated inside a restaurant with Lilian, Unity, and Dia.
After Sahir left for the Celestial Realm, Kent stayed outside the Ice Planet for two weeks, healing the rest of his injuries.
Later, the Tower informed him that Unity’s team had arrived at their mission location, so he teleported there to keep a close eye on them.
He had already made them aware that he would be nearby and that if they found themselves in trouble, he would step in to help.
He stuck to that promise, and the moment he sensed danger, he stepped in.
"Thank you for saving us, too. If you hadn’t stopped those three, perhaps we would have found ourselves in trouble," Unity replied, very happy that they had completed their mission.
Kent nodded at her words.
"So, what do you have planned next?" he asked, now that they were done with their first mission.
He already had plans with Veth.
He planned to reunite with Lady Wu before going elsewhere, and since she had an upcoming auction, he wanted to attend and, if possible, buy anything that caught his eye.
It would also be a nice reunion since they met in an auction house.
"We’ll be going on another mission since there are still more of them left. But first, we’ll return to the Tower to absorb the treasures we received as rewards for completing the mission."
"Sounds like a great plan. However, before returning to the Tower, we should eat something first."
They ordered their food and started eating.
However, while they were busy eating, Uncle Drew and his team of Night Riders arrived at the borders of the Dead World riding their Hellhorses.
Just like there are outposts for the most dangerous realms, where one must meet special conditions before being allowed entry, the Dead World also had such outposts.
It was a city built 100 kilometers away from the Dead Planet. It stood majestic in space, and it mostly housed cultivators who cultivated Death Qi.
While possessing Hellflame was considered a boon when entering such a dangerous world, those who cultivated only Death Qi could also enter.
However, when Uncle Drew, Nara, Lene, Vargus, Eryndor, and Saden arrived riding their Hellhorses, everyone felt the shift in the air.
The potency of the death aura and Hellflame Qi oozing from their bodies made everyone tremble.
Vargus and Lene were Demigods, so naturally, they made the group of six Night Riders look even more intimidating.
However, Uncle Drew and Nara were Immortal Kings with auras that surpassed most Demigods, while Eryndor and Saden were True Immortals. If anything, this was a solid team.
However, the moment the fear they felt subsided, the foolish among them stepped forward and blocked Uncle Drew and his team’s path.

"This is the territory of the Zahki Clan. Those who wish to pass must pay one million high-grade spirit stones," an Immortal Lord wearing the look of an arrogant general demanded, hoping to make a fortune from these new faces.
He had never seen them before, meaning they came from far, and most importantly, this was their first time here.
However, before he could say anything else, Uncle Drew threw a pouch containing the required amount of spirit stones to him. He was visibly shaken when he caught it.
However, after the shock left his face, he grinned and opened his palm, beckoning for more.
"This only covers the passage of one person. If all six of you wish to enter, you must pay for all six."
His shoulders shook slightly, revealing that he was inwardly suppressing laughter.

Of course, everyone around knew that the sole reason this man had the backbone to block six people reeking of death qi was simplly because the Zahki clan was one of the most powerful in the Western Region.
They specialized in cultivating Death Qi, so naturally, the Dead World fell under their jurisdiction.
Nobody dared mess with them, and Uncle Drew’s team, who had done their research before coming, knew this.
Nara waved her hand, and five more pouches flew toward the man, who once again wore a shocked expression as he caught every last one.
Uncle Drew gestured for them to move toward the portal that led directly to the Dead World. After all, they had paid for passage.
However, just as they moved, the man cleared his throat and blocked their path once more.

"Hold it right there. You still haven’t paid for your mounts. In case you are unaware, it costs extra to transport a mount to the Dead World." He gestured with a smirk on his face. "That will be another six million high-grade spirit stones."
Uncle Drew’s Hellhorse neighed, clearly angered by what the bastard was trying to pull.
Uncle Drew narrowed his eyes at the man, who seemed to think he could do as he pleased. Unfortunately for him, he had picked the wrong team to mess with.
"Nightblade, kill him."
"With pleasure."
Nara’s hand moved to her sword, and before anyone could register what had happened, it was already over. The man’s head rolled to the ground, and that was the end of him.
"In your next life, be careful around dead people," Uncle Drew said coldly.
"Half-dead," Nara corrected with a smirk.
"My bad," Uncle Drew laughed.
While they were akin to dead people, all Night Riders existed between life and death, standing on the boundary that separated the living from the dead.
As such, they were not truly undead.
Turning slightly, Uncle Drew’s gaze landed on the people who were still frozen in shock.
"When they come asking who did this, tell them Kael Duskbane, Captain of the Night Riders, did it."
His Hellhorse moved forward and kicked away the head of the bastard who had tried to extort them.
Soon, they vanished into the portal, leaving everyone pale.
They had, of course, heard of the legendary Night Riders before. So if what Uncle Drew said was true, perhaps there would soon be quite a show to watch here.
Meanwhile, after entering the portal, the Night Riders appeared in a world shrouded in red mist, with the aura of death permeating every corner.
Uncle Drew surveyed their surroundings to ensure there were no threats nearby. Once he was certain they were all safe, he began formulating a comprehensive plan.
"Our mission is to traverse this dangerous terrain to the Black Star Domain and kill the Black Fire Demon Dragon. As for what we’re really here for, the Young Master said we’ll know when we see it."

He had already made them aware that he would be nearby and that if they found themselves in trouble, he would step in to help.
He stuck to that promise, and the moment he sensed danger, he stepped in.
"Thank you for saving us, too.
If you hadn’t stopped those three, perhaps we would have found ourselves in trouble," Unity replied, very happy that they had completed their mission.
Kent nodded at her words.
"So, what do you have planned next?" he asked, now that they were done with their first mission.
He already had plans with Veth.
He planned to reunite with Lady Wu before going elsewhere, and since she had an upcoming auction, he wanted to attend and, if possible, buy anything that caught his eye.
It would also be a nice reunion since they met in an auction house.
"We’ll be going on another mission since there are still more of them left.
But first, we’ll return to the Tower to absorb the treasures we received as rewards for completing the mission."
"Sounds like a great plan.
However, before returning to the Tower, we should eat something first."
They ordered their food and started eating.
However, while they were busy eating, Uncle Drew and his team of Night Riders arrived at the borders of the Dead World riding their Hellhorses.
Just like there are outposts for the most dangerous realms, where one must meet special conditions before being allowed entry, the Dead World also had such outposts.
It was a city built 100 kilometers away from the Dead Planet.
It stood majestic in space, and it mostly housed cultivators who cultivated Death Qi.
While possessing Hellflame was considered a boon when entering such a dangerous world, those who cultivated only Death Qi could also enter.
However, when Uncle Drew, Nara, Lene, Vargus, Eryndor, and Saden arrived riding their Hellhorses, everyone felt the shift in the air.
The potency of the death aura and Hellflame Qi oozing from their bodies made everyone tremble.
Vargus and Lene were Demigods, so naturally, they made the group of six Night Riders look even more intimidating.
However, Uncle Drew and Nara were Immortal Kings with auras that surpassed most Demigods, while Eryndor and Saden were True Immortals.
If anything, this was a solid team.
However, the moment the fear they felt subsided, the foolish among them stepped forward and blocked Uncle Drew and his team’s path.
"This is the territory of the Zahki Clan.
Those who wish to pass must pay one million high-grade spirit stones," an Immortal Lord wearing the look of an arrogant general demanded, hoping to make a fortune from these new faces.
He had never seen them before, meaning they came from far, and most importantly, this was their first time here.
However, before he could say anything else, Uncle Drew threw a pouch containing the required amount of spirit stones to him.
He was visibly shaken when he caught it.
However, after the shock left his face, he grinned and opened his palm, beckoning for more.
"This only covers the passage of one person.
If all six of you wish to enter, you must pay for all six."
His shoulders shook slightly, revealing that he was inwardly suppressing laughter.

Of course, everyone around knew that the sole reason this man had the backbone to block six people reeking of death qi was simplly because the Zahki clan was one of the most powerful in the Western Region.
They specialized in cultivating Death Qi, so naturally, the Dead World fell under their jurisdiction.
Nobody dared mess with them, and Uncle Drew’s team, who had done their research before coming, knew this.
Nara waved her hand, and five more pouches flew toward the man, who once again wore a shocked expression as he caught every last one.
Uncle Drew gestured for them to move toward the portal that led directly to the Dead World.
After all, they had paid for passage.
However, just as they moved, the man cleared his throat and blocked their path once more.
"Hold it right there.
You still haven’t paid for your mounts.
In case you are unaware, it costs extra to transport a mount to the Dead World." He gestured with a smirk on his face.
"That will be another six million high-grade spirit stones."
Uncle Drew’s Hellhorse neighed, clearly angered by what the bastard was trying to pull.
Uncle Drew narrowed his eyes at the man, who seemed to think he could do as he pleased.
Unfortunately for him, he had picked the wrong team to mess with.
"Nightblade, kill him."
"With pleasure."
Nara’s hand moved to her sword, and before anyone could register what had happened, it was already over.
The man’s head rolled to the ground, and that was the end of him.
"In your next life, be careful around dead people," Uncle Drew said coldly.
"Half-dead," Nara corrected with a smirk.
"My bad," Uncle Drew laughed.
While they were akin to dead people, all Night Riders existed between life and death, standing on the boundary that separated the living from the dead.
As such, they were not truly undead.
Turning slightly, Uncle Drew’s gaze landed on the people who were still frozen in shock.
"When they come asking who did this, tell them Kael Duskbane, Captain of the Night Riders, did it."
His Hellhorse moved forward and kicked away the head of the bastard who had tried to extort them.
Soon, they vanished into the portal, leaving everyone pale.
They had, of course, heard of the legendary Night Riders before.
So if what Uncle Drew said was true, perhaps there would soon be quite a show to watch here.
Meanwhile, after entering the portal, the Night Riders appeared in a world shrouded in red mist, with the aura of death permeating every corner.
Uncle Drew surveyed their surroundings to ensure there were no threats nearby.
Once he was certain they were all safe, he began formulating a comprehensive plan.
"Our mission is to traverse this dangerous terrain to the Black Star Domain and kill the Black Fire Demon Dragon.
As for what we’re really here for, the Young Master said we’ll know when we see it."

chapters.title: Chapter 1715: First Encounter
paragraphs: "To get to the Black Star Domain, we must travel westward through the Worm Desert and the Howling Mountains," Uncle Drew said, keeping a calm expression.

"The Worm Desert is filled with sand-type beasts, ones said to rival some of the most dangerous immortals and demigods in the universe. According to my report, there are three overlords in the Worm Desert.
If we want to get through that place, the report says we can pass through the Domain Millipede’s territory. It is the most easy-going domain beast in all of the Worm Desert.
Luckily for us, we have steeds, so traversing that place will be easy, especially if we travel at night. However, it is after we cross the Worm Desert that the real problem starts.

That place is the domain of a sole alpha wolf called the Eternal Moon Wolf. It is one of the strongest demigods here, and as you all are aware, we cannot pass through without a battle, so we should be ready for a grave fight.

That said, when we get to the Worm Desert, we should also be ready for battle. None of you should slack off since this is our first official mission. If we fail, it will damage our reputation, so we should bring our best game and be ready to fight grave battles."
His teammates nodded.
They have a vast stretch of land to cover, so leaving now sounds like the best choice.

If the map they bought was real, they would reach the Worm Desert in three days’ time. This meant that if they didn’t encounter any trouble along the way, they would meet the first obstacle in three days once they got to the Worm Desert, where even the sand is dangerous.
So they set off, and as Night Riders, when the sun dipped and night arrived, they would move much faster. But even during the day, they were moving at a speed that defied normal four-legged steeds.

Meanwhile, back on the moon, a couple of hours after Uncle Drew and his team passed through, ten demigods and twenty-five Immortal Lords, each oozing the power of death, arrived, immediately drawing attention.
The moment they arrived, everyone familiar with the Zahki Clan recognized them as the 5th Death Team. They are a formidable team.
Because of how much influence the Zahki Clan had in this side of the universe, their appearance caused many to become alert.

Today, most had witnessed the killing of a high-ranking member of the Zahki Clan. So, with a team of deadly warriors arriving, it was clear their mission was to ensure the people who had killed their clansman were punished with death.

Without even glancing at anyone, they stepped into the portal and vanished into the Dead World, where, using their extensive knowledge of that treacherous place, they would hunt down the six riders who claimed to be Night Riders.
Three hours after they entered, three figures, moving like shadows, appeared and, without paying attention to the new person in charge of collecting the fees, entered the portal.
If Uncle Drew and his team made people tremble, then the presence of these three individuals made them pale with terror.

"To think that Death Paradise had also sent representatives after those Night Riders. Looks like a good show will soon take place in the Dead World and even here. I’d better leave before I get swallowed up in whatever is coming."
Many left, but the few who clearly wanted to see everything remained—the daring ones even paid the fees and followed behind the three teams.
[Two Days Later]

Uncle Drew raised his hand to stop his team just as they were drawing closer to the Worm Desert. They halted, and he jumped down from his hell horse and landed heavily on the ground, placing his right palm against the earth.
After a few seconds, he stood up and turned to Nara, giving her a simple nod.
She nodded back and commanded her hell horse to move. A few seconds later, Saden followed. Then Vargus followed after him. Soon, Lene and Eryndor also left the scene, leaving only Uncle Drew behind.
After they were gone, Uncle Drew took a deep breath and then turned to his left.
"One thing I hate is people who think they can sneak up on me. It usually doesn’t end well for them, so why don’t you reveal yourself so we can have a civilized conversation?"
Nobody said anything for a few seconds. Suddenly, the ground split open, and a figure clad in stone armor emerged, a large broadsword resting on his shoulder.
Judging by the dents on his armor and the fact that his left arm was injured, it was clear he had recently been in battle. Perhaps that battle had nearly claimed his life.
The man examined Uncle Drew for a few more seconds before smirking.
"Stupid of you to let your teammates go. What, were you hoping to send a message that you alone are enough, or that you’re no threat, so I should let you go?"
Uncle Drew smiled and replied, "The former. I alone can take you on. And no, I sent them away because the beasts chasing after you are coming our way, so they must hold them back."

"Oh, so you’re a group of idiots, huh? I guess killing you will allow me to absorb your blood and heal my injuries. I have plans, you see, and you, my friend, happen to have just the right dose of blood I need."
Uncle Drew shook his head, almost as if he pitied the man.
"Such a pity. I actually expected you to ask for help rather than try to take it. However, since you’ve made your decision, allow me to open your eyes."
Uncle Drew extended his hand, and his hell horse vanished. Then his clothing changed, taking the form of red-and-black armor made from a very durable cloak.
In his grip, two identical swords appeared, their blades completely black and decorated with white and red runes.

Uncle Drew himself is a handsome man who appears to be in his early 30s. He possesses short dark hair with a few red strands falling on the left side of his face. His green pupils make him appear regal and, at the same time, dangerous.
The man grinned and lowered his broadsword, thinking he had found prey.
Then, with heavy steps, he advanced, his sword dragging behind him. Uncle Drew shook his head again and started walking forward. His steps soon grew faster, and before long, he was running as well.
In no time, they met, and with both hands gripping the hilt of his broadsword, the man swung hard, the veins on his arms bulging as a deadly pressure descended upon Uncle Drew.

However, when the sword came at him, Uncle Drew planted his left foot into the ground and used the sword in his right hand to block the attack. The ground split open, revealing the immense force behind the strike.
However, before the man could pull back, Uncle Drew lowered his arm, causing the broadsword to drop closer to his shoulder. Then, using his left hand, he swung his other sword at the man’s rib.
This forced the man to pull his sword back to block the attack aimed at his side.
However, by pulling his sword back, he inadvertently gave up his only advantage, which had been keeping Uncle Drew’s right hand occupied. As a dual wielder, each hand was akin to a deadly weapon.

So while the man realized his side was exposed and attempted to defend himself, Uncle Drew’s right hand moved, and the next second, a large hand still gripping a broadsword came tumbling to the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 1716: Kael Duskbane
paragraphs: It was a decisive swing, one that 99% of warriors would have missed.
Judging by how powerful the man’s swing was, most warriors would have struggled to remain focused, let alone find the opportunity to retaliate and gamble like that.
However, Uncle Drew wasn’t like everyone else. He was Kael Duskbane, the greatest warrior to ever walk the face of the universe. He saw an opening, and he exploited it.
The man’s eyes widened, his expression turning pale.
He instinctively staggered back, clutching the bloody stump where his arm had once been. Blood poured out like a crimson fountain, splattering across the broken earth.
However, before he could even process what had happened, Uncle Drew was already in front of him.
A cold glint flashed through the darkness.
The left sword in Uncle Drew’s hand swept through the air.
Slash!
A deep wound opened across the man’s chest.
The stone armor that had protected him throughout countless battles split apart as though it were nothing more than paper.
The man coughed up blood and retreated dozens of meters, staggering and stumbling as he moved.
Only then did Uncle Drew stop advancing.
The injured warrior stared at him in disbelief, even regretting his decision to attack when he should have asked for help instead.
He had mistakenly stumbled into the cave of a very dangerous beast. It took him a great deal of effort to escape from there.
However, just when he could have made a run for it, he was met with yet another obstacle, one he thought would allow him to recover some of what he had lost.
Initially, he hid himself and decided to wait for the right moment to strike.
However, when he saw Uncle Drew’s teammates leave him behind, he saw his chance and took it.
Unfortunately for him, he had come after the wrong person.
"What kind of swordsmanship is that?"
Uncle Drew calmly flicked the blood from his blade.
"The kind that kills people."
Even long before he became the captain of the Night Riders, he was known as the greatest warrior simply because of how decisive he was.

He never missed an opportunity to kill. According to him, the essence of combat was murder, and he had mastered the art of killing. Every small opening could be exploited by him, allowing him to kill in the most inconvenient ways possible.

While legendary warriors like Lord Genesis, Blood Spear King, and Ruthless Bandit had walked this universe with great combat power, none of them came close to understanding the art of killing the way he did.
Standing atop a small peak, Nara and the rest of the Night Riders watched the battle between the man and their captain.
"Looks like he still got it," Eryndor said, his expression brightening.
Before he met Kael Duskbane, he had been hailed as one of the greatest Hell Summoners in the universe.
However, on the day they met, even with the strength and support of his summons, Kael Duskbane dismantled his defenses in less than ten minutes.
It was one of the most humbling moments of his life. Since then, he had become one of the few people who would wholeheartedly give his life for Kael Duskbane before the man even asked.
"Captain has always been the greatest. Now, it seems he has become even more monstrous," Nara said, a smile playing on her lips.
Just as most people have someone they look up to, Nara looked up to Uncle Drew.

She might be the wife of a monster, but in her heart, her Captain was the greatest warrior in the universe. He had saved her life so many times that if she started talking about them, it would take an entire day.
Uncle Drew shook his head for the third time and smiled. Then he sheathed his swords and walked toward the man.
"I won’t kill you since you’ll be answering some questions of mine."
The man tried to reject his offer and arrogantly threatened to kill him. After all, he always had a backup plan in place, one that involved his death.
However, since he couldn’t afford to have his body eaten by beasts, he wanted Uncle Drew to kill him instead.
Before he could say anything, however, Uncle Drew’s eyes lit up with flames, sending chills down his spine.
"No matter what you have in mind, killing you would be the end of you, so you’d better play nice. I might just show mercy and heal you," Uncle Drew said as he stopped before him.
"You came from the direction we’re heading. Judging by the cuts on your armor and body, you fought a beast and ran from it, so why don’t you tell me what happened?"
The aura of Hellflame leaked from Uncle Drew’s body, causing the man to tremble. He quickly answered the question.
"I was ambushed by three agents of the Soul Temple, forcing me to flee. However, after escaping, I mistakenly stumbled into the cave of a Shadowtail Scorpion. I barely survived..."
He sighed and added, "It would be best if you took a different path since that beast isn’t one you and your team are prepared for."
"A Shadowtail Scorpion, you say?" Uncle Drew smiled and nodded. "It would be perfect for Saden’s shadow affinity to finally reach the Absolute Stage."
The man stared at Uncle Drew in horror but said nothing.
"What about the Soul Temple agents? Do you know where they can be found?" Uncle Drew asked, but the man shook his head.

"It is a known fact that in the Dead World, nobody looks for the Soul Temple agents. They find you and make sure you die before they leave. I was lucky to survive against them, so continue on the same path at your own peril."
Uncle Drew nodded and turned around.
"I’d advise you to leave this place before it’s too late."
He flicked his hand, and a Tier 20 Healing Pill flew toward the man, who caught it.
"That will help fix the wound on your chest and reattach your severed hand. If we meet again and you draw your weapon on me, then death is what awaits you."
His shadow moved, and the Hellhorse appeared beneath him. He was lifted onto its back, and moments later, he was gone from sight.
"Haaa..."
The man sighed, finally calming down.
"That was a close call," he muttered, a painful smile appearing on his face.
If only he hadn’t tried to attack Uncle Drew, he wouldn’t have landed himself in this situation. Fortunately for him, he narrowly managed to survive and even earn Uncle Drew’s favor.
After cursing himself a few times for being stupid, he swallowed the pill and began his healing process.
Meanwhile, after leaving the man behind, Uncle Drew reunited with his teammates.
"We have to make a detour to a place where a Shadowtail Scorpion can be found," Uncle Drew said, and his teammates nodded.
The Shadowtail Scorpion was a creature of pure shadow. It was one of the few elemental beasts with a shadow-type elemental affinity, so obtaining it would help Saden elevate her shadow affinity.
Kent had sent them here on a mission, but he also told them to take advantage of the Dead World to grow stronger.

He was lifted onto its back, and moments later, he was gone from sight.
"Haaa..."
The man sighed, finally calming down.
"That was a close call," he muttered, a painful smile appearing on his face.
If only he hadn’t tried to attack Uncle Drew, he wouldn’t have landed himself in this situation.
Fortunately for him, he narrowly managed to survive and even earn Uncle Drew’s favor.
After cursing himself a few times for being stupid, he swallowed the pill and began his healing process.
Meanwhile, after leaving the man behind, Uncle Drew reunited with his teammates.
"We have to make a detour to a place where a Shadowtail Scorpion can be found," Uncle Drew said, and his teammates nodded.
The Shadowtail Scorpion was a creature of pure shadow.
It was one of the few elemental beasts with a shadow-type elemental affinity, so obtaining it would help Saden elevate her shadow affinity.
Kent had sent them here on a mission, but he also told them to take advantage of the Dead World to grow stronger.

chapters.title: Chapter 1717: Shadowtail Scorpion
paragraphs: It took less than 5 hours for Uncle Drew and his team to reach the location of the Shadowtail Scorpion, where they planned to kill the beast and let Saden absorb its core.
This mission they are on is dangerous, so if getting stronger along the way was something they could do, they wouldn’t miss any chance they are present with.
They stopped 2 km away from the cave and started strategizing.
"A shadow creature truly lives here," Uncle Drew said, looking toward the cave in the distance. All of them could also sense the danger hidden inside it.
"So how are we approaching this?" Nara asked, and Uncle Drew quickly came up with a plan. In fact, he had already developed this plan on their way here.
"While it is indeed a dangerous demigod-level beast, all six of us attacking it will just be overdoing it at this point. So the plan is simple.

Vargus, Eryndor, and I will draw it out, and you ladies must work together to kill it. Remember, it is a shadow-type beast that has already touched divinity and even possesses a domain. If you slack off, you will find yourselves in trouble."
They nodded and soon got into action.
Uncle Drew, Vargus, and Eryndor moved forward, allowing the Shadowtail Scorpion to notice them while the three ladies hid and waited for the beast to show itself.
Hidden inside the cave, just as Uncle Drew and his teammates crossed the 1 km mark, a deep purple eye opened, and the shadows began to move.
Soon, the shadows flowed out of the cave and began to darken the surrounding space.
"It has noticed us. You all should be ready for battle."

Just as he said that, shadow tendrils shot out, lashing out toward the approaching figure. Uncle Drew moved back while Vargus leapt into the air and unleashed a deadly attack using his hammer, sending flames flying at the tendrils.
When they collided, the tendrils burst apart, but new ones formed the next second, making the space even darker.
"I will take on close combat to draw its attacks."
Uncle Drew moved forward and closed in on the tendrils.
He spun his right sword and then, with a deadly swing, unleashed thousands of flame arcs that streaked toward the cave.
SKRREEEEKKKKKK
A strange clicking sound came from the cave just as the sword arcs closed in. Then, from deep within the cave, a powerful force surged outward, and Uncle Drew felt his body tense for a second.
"Eryndor..." Uncle Drew called out, and Eryndor’s staff moved, conjuring a green sun.
"BURN."
The sun moved toward the cave, causing the ground to shake. The beast’s oppressive energy was suppressed by the sun, showing it isn’t an ordinary attack.
This made the Shadowtail Scorpion, which had expected its aura alone to intimidate these people, release another piercing clicking sound.
Then a large black-and-purple tail emerged from the cave and pierced the sun, shattering it completely.
"Eat my hammer!" Vargus roared, seizing the moment of destruction to cause even more destruction.
BOOOOM
His hammer slammed into the cave, shattering it. Debris flew everywhere, revealing a large opening where a colossal scorpion could be seen lying down.
It was about 120 meters long, with a body made of metallic fibres. Its tail dripped poison, and even the air around it seemed poisoned while also being infused with shadow energy.
The Shadowtail Scorpion was colossal and extremely dangerous to behold. However, now that its body had been revealed, killing it would become much easier too.

Uncle Drew lifted his swords, and they lit up in flames. As a Night Rider, he naturally has an affinity for Hell Flame. But even if it didn’t, he had once ruled countless battlefields, so this was a piece of cake for him.
"Flame Cleaver."
A large green arc flashed out and landed on the Shadowtail Scorpion’s body, producing a metallic clang.
"Well, that is a problem."
Uncle Drew jumped back, evading a poison dart. However, before he could stabilise his stance, a tail came crashing toward him. He didn’t panic or even make an attempt to defend.
BANG

Vargus appeared and slammed his hammer into the tail, causing it to tremble. However, it didn’t end there. Just before the Shadowtail Scorpion could pull its tail back, Eryndor cast a spell, and a massive boulder came crashing down toward it.
It let out a third clicking sound and dissolved its body into shadows.
"Hell Rend."
Just as it turned into shadow, Nara emerged and attacked, aiming her attack 300 meters away, where nothing worth attacking could be seen.

If someone else saw her attack, they would have thought she had wasted her chance. However, the Night Riders had fought many battles together, and they knew the infamous Nightblade wouldn’t make such a rookie mistake.
Just when her attack was a meter away, the Shadowtail Scorpion reformed from the shadows, only to be met with a deadly strike that carved a large wound into its body.
SKRREEEEKKKKKK

A painful screech came from the Shadowtail Scorpion. However, it had no time to even turn toward Nara since Lene had also appeared and unleashed a deadly spear attack, manifesting a giant spear in the air.
The manifested spear shot forward and pierced the hide of the Shadowtail Scorpion, drawing blood.
"Mountain Falling."
Vargus followed up next, his colossal hammer striking the scorpion’s head.
An arrow came from the side and pierced one of its eyes. Saden emerged from the shadows and unleashed three more arrows before slipping back into them.
Uncle Drew, whose first attack had failed, smiled when he saw how well-coordinated his teammates were.
They knew when to take advantage of an opening and when to hold back. Right now, thanks to Nara’s attack, they had managed to inflict severe damage on the Shadowtail Scorpion.

However, it was still nowhere close to death. In fact, just as Eryndor summoned another giant boulder, a wave of terrifying poison exploded from the beast’s body, forcing the six attackers to retreat.
It isolated Nara and lunged forward. However, it hadn’t gone far when Vargus’s hammer slammed into its side, sending it flying back.
"Giant Form."
Vargus activated a body-enhancing technique. At once, his body morphed and transformed, turning him into a 60-meter-tall giant.
"Hammer Head Dominion."
His hands moved, and the sky changed colour. Then, before the Shadowtail Scorpion could turn and retaliate, Vargus unleashed a devastating blow, sending the beast flying backwards.
This gave Uncle Drew the opening he needed to unleash one of his deadliest sword techniques.
"Sword Bath in Flames."
The air around him turned scorching hot. Then, with a decisive slash, a thin arc of green flames flashed out from his sword, severing the Shadowtail Scorpion’s tail.
Surprisingly, it tried to reattach the tail, shooting tendrils of shadow toward it.

However, Nara appeared like a blur and severed the tendrils. This gave the brute of the team enough time to unleash a bone-crushing hammer strike, shattering the tail and cutting off all attempts to reattach it.
With its tail gone, Saden emerged from the shadows again and pulled back her bowstring, manifesting a 3-meter-tall arrow.
The shadows around her moved and augmented her bow, merging into the arrow and causing the already oppressive energy surrounding it to intensify.
"Shadow Harvesting Arrow."
She let the arrow loose, and like a meteor, it flew through the air, striking the small opening that served as the maw of the Shadowtail Scorpion.
The arrow passed through and vanished into its body.

Uncle Drew sheathed his swords, and Nara did the same. Eryndor, who had already stopped attacking, shook his head and smiled. Lene, who had only attacked once, remained where she was with her arms folded, while the almighty Vargus rested his hammer on his shoulder.
The battle was over, even though the Shadowtail Scorpion was still alive.
Saden smiled faintly, then snapped her fingers.
"Explode."

chapters.title: Chapter 1718: Shadow Spirit
paragraphs: It is not an exaggeration to say that the moment Saden’s arrow enters the body of an opponent, that is the end of the person or beast. It’s unreal, yet truly devastating to imagine.
During the Dark Era, when the Night Riders became enemies of the Universe Council, both humans and beasts came after them, forcing them to go on the run.
One time, while on the run, some of them separated from the team to draw the pursuers away. Saden, being an archer, volunteered to lure away a group of wolfkin warriors.
After pulling them away and running for two days, she was cornered. At that moment, many would have despaired; however, not Saden.
That day, while she was surrounded on all sides, she unleashed her true power upon the universe.
The Universe Council claim that among the Night Riders, only a few could perform wonders and none of them was Saden, the Shadow Archer.
However, that day, the most chilling thing happened, and since then, the legend of the Shadow Archer has started to spread.
They claim she moves without a sound and strikes with absolute precision. They even say her arrows don’t move like normal arrows, but like shadows.
All that was true about the Shadow Archer. However, her true power lies in her uncanny ability to exploit even the smallest opening.
If Uncle Drew can take advantage of small openings to kill, then with Saden, making a mistake when locked in battle against her means dying in the most violent way.
She exploded 1,002 arrows that day, killing 1,000 gods and 2 Supremes. Since then, whenever they are locked in battle, and her arrow enters a beast, they know the battle is over.
Today, the Shadowtail Scorpion was unlucky enough to meet the Shadow Archer, whose arrows are even more deadly when they enter the inside of a beast or a person.
The moment the arrow exploded, the Shadowtail Scorpion fell back, and that was the end of the battle.
When the Shadowtail Scorpion died, a head-sized core appeared from its body, oozing the insidious power of shadow and darkness.
"Go ahead, Saden. We will protect you."
Saden nodded at Uncle Drew’s words, moved forward, and jumped onto the back of the Shadowtail Scorpion without fear.
She took a deep breath and gently extended her hand, touching the core.
BOOOM!
A powerful shadow energy exploded from her body the moment she touched the core. However, just as it appeared, it vanished like smoke. Then strands of shadow qi began to be absorbed into her body.
"Would she attempt to reform her Shadow Spirit?" Nara asked, walking toward Uncle Drew.

Uncle Drew looked at Saden for a moment before replying, "I don’t know how far she has reached in Shadow Cultivation this time around or how much stronger her soul is, but if she can form a Shadow Spirit, that would be good."

"Let’s hope she manages to form a Shadow Spirit then. The last time, after forming a Shadow Spirit, her power took a significant leap. Perhaps this time around, she will become even stronger," Nara sighed, sat on a boulder, and started to wait for Saden to handle her business.
Lene also walked to a stone on the side and sat down.
While in battle, she attacked the Shadowtail Scorpion only once. However, looking down on her for that would be a huge mistake. In truth, her true power is on another level.
Already, she is a Demigod, and soon, she will use the Primordial Chamber to awaken her Primordial Spirit.
Once that happens, just like the rest of Kent’s wives, she will also start walking the Ancient Path. But before that, if there is a chance to grow stronger, then all of them would take it.
As for Vargus, he jumped onto a chunk of the cave wall that remained and started to scan the surroundings. Like Kaizo, he is a lover of battle.
So while this one was short, he enjoyed himself. But now, after having a taste, he wanted more.

Eryndor remained on the side, his green hair billowing behind him. He is perhaps the quietest one in the group, not because he is an introvert, but because he spends most of his time talking to his hell demons.

He had already summoned four, but had yet to use them in battle. Aside from having a Hell Summoner class as his primary class, he also has a Combat Mage class that allows him to tap into the power of his Flame and Ice affinities.
So he may appear to be a summoner of hell demons, but he is actually one of the most accomplished Combat Mages of the Dark Era.
He stood 6’4" tall, with a slim build and a set of green eyes. He is not an elf, but he has long ears. He appears to be in his early twenties, but in fact, he is much older.
A few hours passed, and before long, Saden had spent over five hours absorbing the core. As the minutes went by, Uncle Drew and the others could feel the shift in the air around her.
Clearly, she was advancing closer to the Absolute Rank, where her Shadow Affinity would finally become more versatile, allowing her to tap into it more deeply and use it more actively.
Suddenly, the surrounding light began to grow dim.

Uncle Drew jumped to his feet and scanned the area, but sensed no changes that suggested they were under attack. This made him shift his attention to Saden, whose body had begun to release waves of shadow qi.
"She has reached the Absolute Stage," Lene muttered, a smile appearing on her face.
The rest of her teammates also smiled. A win for Saden was a win for the team, so they all became happy.

However, their joy was amplified when Saden’s shadow suddenly moved and appeared before her. Then, the Shadowtail Scorpion she was seated on started to turn into dark mist. In no time, not even a bone remained.
However, the mist gathered slowly, then began to move and merge with Saden’s shadow.
The process lasted for just two minutes, but after the last strand of mist merged with Saden’s shadow, the remaining core moved and merged into her chest.
BOOOM!
A powerful explosion of energy erupted from both Saden and her shadow. Then, in what could only be described as a shocking sight, the shadow smiled and nodded at Saden, who also nodded back.
"I guess she really did it again this time, too," Nara said with a smile as she started walking toward Saden. "Congratulations, Saden. You have become even more powerful now."
"It is all thanks to you all helping me kill the Shadowtail Scorpion."
Nara hugged her, and Lene joined them.
After the hug, Saden turned and looked at Uncle Drew.
"Thank you, Captain."
"No need to thank me. It was a team effort."
Saden’s shadow stood behind her, wearing an expressionless look on her face. They looked identical, but at first glance, one would know which of them was real.
"Looks like you still need more shadow cores to elevate the power of your Shadow Spirit," Uncle Drew said, and Saden nodded sadly.
"She hasn’t awakened any of her innate abilities yet, so aside from augmenting my bow and arrows, she can’t do anything more than that."
"We will handle that as we travel, so relax for now," Uncle Drew said.
After resting for another hour, they continued on their way...
