chapters.title: Chapter 1719: Sand Centipedes
paragraphs: Uncle Drew and his team travelled several more miles after Saden was done absorbing the shadow core. They are now much closer to the Worm Desert.
Now that Saden had formed her shadow spirit, it was just a matter of getting more cores so she could strengthen it and make it one of her strongest abilities.
With a shadow spirit, she can augment her bow and arrows, strengthening them beyond their current limits. Aside from that, she can use her shadow to move.
She can send her shadow thousands of miles away, and whenever she wants, she can swap places with it or teleport directly to its side.
Unlike the tower, where teleporting inside during danger is impossible, she can easily do that with her shadow. This would allow her to escape grave situations more quickly and safely.

Aside from that, as an assassin, she thrives on keeping her presence concealed at all times. With the shadow spirit, she can remain undetected even from gods and the more she improves her shadow spirit, the more robust that concealing ability becomes.
But like any good thing, it would take some effort to strengthen it. Now, however, she can augment her bow and arrows, making them at least 30% more powerful.
After travelling for a while, they finally arrived at the borders of the Worm Desert. Stretching before them was a vast expanse of red dunes filled with all kinds of dangers.
The most common beasts found within the Worm Desert were the Death Worms and Sand Centipede. They lived beneath the sand and were extremely sensitive to vibrations.
While they would not reveal themselves immediately, the moment they sensed a presence, they would stalk their prey and attack when they believed they had a good chance of winning.
Uncle Drew and his team waited for nightfall before they started moving across the Worm Desert. As Night Riders, their power was strongest during the night.
They chose to take advantage of that, and thankfully, their first night in the Worm Desert was quiet. When they took a break, they camped in a stone valley where several caves served as shelter.
They had the tower with them, so purchasing supplies at their master’s expense was that easy.
However, while the night was quiet, a few hours into their relaxation, the ground shook, and a 250-meter-long Sand Centipede emerged, hissing as it lunged at Lene, who was the closest.

She jumped and landed on its back, her spear stabbing toward the joints along its body. However, before her spear could connect with the beast, it trembled, and bone spears shot out from its body, forcing Lene to leap back.
She spun her spear, deflecting some of them, while a few grazed her arms and shoulder.
The moment she landed on the ground, Vargus roared into battle, his hammer connecting with the back of the Sand Centipede. It was blasted backwards, crashing through the surrounding stones.
Uncle Drew leapt into the air, and a wave of sword qi exploded out of his body. At once, the air around him became razor-sharp.
"Eryndor, draw its attention," he commanded.
Then, with a sudden movement, he appeared above the Sand Centipede and unleashed a deadly arc, carving a deep wound into the creature’s body.
The creature rattled its body and unleashed more bone spears. However, Eryndor was already on the move, his staff weaving runes into existence.
Meanwhile, Saden slipped into the shadows and vanished from sight, while Nara stood back, watching the battle and paying attention to the surroundings.
The moment she sensed danger, she would make a move to counter it.
So, in this battle, only Uncle Drew, Eryndor, Vargus, and Lene were participating. Even Saden hadn’t attacked yet, and the creature was already close to death’s door.
However, for this creature to have snuck up on them, it was clear that the Worm Desert wasn’t as simple as they had thought. None of them saw it coming, not even for a moment.
So they had to remain on high alert.
Of course, that decision saved their lives a minute into the battle.
"Three more incoming!"
Nara shouted, pointing east of their location. Just beneath the surface, three colossal Sand Centipedes sped in their direction, probably alerted by the battle.
Or perhaps they had been following them, just as the first one had.
The moment she alerted the others, she moved and clashed with one of the Sand Centipedes, isolating that one from the horde.
Lene also moved and attacked the second Sand Centipede, while Eryndor and Saden took on the third.
Saden had to come out of the shadows for this one. Her bow oozed shadowy energy as one arrow after another flew out.
Meanwhile, flames and ice spells continued to pour from Eryndor, who had yet to summon any of his Hell demons.
They still didn’t know if these were the only Sand Centipedes in the area, so conserving as much energy as possible was the most logical decision they could make.

Lene brandished her spear, meeting her opponent in a deadly collision that sent shockwaves in all directions. She wasn’t a brute fighter, but she was a Demigod, and against another Demigod-level beast, she wouldn’t allow herself to be outmatched in strength.
After the violent collision, both combatants were pushed back several meters. But as if that was nothing, they clashed again.
Lene moved with deadly speed, harnessing her wind element.
Her spear also lit up with flames, and with one deadly slash, a large, terrifying arc exploded outward and connected with the Sand Centipede, sending it flying backwards.
The Sand Centipede crashed through a dozen stone pillars before finally coming to a stop. Before it could recover, Lene was already upon it.
She understood the need to end the battle before she was forced to fight multiple opponents. With decisive steps and attacks, she was like a blur, her speed blinding.
Her spear thrust forward like a streak of lightning, piercing through one of the gaps in its armoured shell. The beast screeched in pain and retaliated instantly.
Hundreds of bone spikes erupted from its body, turning the surrounding area into a forest of deadly spears.
Lene twisted her body midair, narrowly avoiding most of them. A few tore through her sleeves, leaving shallow cuts behind.
"Looks like I have become rusty after enjoying the comfort of the tower these past years." A smile appeared on her lips, then her eyes lit up with flames.
Rather than retreating, she accelerated, her long, dark, and green hair billowing in the air behind her.
Wind gathered around her body, forming spiralling currents that increased her speed severalfold. Flames danced around the tip of her spear as she descended like a meteor.
Boom!
The attack smashed into the Sand Centipede’s back, creating a massive crater beneath it.
Both her Wind and Flame affinities had already reached the Perfect Harmony stage.
On the side, Saden was like a blinking dot, appearing for a moment and fast enough to unleash an arrow only to slip back into the shadows.f
After attaining Absolute shadow affinity, her control over shadows had increased severalfold.

Every arrow she fired found its mark. The more she unleashed a barrage of arrows, the slower that beast became. Her shadow spirit had augmented her bow, so every arrow carried 30 times the power it usually carried.
However, considering both she and Eryndor are only True Immortals, locked in battle against a demigod, it was only natural that they weren’t having an easy time with the Sand Centipede.
She may have slowed it down, but that doesn’t mean she had killed it.

Every last battle happening was just decisive and extremely chaotic. However, just when Lene was getting closer to killing her opponent, a bang came from the distance, followed by an avalanche of sand.
Uncle Drew’s brow knitted.

chapters.title: Chapter 1720: Eryndor Unleashed
paragraphs: The sand avalanche rose into the air and came crashing down, revealing a colossal Sand Centipede.
This one was far larger and longer than the ones Uncle Drew and his team were fighting.

It stretched over 450 meters in length and was covered in a dense metallic carapace, far harder and more imposing than the others. That alone told them they were looking at the Sand Centipedes’ leader.
Naturally, the moment it appeared, Uncle Drew knew what would follow.
"Eryndor, handle it," Uncle Drew commanded.
Eryndor nodded.

In the distance, dozens of Sand Centipedes could be seen rushing toward them. The moment the leader appeared, the entire horde revealed itself as well, causing the already chaotic battlefield to become even more suffocating.
Luckily, they had many trump cards, and one of them was Eryndor, whose Hell Summoner class had been lying dormant for quite some time.

He waved his staff through the air and, with a powerful thrust, slammed the head of the weapon into the side of the Sand Centipede he and Saden were fighting, sending it flying backwards. Its colossal body rattled like a broken snake.
"Saden, keep it at bay for a minute."
Eryndor moved and appeared two hundred meters away from the approaching Sand Centipedes.
"Hell Gate... Open."
The head of his staff glowed brighter, and then, as if tearing a hole through space itself, four imposing dark gates appeared, each oozing a dreadful aura.
Eryndor had summoned all four of his Hell Demons since the battle required their assistance, despite knowing they would complain.
Of course, none of them had reached their limits yet, but they didn’t have the luxury of revealing more of their personal trump cards before reaching their destination.
It was the secretive nature of the Night Riders that allowed them to survive countless dangers and remain feared throughout the universe.
"Finally, I can stretch my legs."

A voice echoed from within the first gate, followed by the appearance of a three-meter-tall demon with skin forged from living metal. He held two massive broadswords and was clad in jagged crimson metallic armour.
Every movement of his body radiated dense blood qi, making him look less like a demon and more like a walking blood calamity.
The demon stepped out of the gate with a grin stretched across his metallic face. Clearly, like most arrogant demons, he still possessed a rebellious nature.
However, he was needed, so there was no way Eryndor would unsummon him.
The moment his feet touched the ground, the surrounding sand exploded outward under the sheer weight of his presence.
His crimson eyes swept across the battlefield before locking onto the approaching horde.
"Looks like you finally found a battlefield worth summoning me for."
A savage smile appeared on his face, but at least he didn’t try to walk back into the gate.
"You’d better increase my resources after this," Thrakos, the Demon of Dread, said.
Before Eryndor could answer, another figure emerged from the second gate.

Unlike the first demon, this one was lean and tall, standing nearly four meters in height. His body seemed to be made entirely of shadows and darkness. Two curved black blades rested at his waist, while six crimson eyes glowed beneath a hood of living darkness.
The temperature around him instantly dropped, filling the air with intense killing intent.
He glanced at the battlefield and sighed.
"You interrupted the sleep of the great Zandros for insects?"

Eryndor just smirked, forgetting how annoying this bastard actually was. However, if he was being honest, these Sand Centipedes were indeed insects. But Uncle Drew wanted them to use only half of their true power for now, so the hell demons were needed.
The third gate trembled.
A deafening roar erupted from within before a gigantic beast stepped through, its presence radiating dread and the aura of a true predator.

It resembled a demonic lion standing over fifty meters tall. Black flames covered its entire body, while six horns curved backwards from its skull. Beneath its fur, a thick metallic carapace covered its body, making it nearly impossible to wound.
Every breath it released scorched the air.
The moment it emerged, many of the approaching Sand Centipedes slowed down instinctively.

Even beasts understood fear. They could sense that a true predator had arrived, and its gaze was locked onto the leader of the Sand Centipedes, causing the latter to tremble slightly when their eyes met.
The Hell Demon was Kha’zixarath, the Hell Devastator. It had once served Eryndor across many battlefields. Today, he would unleash chaos with it yet again.
Then the fourth gate opened completely.
The battlefield suddenly fell silent, almost as if the Hell Demon had come to feed on the very sounds around it.
Just as everything became quiet, a woman walked out.
She wore a black dress decorated with silver runes. Her pale skin contrasted sharply with her flowing white hair.
Unlike the other three demons, she radiated no overwhelming aura. Yet the moment she appeared, Uncle Drew glanced in her direction.
Even Nara’s expression became slightly serious. Eryndor had already informed them that he had managed to resummon four of the Hell Demons he had contracted in the past.
However, because he hadn’t told them which demons he had summoned—considering he had thousands of them during the Dark Era—they were unaware of the identities of the four.
Yet the moment this woman walked out, a terrible feeling crept back into their hearts.
The woman smiled.
"My, my... it seems Master Eryndor finally remembered I exist."
Eryndor rolled his eyes.
"You complain every single time, Xuanli," Eryndor replied, not caring much about the bad history his teammates had with Xuanli.
"Because you only summon me when you’re in trouble." She pouted, looking hurt.

"Just get the job done and make sure you don’t reveal too much. Kha’zixarath will handle the leader. Your job is to make sure the rest don’t get close to us. And yes, you can take the cores after the battle."
"That is why I like you, Master. You really know how to make me blush."
Xuanli giggled and turned into a blur, appearing four hundred meters above the ground. Then, sitting in a lotus position, a zither appeared before her.
"Time to play some tunes."
She smiled and started plucking notes on the zither, filling the air with a cheerful melody. However, the approaching Sand Centipedes felt their souls invaded by an insidious curse.
Suddenly, they found themselves standing in an empty space. Facing them was the same woman playing the music, only this time she held a sword, and thousands more hovered behind her.

During the Dark Era, when the Night Riders travelled to Hell to temper themselves and strengthen their skills, they had mistakenly wandered into the domain of a Hell Demon known throughout the infernal realms as the Hell Requiem Demoness.

That day, some of them fought on the physical plane while others fought on the soul plane. That battle taught the Night Riders that no matter how powerful they were, there was always someone more terrifying.
Later, after she was defeated, she was forced to sign a contract with Eryndor, and since then, she has served him faithfully.
Over time, she came to like Eryndor and the others. However, they all knew one thing: their greatest defeat had come at the hands of the Hell Requiem Demoness.
Today, she had appeared once more, and Eryndor’s Hell Summoner class was finally unleashed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1721: Ambush
paragraphs: With Eryndor unleashing all four Hell Demons, the battle took a turn.
Kha’zixarath locked in against the leader of the Sand Centipedes, pushing it back several miles to make way for all the deadly attacks he had in store.
While he is a Hell Demon and can take on the form of a demi-human or human, Kha’zixarath chose to remain in his beast form. This was simply because he felt more true to himself in that form.
The beast form also allowed him to unleash more bestial attacks, and considering his opponent was a colossal beast, using his own deadly attacks was the best course of action.
And that had proven right. They both were Demigods, but with every attack, the Sand Demon was being pushed back, and that said a lot.
Kha’zixarath unleashed a deadly claw attack, then with the same momentum, he unleashed a powerful breath attack that scorched the hide of the Sand Centipede.
However, instead of retreating, it unleashed a tail attack that pushed Kha’zixarath back and immediately followed up with a deadly bone attack. For a moment, thousands of bones came at Kha’zixarath.
But as if the bone spears were nothing, he let them land on his body only for them to bounce off him as though he were made of the hardest metal known to man.

This made the Sand Centipede reevaluate its stance. But as if Kha’zixarath already knew the outcome of what it would do, he unleashed a domain skill, causing the entire space around them to be plunged into flames.
Everything was consumed by the domain skill.

In no time, the entire battlefield was sent into a storm of flames, causing Uncle Drew, who had already gained the upper hand and yet again severed the tail of the Sand Centipede as he did with the Shadowtail Scorpion, to grin.
"Looks like Eryndor came prepared this time around."
Back when they had just become Night Riders and he hadn’t yet summoned any Hell Demons, they used to tease him, calling him a summonless summoner.
Now, however, he had become a true Hell Summoner, and his summons were already wreaking havoc on the battlefield.

Away from Kha’zixarath, Thrakos also seemed to move like a shadow, his two curved blades dancing through the air, cutting one deadly wound after another into the bodies of the three Sand Centipedes he had taken on.
He had affinities for Darkness, Wind, and Poison, so every attack he unleashed carried traces of poison and decay, the kind that made him extremely dangerous.

But while he was having a good fight, Zandros was also weaving his way through the battlefield, unleashing one deadly attack after another. His affinities were Flame and Blood, so every attack carried the metallic stench of blood, while flames and destruction followed him.
Xuanli also remained seated, playing her zither while a part of her was raining dread upon the souls of the Sand Centipedes she had pulled into the astral plane.
She was among the few who could live without their souls. In fact, in all of the universe’s history, only a few people could do that, and they were called the Soulless.

They could separate their souls from their bodies, allowing them to live on different planes. Xuanli was able to do that, and now, while her body and mind worked together to unleash dreadful tunes that tortured the mind, her soul was also fighting a different battle, controlling thousands of swords with both her mind and soul.
Lene was also close to killing her opponent, while Vargus had already carved deep wounds into the body of his target.
The only ones still having a dangerous battle were Eryndor and Saden, who, despite their relentless attacks, couldn’t bring the Sand Centipede down.
But despite it all, they seemed calm, almost too calm for two Immortals fighting a Demigod-level beast whose power far exceeded that of most Demigods.
They were already aware of the kind of monsters they would be meeting, so they came prepared.
Some years back, the Immortal Worlds were for Immortals. But these days, the Demigods had dominated every corner of them.
So, coming to the Dead World, they were already prepared to fight grave battles and win every last one of them.

Suddenly, Lene’s body glowed, and wind blades circled her. Then, with a deadly slash, she unleashed an invisible wind blade that flew through the air and carved a deep wound into the body of the Sand Centipede.
Before it could get back up, she was already upon it.
"Wind Blade Cutter."

Another wind blade was unleashed, and as if she had pinpoint accuracy, the attack landed on exactly the same place where the large wound had been inflicted, further opening a massive gash in its body.
Blood poured out of it, causing the already wounded and sluggish Sand Centipede to try and make a run for it.
"Not on my watch."
Lene appeared overhead and, for the third time, unleashed another wind blade, splitting the worm in half.
She made sure the third attack landed exactly where the others had.
With its body split open, it was only a matter of time before it died.

But in the meantime, Lene dashed toward the Sand Centipede Saden and Eryndor were fighting. Just when she arrived there, Saden vanished into the shadows and appeared beside the severely wounded Sand Centipede.

Then, with one deadly arrow after another, she managed to end the suffering of the poor worm. She then collected the core and vanished, appearing beside the Sand Centipede whose tail Uncle Drew had severed, and did the same.
Meanwhile, Uncle Drew had already vanished from the battlefield.

He could not be seen anywhere. However, considering how devastating the battlefield was, nobody seemed to notice. Already, Zandros, Thrakos, Kha’zixarath, and Xuanli had taken the majority of the Sand Centipedes off the board, so the main team wasn’t under much pressure.

However, judging by how devastating the battle was, the disappearance of one of the key warriors, whose presence gave hope to the rest of his teammates, should have been noticed. Yet for ten minutes, everyone remained calm.
Then, just when Vargus brought down his target and was about to examine the battlefield, an arrow came from nowhere and embedded itself in his shoulder.
His body was sent flying back, but against all odds, he landed on his feet and roared, slamming his large hammer against the arrow. It shattered in half, and Vargus’ red eyes glowed.

A deep icy aura exploded from his body, and his long black hair billowed behind him, causing the space around him to freeze. Veins bulged on his arms as the armour around him turned jagged, metallic, black and red.

Already, he stood 7’3" tall. However, he now looked 8’3" tall, with a presence so overwhelming that if he had unleashed it before, perhaps Eryndor wouldn’t have needed to unleash his Hell Summoner class.
"Worms, why hide if you have come here to die?"
Nobody responded, but the next second, they were forced to reveal themselves when a deadly sword arc came out of nowhere, arriving before them.
Nine were quick to act; however, two found themselves at the mercy of Uncle Drew’s deadly attack, one that revealed where he had gone after cutting off the tail of the Sand Centipede.
"Since you have come to die, then die."
His body exploded with sword energy, and at once, the legendary Kael Duskbane was revealed, his presence imposing and commanding.

This was simply because he felt more true to himself in that form.

chapters.title: Chapter 1722: Soul Temple Agents
paragraphs: While the Sand Centipede truly snuck up on the Night Riders, they had long sensed the Soul Temple agents, so they were ever vigilant even during the battle with the Sand Centipede.
They sensed them a few minutes after killing the Shadowtail Scorpion, and when they left for the Worm Desert, the agents started following them.
So, even long before they faced off against the Sand Centipede, Uncle Drew and his team had already made plans on how to deal with them.
Thankfully, while the appearance of the Sand Centipede was unexpected, it also gave them a chance to eliminate the threat, handing over their heads before heading deeper into the Worm Desert.

So, the moment the chaos reached its peak and the entire battlefield descended into turmoil, Uncle Drew slipped away and positioned himself where he would have the highest chance of killing some of them.
Eleven Soul Temple agents had come after them: three Demigods and eight Immortal Lords.
However, while they were much weaker than the Demigod-level Sand Centipede, they were humans, and humans were crafty. So Uncle Drew timed it perfectly, killing two with a single attack.
The moment the remaining nine were forced into the open, Vargus was upon them, his body radiating a power that none of the Soul Temple agents had expected.
"Eat my hammer!"
His voice boomed, and like a mountain crashing from the heavens, a colossal hammer, sizzling with intense heat, appeared above the Soul Temple agents.
"Scatter!" one of the Demigods among them commanded. Then he punched forward, meeting the hammer head-on.
However, he underestimated the power behind the attack.
BOOM!
The devastating explosion rocked the ground, and a deep crater formed as the Demigod crashed into it. His hand shattered, and the grin on his face disappeared, replaced by a pale expression.
"Now die!"
Vargus didn’t even blink as he descended on the Demigod once again. This time, the Soul Temple agent knew he could not overpower Vargus, so he unleashed a technique.
"Tendrils of Damnation!"
Thousands of tendrils exploded from the ground, each stabbing toward Vargus, who sensed the overwhelming soul power hidden within every single one.
Even more shocking, all the tendrils converged on him without a single one missing its target.
"Blade of Darkness."
Before they could reach Vargus, however, Nara appeared and unleashed a deadly sword technique that severed every tendril. This gave Vargus the opening to hammer the poor bastard once more.
But killing a human Demigod was not that simple, especially one proficient in the art of the soul.
The man clapped his hands together, and thousands of souls appeared around him, each howling like wolves. However, upon closer inspection, one would realize they were not howling but screaming.
"How insidious," Vargus muttered as he teleported away.
He knew landing that attack on the Demigod would indeed damage the bastard. However, the resulting backlash from the souls would also severely injure him.
The odds made it clear: he could not afford to get hurt when they hadn’t even reached their destination yet. Besides, Kent had already warned them to be cautious while they were out here.
So he retreated, and Lene took his place.
She didn’t possess brute strength, nor did she specialize in wide-area attacks. So the moment she appeared, her spear trembled.
She unleashed a beam of energy from her spear, forcing the Soul Temple Demigod to abandon his insidious attack and erect a shield.
BOOOM!
He was sent flying backward. Seizing the opportunity, Lene closed the distance and engaged him in close combat. Uncle Drew had already taken on one of the Demigods, while Vargus was battling another.

Meanwhile, Nara, Eryndor, and Saden had taken on the six remaining Immortal Lords. This time, despite being realms below the six Immortal Lords, a clear difference could be seen because they were finally using their true strength.
Nara moved with a speed far beyond what an Immortal King was supposed to possess.
Meanwhile, with his four Hell Demons already keeping the Sand Centipede occupied, Eryndor fully committed himself to his secondary class, the Combat Mage.
He seamlessly combined powerful spells with deadly close-range attacks, wielding both his Ice and Flame elements with devastating precision.
As for Saden, she was like a shadow.
She appeared only long enough to fire an arrow, then vanished just before her opponent could retaliate.

A True Immortal holding off two Immortal Lords was not something that usually happened. However, as things stood, she was doing an exceptional job, and that alone was more than enough to demonstrate the caliber of warrior she was.
Uncle Drew was also displaying incredible mastery.

His swords moved like flowing air, never once missing their mark. Unfortunately for his opponent, who was also a swordsman, he had encountered someone whose understanding of combat existed on an entirely different level of madness.
Uncle Drew didn’t make mistakes, and every strike was aimed to kill. So with every swing of his swords, the poor Demigod found himself being pushed closer and closer to death’s door.

And he wasn’t the only one being pushed toward certain death. Despite their extensive battle experience, it was now clear to them that there were superior teams. Yet despite it all, none of the Soul Temple agents panicked.
Instead, their eyes flashed with madness. To them, this was just one of the many deadly battles they had fought in this Dead World. They possessed an affinity for death, and so they did not fear it.

After all, everyone who cultivated the power of death, or merely possessed an affinity for it, became stronger the closer they came to death’s door. So, although they were being pushed back, they weren’t afraid of death, at least not yet.

It was unfortunate that two of their own had died before the battle had even truly begun. However, now that they were here, the Night Riders, who in their eyes viewed them as nothing more than bugs, would soon witness the true power of the Soul Temple.
Then again, they had no idea they were fighting beings who had once come close to destroying the Soul Temple.
Just as the battle reached a critical moment, the six Immortal Lords suddenly abandoned their opponents and retreated toward the three Demigods.
"What are they planning?" Nara shouted, her voice carrying a hint of unease.
The moment those words left her mouth, the nine remaining Soul Temple agents formed a strange formation, their soul powers instantly resonating with one another.
An oppressive pressure spread across the battlefield.
Suddenly, the souls surrounding the Demigod who had been fighting Lene let out ear-piercing screams as they shot toward the formation, merging with the other agents.
The auras of the nine rapidly climbed, causing the air around them to become saturated with dense soul energy.
"What are they doing?" Lene muttered, narrowing her eyes.
"They’re merging their soul power," Uncle Drew replied calmly, his gaze fixed on the formation. "Don’t let them complete it."
The Night Riders moved almost simultaneously.
Eryndor was the first to attack.
"Hellfire Glacier!"
A sea of icy flames surged forward, freezing and burning everything in its path.
At the same time, Saden unleashed a barrage of deadly arrows while Nara launched an attack that manifested thousands of swords.
Lene also manifested a colossal spear and hurled it toward the formation, while a gigantic hammer followed immediately after. The final attack came from Uncle Drew.
Trails of flames erupted from his swords as his slashes crashed into the formation.
BOOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 1723: Nightblade
paragraphs: BOOOOOOM!
The battlefield disappeared beneath an ocean of explosions.
Flames, ice, sword qi, spear light, shadows, and soul energy collided violently, tearing the surrounding desert apart.
The shockwave spread for dozens of kilometers, reducing towering sand dunes to clouds of dust.
Even the distant Sand Centipede paused for a brief moment, instinctively turning toward the terrifying clash before resuming its battle against the four Hell Demons.
But before it could make sense of what had happened, the Hell Demons were already upon it once more, their deadly attacks raining down relentlessly.
As the dust slowly settled, Uncle Drew narrowed his eyes.
"They’re still alive."
His words had barely fallen when an enormous pillar of black soul energy erupted into the sky, carrying with it a pressure several times stronger than before.
However, a smile appeared on his face when he sensed something else hidden within the storm.
"True Death Qi," he said with a smile.
The rest of his teammates smiled as well, all of them turning to look at Nara.
"Kindly do us the honors, Nightblade," Uncle Drew said.
Nara nodded. She extended her hand, and a black sword appeared in her firm grip, making her a dual wielder.

In truth, aside from Uncle Drew, there were other dual wielders among the Night Riders. However, the greatest of them was Uncle Drew himself. That said, Nara, who mostly went by the name Nightblade, was a special case.
Aside from her Darkness and Lightning Affinity, she possessed two affinities that came with her Ancient Wraith Bloodline.

One was Hellflame, which was natural to all Night Riders, while the second was Death, an affinity she rarely used. Every Night Rider had an affinity for death, but hers was rooted far deeper than the others’.
She could harness Death Qi far more effectively than her comrades. In the past, her left sword, the one she wielded most often, had been forged from True Death Qi itself.

This meant that whenever she chose to fight using her death abilities, that sword became her greatest weapon. It made her exceptionally dangerous, especially whenever she was near a source of True Death Qi.
Today, as the Soul Temple agents harnessed their true death abilities, Nara and her friends already knew the battle was over.
Nara smiled and moved, appearing within the raging soul storm.
"Gentlemen, let’s dance."
She moved as though she were made of wind and appeared behind one of the Immortal Lords.
"Watch out!" one of the three Demigods shouted.
However, before the Immortal Lord could make any attempt to dodge, it was already too late.
His head flew into the air before crashing onto the ground with a dull thud.
Even before the severed head landed, Nara was already standing before the next Immortal Lord, her sword buried through his chest.
One of the Demigods immediately seized the opportunity to close in on her.
However, a grin curled at the corner of Nara’s lips as their gazes met.
"Death’s Gaze."
To the rest of the Soul Temple agents, only a faint purple light flashed across Nara’s eyes.
However, to the Demigod at the receiving end, his consciousness was instantly dragged into a world devoid of light.
Darkness stretched endlessly in every direction.
Just as he was about to wonder where he was, a colossal purple eye slowly opened before him.
It was the last thing he ever saw.
Everything returned to darkness.
Outside, blood poured from his nose, mouth, eyes, and ears.
Then he collapsed onto the ground.
That was the end of him.
Nara capitalized on the shock, eliminating two more Immortal Lords in rapid succession, leaving behind only two Immortal Lords and two Demigods.
"RUN!"
One of the Demigods shouted, and the four of them scattered in different directions.
However, they had only run a short distance before they came face to face with four deadly demons.

Just as Nara had taken advantage of their momentary shock to the Soul Temple Agents and killed two of them, the Four Hell Demons also exploited the shockwave’s effect to their advantage and swiftly ended their respective battles.
Just when the last Sand Centipede died, Uncle Drew told Eryndor to give them a command, causing them to move and stop in four different directions.
It was as if Uncle Drew knew what would happen, so he had planned ahead for them.
Now, Thrakos, Zandros, Kha’zixarath, and Xuanli blocked the paths of the four Soul Temple Agents who had tried to flee.
"You wouldn’t dare kill all of us," one of the Demigods shouted. "Aren’t you afraid of the Soul Temple’s retaliation?"
Thrakos grinned, his broadswords oozing deadly Blood Qi. "And who said we aren’t doing this so they would come after us?"
"True. The Last time, if not because the Dark Creatures interrupted us, we would have reduced your pitiful cult into a pile of bones," Zandros added, a grin forming at the corner of his lips.
They had been with the Night Riders when they attacked the Soul Temple back during the Dark Era, so they knew exactly what they were talking about.
"It is sad that we are now reduced to Demigods because of our master’s laziness in not wanting to grow stronger, faster.
But if I still had my true cultivation, I would have declared war on your Soul Temple tomorrow," Xuanli sneered, not minding that she had just called Eryndor lazy.
She truly meant what she said.
This made the Soul Temple Agents tremble, knowing they were cooked.
One of them retrieved a talisman and was about to activate it when his head fell off his body. Nara caught the severed head by the hair and threw it at one of the Immortal Lords.
He reached out to catch it, but what greeted him was the cold edge of Nara’s black blades. He was split cleanly in half.

The remaining Demigod tapped into his core and was about to ignite it when a large claw belonging to a lion-like beast coated in metallic carapace slammed into him, sending him crashing to the ground.
Before he could get back up, an arrow pierced his head, and that was the end of him. The last Immortal Lord was turned into meat paste by Vargus.

The last thing they wanted was for one of them to escape and report to the rest of the agents. While their deaths would be noticed and investigated soon, by the time anyone reached the battlefield, Uncle Drew and his team would long be gone.
"Let’s leave this place before they come looking for us," Uncle Drew said, and they all nodded.
Eryndor sent his Hell Demons away, and they vanished, leaving the devastated battlefield behind. They now had to cross the Worm Desert and the Howling Mountains before reaching the Black Fire Domain.
It would take them a couple of weeks, but at least they now had a head start.
Three days after they left, another team of eleven Soul Temple Agents arrived at the scene where the battle between the first team and the Night Riders had taken place.
Seeing the bodies of their comrades, their blood boiled with fury.
"Follow them," their leader, a Demigod woman, commanded.
Without hesitation, they departed in pursuit of Uncle Drew and his team.
Of course, if only they had known that, over the past three days, Uncle Drew and his team had grown much stronger, they would have rethought this entire plan of going after them.

In the past, her left sword, the one she wielded most often, had been forged from True Death Qi itself.
This meant that whenever she chose to fight using her death abilities, that sword became her greatest weapon.
It made her exceptionally dangerous, especially whenever she was near a source of True Death Qi.

She moved as though she were made of wind and appeared behind one of the Immortal Lords.

His head flew into the air before crashing onto the ground with a dull thud.
Even before the severed head landed, Nara was already standing before the next Immortal Lord, her sword buried through his chest.
One of the Demigods immediately seized the opportunity to close in on her.
However, a grin curled at the corner of Nara’s lips as their gazes met.
"Death’s Gaze."
To the rest of the Soul Temple agents, only a faint purple light flashed across Nara’s eyes.
However, to the Demigod at the receiving end, his consciousness was instantly dragged into a world devoid of light.
Darkness stretched endlessly in every direction.
Just as he was about to wonder where he was, a colossal purple eye slowly opened before him.
It was the last thing he ever saw.
Everything returned to darkness.
Outside, blood poured from his nose, mouth, eyes, and ears.
Then he collapsed onto the ground.
That was the end of him.
Nara capitalized on the shock, eliminating two more Immortal Lords in rapid succession, leaving behind only two Immortal Lords and two Demigods.

One of the Demigods shouted, and the four of them scattered in different directions.
However, they had only run a short distance before they came face to face with four deadly demons.

Just when the last Sand Centipede died, Uncle Drew told Eryndor to give them a command, causing them to move and stop in four different directions.
It was as if Uncle Drew knew what would happen, so he had planned ahead for them.

"Aren’t you afraid of the Soul Temple’s retaliation?"
Thrakos grinned, his broadswords oozing deadly Blood Qi.
"And who said we aren’t doing this so they would come after us?"
"True.

They had been with the Night Riders when they attacked the Soul Temple back during the Dark Era, so they knew exactly what they were talking about.

But if I still had my true cultivation, I would have declared war on your Soul Temple tomorrow," Xuanli sneered, not minding that she had just called Eryndor lazy.
She truly meant what she said.
This made the Soul Temple Agents tremble, knowing they were cooked.
One of them retrieved a talisman and was about to activate it when his head fell off his body.
Nara caught the severed head by the hair and threw it at one of the Immortal Lords.

He was split cleanly in half.

paragraphs: Lady Wu scanned the entire auction hall before she began to speak...

"Welcome, everyone, to this year’s Brown Maple Mega Auction. I know it has been 10,000 years since we last gathered like this to bid on some of the most valuable treasures collected over the last 10,000 years.
It had been a great experience for all of us. The last Mega Auction witnessed the sale of legendary weapons, armour, artefacts, and all kinds of mind-bending treasures.
However, rest assured that this time around, we will be auctioning even more invaluable treasures, some collected millions of years ago by Supremes and Celestials."
Many gasped upon hearing where some of the treasures had come from.
They knew Lady Wu had extensive reach and countless connections, so they didn’t doubt her words. This meant she truly possessed treasures once owned by such powerful figures.

"Just like 10,000 years ago, only twenty-five items will be auctioned today, and every single one of them is extraordinarily valuable. So I urge everyone to give it your all because, as I always say, there won’t be a second chance for regret."
She smiled, and determination immediately filled many eyes.

"However, before we begin, I would like to announce that we have in our midst the recently ascended Pill God Flura, who, despite still being at the Immortal Cultivation stage, has become a Pill God and had her name inscribed upon the Pill Dao Tablet."

Pill God Flura’s projection appeared in the air, causing many to clap and cheer. It was every alchemist’s dream to establish connections with Pill Gods, so learning that one of them was present made everyone excited.
"We also have with us Lady Veth of the Dream Pill Emporium."
Applause once again filled the auction hall.

Just like Pill God Flura, those seeking God Pills knew that getting closer to Lady Veth would greatly increase their chances. She might not possess a network as extensive as Lady Wu’s, but she had several Pill Gods practically on speed dial.
Aside from that, it was common knowledge that she and Pill God Flura were as close as sisters. Now that Flura had become a Pill God, Veth’s own status had naturally risen alongside hers.
Lady Wu continued introducing several distinguished guests. After five minutes, she returned to the matter at hand.

"As you all know, the same rules still apply," her voice echoed throughout the auction hall, reaching every corner. "In here, your overwhelming authority—whether you are a Demigod, God, or even a Supreme—means nothing. Within these walls, only wealth speaks.
No one is allowed to threaten another bidder using their background or status. Nor will anyone attempt to manipulate the auction for personal gain.

Doing so will result in a permanent ban from every Brown Maple Auction House across the universe. Follow these rules, and we will all have a wonderful time. Break them, and don’t say I didn’t warn you.

Lastly, all bids must be made using Spirit Stones. However, payment may be made with God Coins, Supreme Crystals, or Celestial Jade. You may either pay immediately after winning a bid and receive your item at once or settle your payment after the auction concludes, before collecting your winnings."
The rules and additional information were already familiar to most of the attendees, but announcing them remained a necessary part of every Mega Auction.
Now that the formalities were complete, the first item was brought onto the stage.
It was a small map fragment sealed inside a thick glass chamber powerful enough to block every known form of appraisal.
"With the announcements concluded, allow me to officially begin the 21st Brown Maple Mega Auction with our first item."
She swept her gaze across the crowd one last time before continuing.
"Enclosed within this glass chamber is a map fragment recovered by a powerful God two million years ago from an ancient ruin believed to be the tomb of a legendary explorer from the Chaos Era.

According to the item’s owner, this map reveals the location of an extraordinary treasure known as the Grand Mage Key, an artefact once wielded by the legendary Three-Star Fire Mage during the Chaos Era."
Gasps spread across the auction hall, but Lady Wu wasn’t done.

"According to the owner, this map will prove its true value when the Chaos Rift opens a hundred years from now. After all, this map will lead to the Grand Mage Key, a treasure that even Celestials would kill for."

Everyone knew she wasn’t exaggerating. Celestials would indeed kill for such a treasure simply because of who it once belonged to. The Grand Mage Key was said to contain three legendary 100-layered flame spells, each created by the Three-Star Fire Mage during the Chaos Era.
Kent, seated comfortably in the embrace of two beautiful women, smiled.
"Looks like that old fogey really died during the Chaos Era, huh?" A smile formed on his face, causing Veth and Flura to wonder why he seemed so pleased.

If only they knew that one of the Divine Beast Tamers’ greatest rivals had been the Three-Star Fire Mage. The two had fought countless times before, eventually joining forces against the Chaos Beasts.

However, during one of those decisive battles, the Three-Star Fire Mage betrayed the Divine Beast Tamer and deserted the battlefield, leading to the deaths of many great warriors, most of whom belonged to the Divine Beast Tamer’s beast legion.
Had it not been for the Divine Beast Tamer’s Thirteen Divine Wonder Beasts, they would have lost that battle to the Chaos Beasts.
"Serves him right," Kent muttered, his mood improving even further.
"The starting price is set at 10 billion High-Grade Spirit Stones. Each subsequent bid must increase by at least 100 million High-Grade Spirit Stones."
She paused for a brief moment before announcing,
"Begin."
"15 billion!"
The first bid immediately increased the price by 5 billion, a clear sign that everyone wanted the map fragment.
"20 billion!"
"30 billion!"
"60 billion!"
The price quickly reached 60 billion, yet not even a minute had passed since the bidding war began.
"Aren’t you going to bid for it?" Veth asked Kent, knowing he intended to enter the Chaos Rift when it opened. Obtaining the map would surely give him a significant advantage.
To her surprise, Kent smirked.
"I don’t need a map to navigate the Chaos Era. I know that era like the back of my hand."
The two women narrowed their eyes but remained silent. Their sisters had already briefed them on the monstrous nature of the man they loved, so they recognised this as one of those moments.
"Then, can you tell us more about this Three-Star Fire Mage?" Flura asked.
Kent smirked once more.
"He was a scum, a coward, and a traitor. I don’t know what people think of him these days, but the bastard I knew was a coward who abandoned his comrades when they needed him the most."
Kent clenched his fist and muttered coldly,
"I don’t know whether he’s dead or alive. If it’s the former, then good riddance. But if he’s still alive, then one day, when I find him, I’ll make sure he dies screaming."

Veth and Pill God Flura could clearly see how deeply Kent hated the Three-Star Fire Mage. Whatever that man had done to earn such hatred had left an unforgettable scar, and if he were still alive, it would one day become his greatest calamity.
The price of the map fragment continued to climb. Before long, it had surpassed 100 billion High-Grade Spirit Stones, yet the bidding war had only just begun.

"With the announcements concluded, allow me to officially begin the 21st Brown Maple Mega Auction with our first item."
She swept her gaze across the crowd one last time before continuing.
"Enclosed within this glass chamber is a map fragment recovered by a powerful God two million years ago from an ancient ruin believed to be the tomb of a legendary explorer from the Chaos Era.

According to the item’s owner, this map reveals the location of an extraordinary treasure known as the Grand Mage Key, an artefact once wielded by the legendary Three-Star Fire Mage during the Chaos Era."
Gasps spread across the auction hall, but Lady Wu wasn’t done.
"According to the owner, this map will prove its true value when the Chaos Rift opens a hundred years from now.
After all, this map will lead to the Grand Mage Key, a treasure that even Celestials would kill for."
Everyone knew she wasn’t exaggerating.
Celestials would indeed kill for such a treasure simply because of who it once belonged to.
The Grand Mage Key was said to contain three legendary 100-layered flame spells, each created by the Three-Star Fire Mage during the Chaos Era.
Kent, seated comfortably in the embrace of two beautiful women, smiled.
"Looks like that old fogey really died during the Chaos Era, huh?" A smile formed on his face, causing Veth and Flura to wonder why he seemed so pleased.
If only they knew that one of the Divine Beast Tamers’ greatest rivals had been the Three-Star Fire Mage.
The two had fought countless times before, eventually joining forces against the Chaos Beasts.

However, during one of those decisive battles, the Three-Star Fire Mage betrayed the Divine Beast Tamer and deserted the battlefield, leading to the deaths of many great warriors, most of whom belonged to the Divine Beast Tamer’s beast legion.
Had it not been for the Divine Beast Tamer’s Thirteen Divine Wonder Beasts, they would have lost that battle to the Chaos Beasts.
"Serves him right," Kent muttered, his mood improving even further.
"The starting price is set at 10 billion High-Grade Spirit Stones.
Each subsequent bid must increase by at least 100 million High-Grade Spirit Stones."
She paused for a brief moment before announcing,
"Begin."
"15 billion!"
The first bid immediately increased the price by 5 billion, a clear sign that everyone wanted the map fragment.
"20 billion!"
"30 billion!"
"60 billion!"
The price quickly reached 60 billion, yet not even a minute had passed since the bidding war began.
"Aren’t you going to bid for it?" Veth asked Kent, knowing he intended to enter the Chaos Rift when it opened.
Obtaining the map would surely give him a significant advantage.
To her surprise, Kent smirked.
"I don’t need a map to navigate the Chaos Era.
I know that era like the back of my hand."
The two women narrowed their eyes but remained silent.
Their sisters had already briefed them on the monstrous nature of the man they loved, so they recognised this as one of those moments.
"Then, can you tell us more about this Three-Star Fire Mage?" Flura asked.
Kent smirked once more.
"He was a scum, a coward, and a traitor.
I don’t know what people think of him these days, but the bastard I knew was a coward who abandoned his comrades when they needed him the most."
Kent clenched his fist and muttered coldly,
"I don’t know whether he’s dead or alive.
If it’s the former, then good riddance.
But if he’s still alive, then one day, when I find him, I’ll make sure he dies screaming."
Veth and Pill God Flura could clearly see how deeply Kent hated the Three-Star Fire Mage.
Whatever that man had done to earn such hatred had left an unforgettable scar, and if he were still alive, it would one day become his greatest calamity.
The price of the map fragment continued to climb.
Before long, it had surpassed 100 billion High-Grade Spirit Stones, yet the bidding war had only just begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 1733: Heaven’s Breath Crystal
paragraphs: "300 Billion,"
"340 Billion."

The price of the map fragment had already risen so high that many people started to drop out. After all, the chance to get their hands on the map, which would lead them to a great treasure, would also deprive them of the chance to win treasures available at the auction.
In their opinion, it was always better to fight for what was right in front of them than to hope for something that was only assumed to exist.
What if, after everything, the map leads them to a dead end?
The moment remained tense for a few minutes before the final bid of 600 billion was placed by a man inside VIP Room 45.
"Sold to the gentleman in VIP Room 45!"

"Yes!" the man shouted, feeling delighted to have secured such a priceless treasure. If given the chance, he would ensure that only his people got their hands on the Grand Mage Key when the Chaos Rift opened.
Obtaining such a treasure would push his power to a whole different level.
If only he knew that people had already started planning how to get their hands on the map the moment the auction ended. Inside the auction house, he was safe.
Once he stepped outside, however, people could do whatever they wanted to him, and he would have his own strength to defend himself.
"Would this gentleman like to pay now and collect his prize, or would you prefer to wait until the auction is over?" Lady Wu asked, and the man immediately replied,
"I will pay now."
"Great. Then the item will be delivered to your room shortly." The map was carried away by a maid, and the next item was brought onto the stage by two maids.
Inside the glass chamber was a pentagonal crystal featuring three colours: blue, white, and gold.
It was suspended in midair inside the glass chamber, which was at least as tall as a teenage human, making it appear even more regal and mysterious.
After it was set down, everyone quieted down to listen to what Lady Wu had to say about it.
Of course, the knowledgeable ones like Kent had already determined the nature of the crystal and had already made up their minds to fight for it.

"This is the Heaven’s Breath Crystal, a crystal formed from the very breath of the heavens. It is said to contain a strand of the Heavens’ Dao, as well as mysterious knowledge that leads to a place within the Primordial Chaos housing a very powerful treasure.
However, this knowledge is locked behind a very powerful seal, one that even Celestials have failed to break. But that is only a minor setback when one focuses on the Dao hidden within it.
Simply cultivating beside it will enhance your understanding of the laws and even improve your Dao, as long as you can comprehend it.

Aside from that, absorbing even a small chunk of it will enhance all your attributes, accelerate your cultivation, cleanse your soul and karma, aid in refining pills and treasures, and lastly, allow you to absorb Chaos Energy.
Even if the seal remains unbreakable, its other uses are boundless."
Many nodded at Lady Wu’s words, knowing full well that those benefits alone were enough to drive people into a frenzy. The crystal was large enough to refine at least four treasures or a dozen pills.
"The bidding starts at 150 billion, and each increase must be at least 50 billion."
Everyone shifted to the edge of their seats and waited for her to begin the bidding. The moment she gave the go-ahead, everyone scrambled.
"300 Billion!"
The price instantly doubled, a clear sign that the battle is on.
"400 Billion!"
"500 Billion!"
Kent changed his posture, his gaze locked onto the Heaven’s Breath Crystal. Inwardly, he held a smile on his face as he stared at the message the Tower had displayed before him.
[Master, this crystal can be used to upgrade Sir Veydris and the other Lost Knights.]
’Finally,’ Kent smiled inwardly and asked a question, ’How many of them can be upgraded using this Heaven’s Breath Crystal?’

[Because only Sir Veydris has been upgraded once, if this crystal is used well, we can upgrade him to the True Immortal Realm, while the rest will be upgraded to the Heavenly Ascension Stage. There is even a chance Sir Veydris will awaken some innate talents and be able to speak or take on his humanoid form.]
’That is good enough. I am sure that by the end of this auction, we will get other minerals like this that can help us make them strong enough.’
[That is possible.]
’In that case, do we have enough money to go all out?’
[Yes. The Master shouldn’t worry about his finances right now. We have more than enough to win this bid.]
Kent nodded and turned his attention back to the auction proceedings, where the bid had already reached 900 billion. Soon, the next two bids pushed it to a trillion.
"1.2 trillion," someone placed a bid, and many quieted down. However, Kent smiled and added his bid.
"1.5 trillion."
More people quieted down, but a few others remained, some raising it by a few billion while others with deep pockets raised it by even more.
Kent remained calm, paying attention to the repeated voices and to those who, like him, had only just started bidding.
"2 trillion," the bid rose again, and Kent immediately pushed it further.
"2.2 trillion."
"2.4 trillion," a voice that had just joined the bidding raised the price again. However, Kent remained unfazed and raised it as well.
"2.7 trillion."
"3 trillion."

Veth and Flura furrowed their brows upon hearing a new voice join the bidding. Kent also smiled and tried to use his Omniscient Jade Eyes to look through the formation. However, he saw that something external was blocking him from doing so.
Regardless, he knew he had to man up, so he took the bid to another level.
"3.7 trillion."
He wasn’t even done when the person raised the bid again.
"4 trillion."
"4.5 trillion."
"5 trillion."

"5.5 trillion," Kent raised it further, causing everyone inside the auction house to start murmuring. The person Kent was competing against was someone many recognised by her voice and knew came from the Blacksmith Association.
In fact, she was one of the few Platinum Badge Immortal Blacksmiths in the Eastern Region, Lady Khronisia. She was highly respected, and many wished to be in her good books.
In fact, she was set to take her first Blacksmith God Trial, and if she passed, she would become a Blacksmith God.
So while the auction stated that one could not use one’s name or position to intimidate others, many still paid attention to certain people and tried their best not to offend them.
Kent clearly didn’t care about that. But even if he did, he wouldn’t pass up the chance to upgrade his 14 Lost Knights, one of his legions.

The 14 Lost Knights were his smallest yet most dangerous legion. In the past, they fought to protect the innocent, giving their lives to ensure that every last soul under their care remained safe and sound.
They had lived during the Divine Era.
Back then, his incarnation, Lord Genesis, found the 14 knights. They were at the brink of death when he found them. In fact, dozens of them had already died, and only 14 remained.

He saved them and helped them return to their peak. Later, he gave each of them an inheritance meant for knights. During the last War of Sanguine, they all perished, but not before saving every last one of the Lost Children of the Mother.
Jest died a few years after that, but he was proud of every last one of them for their bravery.
He wouldn’t pass up the chance to bring them back to life... not even for someone as respected and powerful as Lady Khronisia.
"6 trillion..."

chapters.title: Chapter 1734: Heated Bidding War
paragraphs: When the price was raised to 6 trillion, everyone in the hall began to murmur, some simply because they could.
The rules were there, but when the offence was not directed at anyone, no harm was caused.
"I never knew a day would come when someone wouldn’t give face to the mighty Blacksmith Association," someone said, making sure Kent became aware of the person he was bidding against.
"I know, right? To think there is someone alive with that many balls. Makes me wonder who they are, though," another person joined in.
"Maybe they are not from this region, so they don’t know how things are done over here."
"It seems so. But again, he should give face to a senior. While the Heaven’s Breath Crystal is one of a kind, letting his ego get in the way of greatness is something he shouldn’t entertain."
Kent heard everything they were saying, but he didn’t even bother to consider offering the Heaven’s Breath Crystal to the person he was bidding against.
Slowly, the price reached 10 trillion, and for the first time, the lady bidding against Kent didn’t raise the price. Instead, a calm and almost soothing voice came from VIP room 69...

"It appears today is not the day I, Khronisia, am destined to have such a priceless treasure," she said, letting a chuckle end her statement, which, from where Kent sat, sounded like a threat packaged in a bag of sweetness.
She mentioned her name to intimidate him. However, she clearly didn’t know she was the one who should be afraid.
The moment she said those words, everyone turned their heads toward VIP room 13 to hear Kent’s reply.

Initially, he didn’t want to reveal his identity. After all, he was here to surprise Lady Wu. However, he knew Lady Wu had already discovered his identity simply from how he behaved around Veth and Flura.
Since he had lost the element of surprise against her, he might as well use that surprise somewhere else.
Letting a small smile form on his face, he replied, "In that case, I, Kent Madson, would have to thank this senior for her generosity."
Eyes widened, and jaws dropped when they heard Kent introduce himself.
Inside VIP room 69, Lady Khronisia narrowed her eyes at VIP room 13. For a moment, she had doubt, but then she recognised where they were causing her to turn pale.
Clearly, she had become regretful that she had tried to outbid someone she had actively searched for months after Kent’s name appeared on the Ice Dao Tablet.
She was a very good and respected blacksmith. Because of this, she had access to many places and things that many others did not.

So when she learned someone had appeared on the Ice Dao Tablet, she first asked who. When she found out it was the legendary Kent Madson, so she tried to find him, not because she intended to suppress him, but because she needed his help.
It was well known that the only way to get on the Ice Dao Tablet or any elemental Dao Tablet was to comprehend a True Name of the element.
In all of the universe’s history, only 24 Ice cultivators had managed to do that, and all of them were legendary figures, so she couldn’t get to them easily.
However, Kent was within her realm, meaning getting to him was as simple as sending people to fetch him.

She needed his help in creating a masterpiece, one she intended to leave as her mark in the Immortal World before ascending. She needed his Ice element, one that possessed a True Name, for that masterpiece.
If she had known the person she was competing against was the same person whose help she needed, she wouldn’t have pressed on like that.
She looked at her palm and was about to slap herself when Kent spoke again...

"Sorry for pressing on, Senior, but I really needed Heaven’s Breath Crystal. However, learning that you are a blacksmith, I am willing to give you a chunk. I hope that makes up for my unruly behaviour."
Lady Khronisia was a bit stunned for a moment. She clearly never expected Kent to apologise. However, since he did, and to keep up her composure, she sighed and replied to him.
"No need to apologise, Kent Madson. The Heaven’s Breath Crystal is a heavenly treasure, so it is perfectly normal to bid for it. However, I do wonder what you intend to do with it.

As far as I know, you are a swordsman and an alchemist, so blacksmithing isn’t a field you dabble in. But even if you need it for alchemy, you wouldn’t be able to use it until you become a Pill God, so care to share with me what you intend to use it for?"

Kent smiled and replied, "Well, I dabble in many things, but you are right, I am no blacksmith. However, I know how to refine weapons." He paused for a moment, staring at the message before his vision...
[Notice: You have received a quest]
[Quest Name: Rescue Lady Khronisia]

[Description: On her way back from the auction, Lady Khronisia will be attacked, and she will die. Your mission is to make sure she makes it back home, and all threats around her are handled with precision.]
[Rewards: Heaven’s Breath Crystal and Red Obsidian Lightning Ore]

"However, let’s talk about what I will be using the Heaven’s Breath Crystal for over dinner after the auction. I would also love to pick your brain about something related to blacksmithing... that is, if you don’t mind."
"That would be great, Kent Madson."
"Great. Then we will have dinner after the auction."
Lady Wu, who was inwardly happy and even failed to contain her joy, sighed in relief when Kent and Lady Khronisia finally found a pleasant ending to their rivalry.
"The bid goes to the gentleman in VIP room 13," she said with a slight smile before asking, "Do you want to pay now or later?"
"I will handle it later," Kent replied, and the Heaven’s Breath Crystal was taken off the stage.
And just like that, the second item of the auction was sold for a staggering 10 trillion high-grade spirit stones. Compared to the first item, this one was several times more expensive.
And that was only natural because the Heaven’s Breath Crystal was far more valuable than the map fragment. So selling it for such a high price was only normal.

Of course, the price also reached that height because Kent and Lady Khronisia didn’t want to lose the bid to each other. If one of them had given up earlier, it might not have even reached that amount.
But the bidding had already ended, and now Kent owned the Heaven’s Breath Crystal, worth ten trillion high-grade spirit stones.
Even though it was overpriced, the reason behind this purchase was to upgrade the Lost Knights so they would finally be recognised by the Tower as one of its legions.
The 14 Lost Knights were special, and so even if he couldn’t bring all of them back just yet, bringing at least six back to life would do for now.
Veydris had already fallen behind the rest of his legions since he wasn’t even at the Heavenly Ascension Stage yet. So this item would come in handy.
After the Heaven’s Breath Crystal was sold, the next item was brought to the stage...
Kent only took a single glance at it, and he passed out, startling the two ladies beside him.

After the Heaven’s Breath Crystal was sold, the next item was brought to the stage...
Kent only took a single glance at it, and he passed out, startling the two ladies beside him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1735: Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith
paragraphs: CLANG
The first thing Kent heard when he woke up was the sound produced by metal striking metal.
He turned around and saw that he was in a place he couldn’t quite bring himself to describe.
The mountains around him were made of minerals many blacksmiths would kill to have even a chunk of. There were bones from legendary beasts, some of which had even gone extinct.
The rivers there were made of either water, ice, or flames. Yes, there was an ice river there. In the air, thousands—tens of thousands—of treasures hovered around.
More shocking still, this world felt like home, almost as if appearing there was the most important decision he had ever made.
Kent knew he had arrived in a world where one of his incarnations was waiting for him.
He had already met Chaos, Faceless, Jest, Ruthless Bandit, and Sanders. He had yet to meet Kevin Sage and the Divine Beast Tamer, but he knew he was about to meet yet another incarnation of himself.
CLANG

The sound of metal striking metal once again resounded across the space, drawing his attention toward the east. Without any hesitation, he took off, and in no time, he arrived at a valley where a large red building sat in the middle of a pool of lava.
Kent immediately sensed that getting close to the lava would mean his end. The pressure coming off it and the sheer amount of flame essence he felt were far beyond anything he had ever experienced.
It was as if his Nirvana Flames and Chaos Flame were children before it.
CLANG
Another metallic ring came from the building, followed by a booming voice.
"Are you just going to stand there or come meet me?"
Kent didn’t know where the courage came from, but the next second, he moved, and before he could stop himself, he was already standing in front of the building.

The door swung open, and he entered, ready to die the moment he stepped inside. However, what greeted him was the sight of a bare-chested man holding a large hammer with a red handle and a black head.

He was muscular, but not overly so. He stood a staggering 7’2" tall, with a wave of green hair cascading down his back. Because he was drenched in sweat and completely engrossed in his work, his hair clung to his skin, almost as if water had been poured over him.
Turning slightly, his green eyes met Kent’s, and for a moment, Kent felt like a lump of ore about to be thrown into a fire and shaped into a treasure.
The man smiled and set the hammer down, turning fully to face Kent. That was when Kent saw an X-shaped scar on his chest.
’A barbarian, huh?’ Kent said inwardly, a smile forming on his face. He was many beings in the past, after all.

He was a dragon, then a human (Jest and Ruthless Bandit), and then an Umbra-human (Darkborne, mostly called Shadow Demons). He went on to become an Elf (Divine Beast Tamer) and a half-elf in two lives (Kevin Sage and Sanders).
Now, it appeared he had once lived as a barbarian.
"Gosh, I hate tiny people," the man said, his voice booming across the room.
Kent smirked and replied, "You are just seven inches taller than me."
"That still makes you tiny," the man laughed and walked toward Kent with heavy steps. When he stood before him, he placed a hand on Kent’s shoulder and smiled.
"So, you are who we turned out to become, huh?"

Perhaps seeing the way the man was looking down at him, Kent’s ego couldn’t handle it, so he assumed his demi-dragon form, rising to 7’1". Still, he was an inch shorter, but that was better than seven inches.
The man laughed and tapped Kent on the shoulder more forcefully this time.
"Haha, I guess we haven’t lost our sense of humor." He let go and extended his hand, causing a wine bottle to fly toward him.
When he caught it, he took three gulps before handing it over to Kent, who also took three gulps, clearly in competition with himself.
"Better. I am now convinced we didn’t turn out to be losers after all," he laughed again and waved his hand, causing them to appear atop a mountain. Below them stretched a sea of lava.
"I was called many names and given many titles during my day. However, you can call me Kaelgorin Fjorge, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith."
Kent turned, looked at his past incarnation, and nodded.
"Good name and title. We were once known as the Primordial Chaos Dragon, Lord Genesis, Ruthless Bandit, Bone Lich Undead Emperor, Divine Beast Tamer, Grand Pill Celestial Kevin Sage, and many more."
Kaelgorin Fjorge laughed and tapped Kent on the shoulder again.
"Good titles. I guess we were badass, huh?"
Kent nodded and replied, "That we were, so don’t lower the bar, buddy."

"Rest assured, I had the most badass life among all of us. After all, have you ever met a barbarian who was kidnapped a few days after he was born, sent down to Hell to fight in the Damnation Arena, won his way to the top, killed the Hell Emperor, and ruled Hell for 10,000 years before taking an interest in forging?"
Kent looked at Kaelgorin Fjorge for a few seconds before he exploded into resounding laughter.
"That sounds like a dark and twisted fairy tale, but I am going to enjoy it."

"You will." Kaelgorin Fjorge laughed and added, "While that was merely 10% of our life, I am sure the trip down memory lane, starting with a devastating hellride, will make this visit worthwhile. And rest assured, not even a minute will pass on the outside by the time you leave."
"That is reassuring. I wouldn’t want to miss out on the dragon whip."
Kaelgorin Fjorge laughed again, making Kent wonder if he would also become this lively after absorbing his memories.

"The Nine Dragon Whip," Kaelgorin Fjorge muttered, smiling as he recalled one of his famous creations. "It was one of my masterpieces when I was a Blacksmith God. It is actually funny how that whip came about. Do you want to hear?"
"No, I would probably see it in the memories," Kent rejected the offer, but it didn’t go anywhere.
"I will tell you."

Kaelgorin Fjorge laughed and began, "One time, I was bored, so I decided to pop down to Hell and see how my pals were doing. One thing led to another, and we found ourselves in one of the Hell Calamity Caves, attacked by a horde of dragons.
The battle was so intense that when we managed to escape, some of my pals developed trauma toward that place. However, I reaped some benefits in the form of nine dragon souls.

When I returned to the land of the living, a very annoying, pesky blacksmith challenged me to a duel where we each had to create a God-grade living weapon, and the winner would strike the loser with their weapon.

I crafted the Nine Dragon Whip, obliterated that sucker’s soul, and later gifted it to an old flame of mine. She was one hot-headed vixen. I loved her so much." Kaelgorin Fjorge laughed out loud, clearly happy as he recalled such memories.
Kent stared at this brute for a few moments before smiling and shaking his head.
’Maybe Ruthless and Sanders aren’t the worst versions of me.’
