chapters.title: Chapter 1736: Devastating Life of a Barbarian Warrior
paragraphs: Kent remained stunned for a few minutes, simply watching his Blacksmith Incarnation laugh his heart out. He had no idea he would meet one of his incarnations at the auction.
However, as things stood now, the appearance of the Nine Dragon Whip had triggered some of his memories, and soon, the rest would return to him.

In fact, Kent can already sense that this auction has fate’s fingerprint all over it. First was the Heaven’s Breath Crystal, which he needed to upgrade the 14 Lost Knights, and now, this Nine Dragon Whip, which had triggered his memories.
He wondered what else awaited him.
He smiled, knowing he would be sent on another devastating journey, one in which he would relive the life of a past incarnation to reclaim the memories that would one day shape his future once again.

He only hoped the tower had acted by sending him inside the sword tower to mask the passage of time even more. Then again, Kaelgorin Fjorge had assured him that not a single day would pass outside, so he had nothing to worry about.
"You know what? Why don’t you send me on my way? As it happens, I was in the middle of something before you called me over," Kent said, and Kaelgorin Fjorge nodded.
"Very well."
He stamped hard on the ground, and it cracked open, revealing a door.
"Walk through, and good luck."
Kent accepted Fjorge’s handshake before walking toward the gate. With one easy step, he passed through it.
The next second, he found himself as a baby...

The cry of a baby caused thousands of barbarian warriors to take up arms and become alert. Today was the last day of the siege, and out of over forty million people, only four hundred thousand remained.
The Hell Crusaders had attacked their small planet and either slaughtered its people or dragged them down to Hell under the orders of the Hell Emperor.

After the previous Hell Emperor died in the battle against the Chaos Beast Race, his successor had turned Hell upside down. For years, he made sure the land of the living felt his wrath simply because he believed they were responsible for his father’s death.
Today, the Barbarian King welcomed his lastborn son, one he loved but regretted siring, given the desperate situation they were in. It was no world for a child to be born into.
Yet the moment the child’s cries echoed through the air, every warrior knew they had to fight for him.
The Barbarian King, a man with pure green hair and green eyes, held his son in his arms with a tired yet warm smile on his face.
"My son, you shall be known as Kaelgorin Fjorge, a Barbarian Prince and a great warrior who will one day liberate our people from the clutches of our enemies."
He pulled out a dagger and cut a wound across the baby’s chest, drawing blood. Then he pressed his thumb against the child’s forehead, and the wound healed, leaving behind a scar.
Turning slightly, he handed the child to his mother before running off to the battlefield. He was the strongest warrior among them, so he had to stand at the front lines.
The woman held Fjorge in her arms for a few minutes, tears rolling down her face.
"You will grow up, Fjorge. You will become a great warrior, just like your father."
After saying that, she planted a kiss on his forehead and handed him to three maids.
"Take him away and never look back. Protect him with your lives, even if it costs you everything."
The three women nodded and took off, running as fast as their legs could carry them.
Ten days later, the three barbarian women lay dead.
A baby barbarian was held by one leg, dangling in the air as a Hell demon with a skull-like face swung him from side to side.
"So young and tiny, yet full of life," the Hell demon muttered, pinching Fjorge’s nose. "You will make a fine warrior for the arena."
He turned to look at his men.
"We’re taking the little barbarian with us."

Weeks later, they passed through the gates of Hell and entered Bone City, one of the great cities within the Bone Hell Layer. The first thing the Hell demons did was sell Fjorge to a merchant who specialized in purchasing children destined to become arena warriors.
Though Fjorge was only a baby, they knew he would one day grow into a fearsome warrior. Seeing his potential, the merchant bought him and took him to a brothel, where he would be raised.
Twelve years passed in the blink of an eye.

Inside an arena littered with the battered corpses of Hell demon beasts, a twelve-year-old barbarian who looked more like a Hell demon than a barbarian stood amidst the carnage, a massive hammer resting on his shoulder.
The boy was Fjorge, an underdog who had slowly begun to rise through the ranks of the Hell arenas.

He had not yet begun cultivating, yet his physical strength was already comparable to that of a Core Formation expert. Though only twelve years old, he stood 5’2" tall with a heavily muscular physique.
BANG!
A hammer slammed into the head of a Hell demon, causing it to explode. Blood and brain matter splattered across the arena floor and sprayed into the air.
Thunderous cheers erupted throughout the arena as tens of thousands of spectators chanted the name of the warrior who had delivered the devastating blow.
Fjorge rested his hammer on his shoulder, a faint smile curling at the corner of his lips as he waved with his free hand, completely ignoring the blood and brain matter covering his skin.
He was now seventeen years old and had already reached the Heavenly Ascension Stage. More impressively, he had begun hunting and killing immortals. No Immortal had survived against him yet.

Years continued to pass, and before long, Fjorge became an Immortal Lord at the age of twenty-five. Standing 6’9" tall, he possessed an overwhelming presence that radiated both bloodlust and killing intent.

By then, he had already dominated every lesser arena. Today, however, he had been invited to step into the legendary Damnation Arena, where Demigods, Gods, Supremes, and even Celestials fought to the death every single day.
Each match ended with only one survivor.
The mortality rate was terrifying, but when Fjorge received the invitation, he was overjoyed. After all, he had dreamed of setting foot in that arena ever since he was a child.
And he did.
Only, the moment he arrived, everything changed.
His life became an endless cycle of battle, slaughtering one opponent after another. Before long, his name spread throughout Hell, and with every victory, his strength continued to soar.

He became a Demigod at the age of thirty-five and ascended to Godhood by the age of seventy-five. Even before reaching those realms, however, he had slaughtered so many powerful opponents that even the Hell kings and queens began to take notice of him.
By the age of twelve thousand, he had reached the Supreme Realm. Long before that, however, he had already been hunting Supremes, making every one of them regret crossing paths with him.
After becoming a Supreme, he finally stepped away from the Damnation Arena briefly to pursue a different goal.
It was then that he discovered where he had truly come from... and who had torn him away from his family.

When he learned that the Hell Emperor was responsible, he embarked on a path of vengeance, one that left an ocean of blood in his wake. His fury engulfed the entirety of Hell, and his relentless campaign claimed the lives of millions.
At long last, after countless battles and immeasurable sacrifice, he slew the Hell Emperor.
Using the emperor’s blood, he cleansed himself of every trace of demonic stench before setting out to search for his parents.
His name was forever engraved upon the walls of the Damnation Arena, marking the end of a legend—a warrior who had turned every Damnation match into a spectacle no one dared to miss.
His parents had named him Kaelgorin Fjorge.
But throughout the Damnation Arena...
He was known only as the Blood Hammer King.

chapters.title: Chapter 1737: Devastating Life of a Barbarian Blacksmith
paragraphs: The first time Fjorge set foot in the land of the living, he arrived in the middle of an intense battle between humans and demons.
When the demons sensed the aura of a seasoned Supreme radiating from him, they erupted into cheers, believing he had come to fight on their side.

Fjorge was indeed an imposing and, at the same time, terrifying figure. After spending hundreds of thousands of years in Hell, surviving the horrors of the Damnation Arena, he was hardly any different from a Hell demon.
He had no horns, but the overwhelming aura he had forged through endless bloodshed made him even more terrifying than most demons.

However, after learning that his family had perished at the hands of Hell demons, Fjorge had grown to hate their race with every fiber of his being. That hatred was what had driven him to kill the Hell Emperor and countless other Hell demons.
After taking the hell emperor throne, he issued a single decree.
No Hell demon would ever again be allowed to set foot in the land of the living.

By then, he had finally come to understand that while he had become a legend in Hell, he had also unknowingly killed countless innocent humans, dragons, demons, and other living beings who had been kidnapped and forced into the Damnation Arena, just as he had.
But while he regretted that part of his past...
Killing Hell demons was not among those regrets.
He had enjoyed every second of it.
So when he saw demons slaughtering humans, he didn’t even bother asking who was right or wrong.
He simply began massacring the demons as though they were his lifelong enemies.
By the time the battle ended, even the humans he had saved were terrified of him.
Fjorge merely smirked before turning and walking away, intending to search for the family he already knew belonged to the barbarian race.
Unfortunately, he soon realised that finding them in a universe this vast wasn’t something that could be accomplished by wandering from one planet to another.
He needed to adapt.
Otherwise, he would never achieve anything.
Hell had been far simpler than the worlds of the living.
He knew he had to adapt. However, he soon came to another realisation.
Aside from smashing living things to death with a hammer, he possessed no practical skills that could earn him a living.
However...
He needed money.
He needed a reputation.
He needed connections.
Without them, navigating the complexities of the universe would be impossible.
"Fuck... why did I even come to the land of the living?" Fjorge cursed aloud before dropping onto his backside atop a mountain overlooking a vast sea of lava.
"At least the scenery here is far more pleasing than anything in Hell."
He chuckled before falling onto his back and drifting into a deep sleep. Seeing a vast sea of lava as pleasing to the eye, even said everything about him.
That nap lasted ten years.
When he finally woke up, it was because a group of humans had disturbed his sleep.
To Fjorge, who is muscular and tall, these humans were merely bugs.
There were three of them—identical twin siblings and their older sister, who had already reached the Demigod Realm.
From their conversation, he learned they had come to the mountain to mine ore for their father, who is a blacksmith.
It was the first time Fjorge had ever heard the term blacksmith.
Back in Hell, no one forged weapons.
They either hunted for them as natural born treasures in the countless Hell Seas or shaped bones and other materials into crude weapons through battle itself.
His curiosity was instantly piqued.
He helped the siblings gather far more ore than they had hoped to collect and even carried everything back to their home.
Then, for the very first time...
He witnessed blacksmithing.
The rhythmic ringing of a hammer against metal.
The glowing furnace.
The transformation of raw ore into a weapon.
He fell in love with it immediately.
"I like hammering things," Fjorge said as he looked at the man before him. "So this is probably the only thing I would be capable of doing. Please... take me as your disciple."
The blacksmith before him had yet to reach the Demigod Realm.
Under normal circumstances, someone like him should have been begging to become Fjorge’s disciple.
Instead, that day...
Immortal Blacksmith Ricado became the first man in history to accept a Supreme as his disciple.
Ten years later...
Immortal Blacksmith Ricado stood frozen, his jaw hanging open as he stared at the finest dagger he had ever laid eyes upon.
Fjorge stood behind the anvil, sweat trickling down his body as he smiled broadly at his master—or perhaps more accurately, his equal now.
Regardless, he had created the finest weapon any immortal had ever forged since the beginning of time.
But Immortal Blacksmith Ricado’s stunned expression wasn’t because of the dagger’s flawless beauty; it was because of the runes inscribed upon it.

Under normal circumstances, Immortal-grade weapons could hold only 10,000 runes. However, the dagger resting on the table before him contained 55,000 runes. This meant every aspect of craftsmanship that had gone into forging the dagger was flawless.
"I will call it Midnight Dagger," Fjorge said.
The dagger hummed, releasing a mist of darkness. The sight further stunned the poor Ricado, who immediately fell to his knees.
"Please, Senior Fjorge, take me as your disciple and teach me proper blacksmithing."
Fjorge laughed out loud, set down his hammer, and lifted Immortal Blacksmith Ricado to his feet.
"No need for such formality, Master. I am your disciple, so regardless of how high I climb, I will always see you as my master. And I will make sure the rest of the universe knows that."
That night, Fjorge and Immortal Blacksmith Ricado drank to their hearts’ content.
Over the next couple of days, Fjorge forged many new weapons, further cementing his mastery of blacksmithing. A year later, he left to pursue even greater knowledge.
However, before departing, he left behind thousands of years’ worth of blacksmithing knowledge for his master.
He knew it would be a long time before he returned, so he carefully documented everything he had learned.
He even included several outrageous theories that he believed would, if his master dared to experiment with them, greatly improve his craft.
Thousands of years later, the name Fjorge began to spread across cities, continents, planets, star systems, galaxies, and eventually the entire universe.
In time, he became known as the [Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith], simply because he commanded nine Sacred Flames that he had personally extracted from the Underworld.
After becoming the Supreme Blacksmith, the Flame Dao recognised him as one of its legendary wielders after he proclaimed the true names of all nine Sacred Flames under his command.

When the announcement spread across the universe, a small tribe of barbarians in a remote corner of the cosmos heard the news. Because both the name and title were included in the announcement, the tribe recognised him immediately.
That day, a father and mother who had mourned the death of their son for thousands of years finally found him again.
Kaelgorin Fjorge was the name his father had given him on the day he was born, and it had stayed with him throughout his life.
It took them another ten years to reunite with their son.
On that day, even the heavens celebrated, for the son whose destiny had been to destroy the universe while searching for his parents finally reunited with them, erasing that fate forever.
The happy ending so many dreamed of finally came to pass for that small family.
Fjorge had two younger sisters and a younger brother. In time, he became the King of the Barbarians and came to dominate the world of blacksmithing.
When the Flame Race invaded, he lifted his hammer once more and marched into battle, determined to ensure that the family he had finally found would continue to live on for countless eras.
Kent snapped his eyes open, and a powerful aura of flames, blood, and killing intent erupted from his body. Fortunately, when he had passed out, the tower had transported him to the Sword Tower.
As a result, the terrifying aura emanating from his body had no effect on anyone. Veth and Flura had already been informed by the tower that Kent was safe and would return before long.
The moment he awakened, his cultivation surged into the Immortal Emperor stage and kept rising.

chapters.title: Chapter 1738: Barbarian Dragon
paragraphs: "What in the Barbarian King is happening to Kent?" Vexthra muttered, standing atop the Sword of Enlightenment and staring at a 7’4" feet tall barbarian with dragon horns and a tail.
Standing beside her were Umai, Pandora, Yukiko, and Elina.
"So he was once a barbarian, huh?" Yukiko blushed, her eyes narrowing at the monster between Kent’s legs. "Good to know."
Her sister smirked, knowing Selene’s virus had gotten to her too.
But they also looked, and indeed, the monster between his legs was mighty.

Kent had told them that after he awakened the 13 Layered Life Discs, he gained the ability to morph into the appearance of his past incarnations. When he transformed, not even a Celestial could tell he had used a transformation ability.

But aside from that, he could tap into his past incarnations and make his body take on some of their properties. Right now, he looked and felt like Kent, but with the body of a barbarian mixed with a dragon.
He wasn’t the one who did that. It was basically his body taking on such a form, since he had just learned that in one of his past lives, he had indeed been a barbarian.

But by becoming a barbarian dragon, his physical strength had reached a level even he had no idea about. He had already been regarded as a monster when he was just a dragon, but as a barbarian dragon, his strength had multiplied severalfold.

Aside from that, his cultivation had already advanced to the Peak of the Immortal Monarch stage. That also contributed to his surge in strength, and as the five ladies stared at him, they could feel it overflowing.
Kent examined his body for a few minutes, then smiled. "It appears I keep changing every life I recover. If this continues, I might just become a completely unrecognisable monster one day."
He smiled, lifted his head, and waved at his wives, who, without any invitation, appeared before him, and Yukiko immediately went for his dick and started stroking it.
Vexthra kissed him, followed by Umai, Elina, and Pandora.

"Ladies, I was at an auction when this happened, so how about I go back before they start the bidding without me?" While technically only seconds had passed outside, he wanted to do something before Lady Wu announced the start of the bidding.
The five ladies became sad upon hearing he had to leave.
Kent smiled and returned to his dragon form. Even so, he had grown from 6’5" tall to 6’7", and his body had become even more refined.
He had become even more handsome, and most importantly, the girls thought his dick had become even more beautiful.
They wanted to play with it, but in the end, he had to leave.
"Then we’ll tag along," Umai suddenly declared, not ready to part with that dick.
The rest of her sisters nodded, and Kent, who had wanted to leave alone, had no choice but to take them with him. They appeared in the VIP room just before Lady Wu announced the third bid.

For the first time in many years, Kent used his teleportation ability and appeared at the center of the auction hall, causing many people to widen their eyes. Some even gasped the moment they saw him.

Kent had indeed become even more of an eye-catcher, but it was his overflowing aura as an Immortal Monarch, and the fact that his bloodline had grown even stronger, that made everyone present feel his overwhelming presence.
"Sorry for the interruption, Lady Wu, but I have something to say about this weapon before you announce the start of the bidding."

The person asking for a chance to speak was Kent Madson, someone everyone in attendance knew, so no one would have objected. However, to Lady Wu, Kent meant everything to her, so she nodded without the slightest hesitation.
In fact, she wanted to jump into his arms and kiss him. However, she managed to calm her racing heart.
"Go ahead," she said, a slight smirk tugging at the corner of her lips.
But how could Kent let her off so easily? His original plan to surprise her had already been ruined by her incredible attention to detail.
So he knew he had to win somehow. Thankfully, even though she wasn’t one of his beast companions, Kent could use spiritual energy to speak to her telepathically.
Just as she turned around to step back, Kent’s voice echoed in her mind.
"Have you been doing squats? I can see your butt has become much bigger."
Lady Wu missed a step and tripped, but managed to steady herself before she could fall. Although she regained her balance, her cheeks had turned crimson for no apparent reason.
Inside VIP Room 13, Kent’s wives facepalmed, knowing Kent had probably said something shameless that had nearly caused the dignified Lady Wu to stumble.
Kent then took the stage, pretending he hadn’t done anything to Lady Wu.

"Good day, everyone," he began. "I believe you all know who I am, but for those who don’t, my name is Kent Madson. I am a dragon, a swordsman, an alchemist, an assassin, a spirit painter, a mage, and a scholar." He grinned, knowing many were probably stunned by now.
"I also dabble a little in the dark arts, but that is a revelation for another time. I am here today because of my Scholar class.

"As most of you are aware, I will be participating in the Trial of Wisdom in a couple of months. So, with the credibility of the Cult of Wisdom on the line, whatever I am about to say is the truth and nothing but the truth."
Many people shifted in their seats, ready to listen. Kent may be a youngster, but he has already achieved so much that many of them never even dreamt of.
Kent pointed at the golden weapon shaped like a dragon’s tail, ending in a talon with a dragon’s head.
"This is the Nine Dragon Whip, a weapon created by one of the most legendary blacksmiths ever to walk the face of this universe.
"He was widely known as the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith."

Gasps spread throughout the auction hall, and even Lady Wu covered her lips as shock spread across her face. She had only been told that the Nine Dragon Whip was a weapon forged by a legendary blacksmith from a bygone era.
She had never imagined it had been crafted by perhaps the greatest blacksmith the universe had ever known.
"Kent Madson, are you certain this weapon was forged by that legendary figure?" asked a lady in VIP Room 79.
Kent nodded.
"Indeed. I have researched that expert extensively and learned about many of his achievements. He was truly the best—perhaps the greatest blacksmith to have ever lived.
His accomplishments were legendary, and most importantly, he was one of the few blacksmiths who forged weapons only to give them away for free."

Clearly, Kent was praising himself. However, he had indeed rendered a great service to the universe. In fact, he had made it a better place by placing powerful weapons into the hands of the right warriors.
During the Flame Era, everyone who wielded his weapons fought bravely. Some died, while others survived, but every one of them earned a place in the history books for their courage.

chapters.title: Chapter 1739: Nine Dragon Whip
paragraphs: "To make you all understand the true nature of this weapon, how about I tell you how this weapon came about?" Kent smiled and started to reveal how he created the Nine Dragon Whip...
"So, the Nine Dragon Whip was created from the souls of nine Celestial-stage Hell Demon Dragons."
Yet again, many gasped, not expecting the whip to be that advanced and extremely dangerous.
"I only know a little, but from two known records, it was said that the Nine Dragon Whip was created by the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith as a gift for one of his lovers.

It is a living weapon possessing the souls of nine Hell Demon Dragons and has been wielded by its owner during the Flame Wars, killing thousands of flame demons and beasts. In fact, contained inside the whip now are nine dragon souls that, if Lady Wu would permit me, I would like to awaken.
This also means the value of this whip would shoot from a mere God-grade weapon to a Celestial-grade living weapon."
Kent turned to Lady Wu, who nodded and muttered, still in shock, "Go ahead."
He nodded and opened the glass chamber, picking up the whip. His memories were triggered by the nine souls inside the whip.
The moment he set his sight on it, all nine of them opened their crazed eyes and looked at him, sending him down memory lane.
So he knew they were ready to awaken, just as he had also awakened his memories of the past.

Of course, if not because Kent was here today, perhaps the nine arrogant dragons wouldn’t have awakened to aid anyone. The person Fjorge created them for fell during the Flame Wars, and since then, they had never chosen another master.
Kent turned and looked at VIP Room 79 briefly before turning back to the whip.
He extended his left hand and summoned crimson flames. The moment the flames appeared, the whip wiggled, and it started to uncoil.

Kent brought the flame closer, and under everyone’s stunned gaze, he lit it with flames. Many gasped yet again, some fearing he had ruined the whip. However, a few seconds later, the whip released a powerful pressure.
ROAR! ROAR! ROAR! ROAR!...

Nine terrifying dragon roars followed, causing many to widen their eyes, with some turning pale. The pressure that came was so overwhelming that, had Kent not asked Pandora to block 90% of it, everyone would have passed out by now.

"Relax, guys, this is not the place to make a fuss," Kent said with a slight smirk before letting go of the whip. The moment he did, it separated into nine different whips and then transformed into nine terrifying dragon heads.
Every bccame even more pale now. Pandora was able to block the aura, but she did not shield their appearance.
All nine dragon heads locked their gazes on Kent, almost as if they wanted to devour him.
Then, in a language nobody understood, the red dragon head spoke, releasing flames from its eyes...
"So you have returned, Barbarian."
Kent smiled and responded, "Why, did you miss me?"
"Tch, as if anyone would miss a bastard like you," the white head, who had command over metal, sneered as he looked at Kent with disdain.

"No hard feelings, you nine, but you ambushed us and died fighting me. So, in my book, you lost fair and square. So what’s all this squirming for? Or are you telling me mighty dragons such as yourselves lack the basic decency to accept defeat?"
"You clearly know what you did, bastard," the black dragon head said, mist of water surrounding him. "You promised to upgrade us when you handed us over to that feisty lady.

But what did you do? You went and died like a chicken, leaving us to be wielded by lowlifes and overprivileged bastards. You owe us as a Barbarian. You owe us big time, so you’d better start planning how to repay us."
Kent smirked. "I know I owe you guys, and no, I didn’t die like a chicken. I died fighting terrifying Primordials. Or do you think someone like me would die that pitifully?"
He turned slightly and looked at VIP Room 79. "Plus, your master is already back. Or you losers can’t sense her feisty aura inside this place?"
The nine dragons narrowed their eyes for a moment. Then, in one motion, they all turned and looked at VIP Room 79...

Inside the room, a lady with a slave collar around her neck stood beside a fat-looking man who clearly had a knack for indulging in anything oily and greasy, even while he was slowly dying from poison.
The lady was more like the fatty’s spokesperson. When she questioned Kent a few minutes ago, it was at the command of the fatty, whose wealth made him untouchable.

Unfortunately for him, fate had arranged this auction for Kent to recover the memories of one of his past lives and also to reunite him with not one, but several people close to him, both from this era and the past.
The lady with the slave collar was both Kent’s lover from his past incarnation as Fjorge and one of the finest warriors he had ever known. She was the original wielder of the Nine Dragon Whip.
Now, she had been reduced to a mere slave. However, because he had decided not to destroy this place, his anger had been suppressed with all his willpower.
The dragons became furious when they saw the state their master was in, but Kent calmed them down and said in the language they were speaking...
"Relax, guys. I will make sure he dies the most painful death possible. For now, go back inside the whip and wait for the auction to end. We’ll discuss the details of your upgrade later."
They nodded and returned to the whip. Kent then placed it back into the glass chamber and turned to Lady Wu.

chapters.title: Chapter 1740: Bidding War
paragraphs: "Ten Trillion."
In no time, the bid was raised to ten trillion by a man in VIP room 27. However, he wasn’t done when the bid rose again.
"11 Trillion,"
"11.5 Trillion."

There was no slowing down, not when something this valuable was on the table. If it were before Kent revealed the blacksmith who created the Nine Dragon Whip and awakened the weapon spirits, the maximum price would have been capped at 10 trillion.
However, the weapon being sold now is far too precious.
In fact, even if the person who put it up for sale were here, they would have prevented Lady Wu from auctioning it.
They would have taken it for themselves since, regardless of what one thinks, a living weapon doesn’t require the wielder to know how to handle weapons.
They can fight for themselves, so even someone like the fatty in VIP room 79 would be able to use it since, when in danger, the whip would fight by itself, defending him from all forms of danger.

Because of that, irrespective of the grade of the weapon, whenever one appears at an auction, people wage war over it. Living weapons are always a cause of bidding wars that mostly end in death after the auction.
So, within five minutes, the price had already climbed so high...
"20 Trillion," someone raised the bid from 15 trillion, causing many to fall silent. They recognized that someone with much deeper pockets had stepped into the bidding war.
But he wasn’t the only one with deeper pockets.
Veth, whom Kent had tasked with winning the bid, smiled and called out her bid.
"22 Trillion."
On the stage, Lady Wu looked toward VIP room 13 and smiled.
Hearing one of her sisters’ voices made her happy. If the whip were something her adventurers had found, she would have outright handed it over to Veth now that she realized she needed it.
But unfortunately, Veth would have to win the bid like everyone else.
Meanwhile, Kent was seated between six damsels, one of them already sucking his dick while Pandora was feeding him her breast milk.
While the rooms were protected by soundproof arrays, Veth’s bidding had now deactivated them. However, Pandora merely had to think it, and no sound except Veth’s would go out.
So even if they were to have sex now, nobody would know.
But they were taking things slowly for now since they knew the auction hadn’t even truly begun yet. Seeing that only two of them were having fun, they reclined in their chairs, making Kent lean back.

Yukiko jumped on him and continued to suck his dick while Vexthra went for his balls. Elina, Umai, and Flura would have to wait for their turn. A few seconds later, they ripped Kent’s clothes off and started leaving kiss marks on his body.
Veth turned slightly to see what her sisters were doing. Seeing that she was missing out on some fun, she kept raising the bid, making sure to win while keeping the price fair.

But she underestimated the wealth of some people. The more she raised the bid, the more they countered. Soon, the war heated up, and those who could sense non-verbal threats saw killing intent rising in the air.

Meanwhile, Kent, who was getting attention from his wives, allowed himself to enjoy the moment while his mind went through the memories he had recovered of his life as Fjorge, the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith.

He had recovered all the memories of that life. Of course, he knew there might still be a few hidden ones, just like how a few memories of the ruthless bandit had remained hidden until he recovered them when he went to the Star Realm.
The same was true for Chaos, whose memories of the Bone Tempering Art were sealed until Kent obtained the technique himself.
But aside from that, his memories of Fjorge were indeed wild. From when he was just a child to the day he died, his life had been one challenge after another.

He had so much fun in Hell, killing hell demons like it was a normal Tuesday. Then he became a blacksmith, and that trend continued, only this time, instead of killing, he kept creating one treasure after another.
He created thousands of spears, thousands of swords, and many more just because he wanted warriors to have the best weapons when going into battle.

Kent witnessed it all—the times when he was called mad for coming up with ideas many claimed were impossible. Some even claimed his ideas were infeasible, yet by the time they realized it, he had already created it.
His legendary feats, such as creating the Ten Dao Weapons, the 1,000 Deadly Daggers, and many more, were all ideas he came up with but was ridiculed for.
However, his wildest creation idea came when he proposed creating weapons with Resentful Spirits as their weapon spirits.
It was during the Flame War that, after the second wave arrived, the Flame Race managed to devise ways to block the weapon spirits of the soul weapons wielded by the warriors of this universe.
Many died because their weapons failed them.
The Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith proposed the creation of such dark weapons, but he was called a madman. He laughed and left, then forged the 100 Cursed Weapons anyway.

Later, when the leaders of the universe came begging, he merely laughed and handed them the weapons. They knew the risk of being corrupted by the weapons was high; however, they were desperate, so the weapons were made.
Kent witnessed the climax of the war when Fjorge was locked down by five Pseudo-Primordials and a Primordial.
That moment was his weakest, but it was also the day his breakthrough—or at least a glimpse of the next realm, the Primordial Blacksmith—came to him.
That moment told him everything he had been blind to...
"This is your end, barbarian." A bull-like, muscular flame beast in his demi-human form, with a head made of bones engulfed in purple flames, spoke.
"Your universe will fall into the hands of the Eternal Flame Empress, and there is nothing you can ever do about it."

Fjorge, whose body was littered with all kinds of horrific injuries, one eye blinded, raised his head and laughed. He turned and looked at the Purple Flame King, or at least that was what he chose to call him.
"You know what is funny?" Fjorge spat out a mouthful of blood and grinned. "I have been hammering metal ores and skulls for my entire life, but never have I once dared hammer my own skull."
The Purple Flame King narrowed his eyes, and the five Pseudo-Primordials frowned.
Fjorge slowly stood up, stretched his broken arms, and smiled.
"A wise man once said, ’The way beyond is threaded backward.’ In the past, I never understood it until today."
He extended his hand, and the hammer that had accompanied him for a lifetime flew into his grasp.
"I have forged many weapons and dealt with all kinds of weapon spirits, but never have I once dared put a soul into this hammer. Do you know why?"
"You are going to tell me anyway, so why even bother to ask?" the Purple Flame King replied, and Fjorge grinned.
"Indeed, I will tell you."
He looked at the hammer for a few seconds, then smiled one last time.
"I have lived with this hammer for years, treating it as a tool when I should have seen it as a companion."
He sighed before looking at the hammer and declaring,
"I am sorry, buddy. I was blind to the truth, so to make it up to you, I set you free. From this day onward, you shall bear the name Mjönir, the Primordial Hell Damnation Hammer."
Fjorge imbued his soul into the hammer, and then he smashed it into his own head, offering his blood too.
That day, one Primordial and five Pseudo-Primordials died miserably, feeling the wrath of the first Primordial-grade weapon ever forged in the history of this universe.

His words, however, told everyone he was a Supreme. At once, many backed down, causing Lady Wu to frown. She had a 15% stake in this bid, so even if her sister Veth failed to win, she would still make a fortune.
However, with this man subtly revealing his status, no mortal with a functioning brain would dare go against him unless, of course, they wished to court death.
Kent narrowed his eyes at VIP room 1 to see who dared mess with his woman. However, before he could do anything, Veth beat him to it.
"120 trillion."
She increased the bid by 20 trillion, and in that instant, the mood in the auction hall changed at once. From within VIP room 1, a chilling aura began to emanate, heading directly toward VIP room 13.

Perhaps forgetting that Kent and her sisters were behind her, Veth reached into her space ring and pulled out a golden ring. The moment she slipped it onto her left index finger, a protective dome appeared around her, blocking the aura.

Kent and his wives were stunned, not expecting Veth to have the willpower to challenge a Supreme. Clearly, she had realized that the person she was locked in a bidding war with was no longer someone she could casually compete with. However, she didn’t seem to care and had even increased the bid by 20 trillion.
That was bold, and to Kent, it was badass.
’She has become bolder and more confident now.’ He smiled. ’Good job, Veth. I am proud of you.’
Seeing that his aura wasn’t doing the trick, the man in VIP room 1 resorted to breaking the rules by issuing threats.
"I never expected lower beings such as mere immortals to dare compete with a Supreme such as myself, the Green Banner Arcana Supreme, leader of the Green Banner Supreme Guild."
He chuckled and raised the bid again.
"200 trillion."
Kent’s eyes narrowed, and then a smile formed on his face.
’Damn, Elon Musk got nothing on him.’
Veth smirked.
"Clearly, the division of the universe has made the Supremes look down on us immortals. Today, I, Veth, will open your eyes to the truth. Supreme or Immortal, this is an auction, so bid with dignity"
"300 trillion."
On the stage, Lady Wu smiled.
’Well, it looks like with Kent around, she has finally grown a pair.’
She looked toward VIP room 1, where she could hear the heavy breathing of the Supreme who had come in place of another Supreme she had invited.
’I am sure Lady Costa will be pissed when she finds out this bastard tried to use his status to rig the auction.’
She waited to see what the Supreme would do. After a minute, the man spoke.
"We will meet again, bitch."
Everyone heard a door slam, signaling that the man had abandoned both the bidding war and the rest of the auction. This sounded like good news to them.
However, the current price was no longer something anyone would dare challenge, especially when there were still twenty-two treasures left to be auctioned.
"Are we just going to allow him to leave like that?" Elina asked, looking at Pandora, her big sister, who claimed she was the strongest in the entire universe.
The girls smiled, knowing Elina simply wanted to get revenge for her big sister, Veth.
Fortunately, when it came to the Chaos Dragon Harem, the women always supported one another.

"I have already trapped him in an illusion that will activate once he reaches the Supreme Realm. Hopefully, when the illusion breaks a hundred years from now, he won’t dare look down on immortals ever again."
"You are the best, Big Sister Yukiko."
Elina hugged Yukiko, who at the moment was the second strongest in the harem and also a master of illusions.

Even Adina, the undisputed beauty of the harem, had taken Yukiko as her master. As one of the Thirteen Divine Wonders and a Pseudo-Primordial, placing a Supreme under an illusion without them noticing was as effortless as a single thought.
That was how much control she possessed when it came to Illusions.
Kent simply smiled, knowing he had nothing to worry about. His wives had already handled everything.
"Since there are no more bids, the Nine Dragon Whip goes to the lady in VIP room 13."
"I will pay after the auction," Veth said with a smile before turning back to Kent, who opened his arms for her to dive into. She had done well, and that alone was enough to make Kent happy.
Veth removed the ring, causing the protective dome to disappear, before jumping into Kent’s arms, earning eye rolls and jealous looks from her sisters.
But she didn’t care. Now that she had won, she intended to enjoy her reward.
Lady Wu gestured for the next item to be brought onto the stage. It was a suit of armor, something Kent had no use for, so he ignored it.
He had only come for things he couldn’t obtain from the Tower Shop.
After hugging him for a while, Veth pulled her head back and looked at Kent with a determined expression.
"I want to become stronger so no one can ever make me feel scared again."
Upon hearing her request, her sisters immediately surrounded her, instantly forgetting that they had been jealous of her for using Kent’s body as her pillow.
Kent cupped her cheeks and smiled.
"Of course. I will make you stronger. In fact, you will become one of the greatest archers in the universe soon."
The ladies, who knew that most of them had, in one way or another, crossed paths with Kent’s past incarnations, looked at him with questioning gazes.
Kent merely smirked before revealing a small part of the truth.

"Yes, Veth was one of my friends during the Flame Era. She was the daughter of my blacksmith master. She followed me around for a while before later joining a women-only sect that specialized in archery.
She fought on the front lines during the Flame Wars. In fact, she was the vice-captain of the Flame Valkyries, a group of elite female warriors, each an exceptional wielder of the Flame Dao."

The ladies turned to look at Veth, who smiled before resting her head back on Kent’s chest. She had no idea she had lived such an extraordinary life in her past. So while she was still in shock, she also couldn’t help but feel happy.

She had a 15% stake in this bid, so even if her sister Veth failed to win, she would still make a fortune.
However, with this man subtly revealing his status, no mortal with a functioning brain would dare go against him unless, of course, they wished to court death.
Kent narrowed his eyes at VIP room 1 to see who dared mess with his woman.
However, before he could do anything, Veth beat him to it.
"120 trillion."
She increased the bid by 20 trillion, and in that instant, the mood in the auction hall changed at once.
From within VIP room 1, a chilling aura began to emanate, heading directly toward VIP room 13.
Perhaps forgetting that Kent and her sisters were behind her, Veth reached into her space ring and pulled out a golden ring.
The moment she slipped it onto her left index finger, a protective dome appeared around her, blocking the aura.
Kent and his wives were stunned, not expecting Veth to have the willpower to challenge a Supreme.
Clearly, she had realized that the person she was locked in a bidding war with was no longer someone she could casually compete with.
However, she didn’t seem to care and had even increased the bid by 20 trillion.
That was bold, and to Kent, it was badass.
’She has become bolder and more confident now.’ He smiled. ’Good job, Veth.
I am proud of you.’
Seeing that his aura wasn’t doing the trick, the man in VIP room 1 resorted to breaking the rules by issuing threats.
"I never expected lower beings such as mere immortals to dare compete with a Supreme such as myself, the Green Banner Arcana Supreme, leader of the Green Banner Supreme Guild."
He chuckled and raised the bid again.
"200 trillion."
Kent’s eyes narrowed, and then a smile formed on his face.
’Damn, Elon Musk got nothing on him.’
Veth smirked.
"Clearly, the division of the universe has made the Supremes look down on us immortals.
Today, I, Veth, will open your eyes to the truth.
Supreme or Immortal, this is an auction, so bid with dignity"
"300 trillion."
On the stage, Lady Wu smiled.
’Well, it looks like with Kent around, she has finally grown a pair.’
She looked toward VIP room 1, where she could hear the heavy breathing of the Supreme who had come in place of another Supreme she had invited.
’I am sure Lady Costa will be pissed when she finds out this bastard tried to use his status to rig the auction.’
She waited to see what the Supreme would do.
After a minute, the man spoke.
"We will meet again, bitch."
Everyone heard a door slam, signaling that the man had abandoned both the bidding war and the rest of the auction.
This sounded like good news to them.
However, the current price was no longer something anyone would dare challenge, especially when there were still twenty-two treasures left to be auctioned.
"Are we just going to allow him to leave like that?" Elina asked, looking at Pandora, her big sister, who claimed she was the strongest in the entire universe.
The girls smiled, knowing Elina simply wanted to get revenge for her big sister, Veth.
Fortunately, when it came to the Chaos Dragon Harem, the women always supported one another.
"I have already trapped him in an illusion that will activate once he reaches the Supreme Realm.
Hopefully, when the illusion breaks a hundred years from now, he won’t dare look down on immortals ever again."
"You are the best, Big Sister Yukiko."
Elina hugged Yukiko, who at the moment was the second strongest in the harem and also a master of illusions.
Even Adina, the undisputed beauty of the harem, had taken Yukiko as her master.
As one of the Thirteen Divine Wonders and a Pseudo-Primordial, placing a Supreme under an illusion without them noticing was as effortless as a single thought.
That was how much control she possessed when it came to Illusions.
Kent simply smiled, knowing he had nothing to worry about.
His wives had already handled everything.
"Since there are no more bids, the Nine Dragon Whip goes to the lady in VIP room 13."
"I will pay after the auction," Veth said with a smile before turning back to Kent, who opened his arms for her to dive into.
She had done well, and that alone was enough to make Kent happy.
Veth removed the ring, causing the protective dome to disappear, before jumping into Kent’s arms, earning eye rolls and jealous looks from her sisters.
But she didn’t care.
Now that she had won, she intended to enjoy her reward.
Lady Wu gestured for the next item to be brought onto the stage.
It was a suit of armor, something Kent had no use for, so he ignored it.
He had only come for things he couldn’t obtain from the Tower Shop.
After hugging him for a while, Veth pulled her head back and looked at Kent with a determined expression.
"I want to become stronger so no one can ever make me feel scared again."
Upon hearing her request, her sisters immediately surrounded her, instantly forgetting that they had been jealous of her for using Kent’s body as her pillow.
Kent cupped her cheeks and smiled.
"Of course.
I will make you stronger.
In fact, you will become one of the greatest archers in the universe soon."
The ladies, who knew that most of them had, in one way or another, crossed paths with Kent’s past incarnations, looked at him with questioning gazes.
Kent merely smirked before revealing a small part of the truth.
"Yes, Veth was one of my friends during the Flame Era.
She was the daughter of my blacksmith master.
She followed me around for a while before later joining a women-only sect that specialized in archery.
She fought on the front lines during the Flame Wars.
In fact, she was the vice-captain of the Flame Valkyries, a group of elite female warriors, each an exceptional wielder of the Flame Dao."
The ladies turned to look at Veth, who smiled before resting her head back on Kent’s chest.
She had no idea she had lived such an extraordinary life in her past.
So while she was still in shock, she also couldn’t help but feel happy.

chapters.title: Chapter 1742: Blood Sand Berserker
paragraphs: The auction continued with the fourth item, but Kent and his wives had tuned out since the item up for bidding wasn’t something they wanted. In fact, they chose to ignore everything and focus on their own enjoyment.
Meanwhile, far away on another immortal planet, three of his wives—Liora, Princess Lovina, and Enzi—had arrived at the location where their mission would take place.
Their mission had brought them to a planet called Zhrakn. It was a desert planet inhabited by a race of Sand Demons whose nature is quite mysterious to many.
They had only interacted briefly with other races in the past.

However, they had later retreated to the deeper parts of their planet, where ordinary demons and humans could not reach. Nobody knew why they had done that, but as the years passed, they remained there, and most people eventually stopped paying attention.

Five years ago, they sent out a distress signal suggesting they were in danger. Upon investigation, it was discovered that they had been kidnapped—or rather, driven into a corner—by a very powerful beast called the Blood Sand Berserker.

Many had tried to hunt down the beast, but none of the thousands that went after it ever returned. Obviously, the beast wasn’t an ordinary one. Over time, people stopped bothering to go after it, leaving the Sand Demons at the mercy of the Blood Sand Berserker.
Kent had received a quest to kill it, but since his wives had chosen missions of their own to embark on, he handed the quest over to Liora, Princess Lovina, and Enzi.
They had arrived on the Sand Planet two days ago and had been tracking the Blood Sand Berserker ever since. Their mission was simple: kill the Blood Sand Berserker.
After two days, they finally managed to locate it. The three ladies then found a place to camp for the night.
Liora, being the assassin of the team, had scouted ahead to map out the terrain. After a couple of hours, she returned with both good and bad news.
"So, what is the good news?" Princess Lovina asked, handing a spirit fruit to Liora.

"The good news is that the battle will take place in a forest filled with dried plants. That will create plenty of shadows I can use to my advantage. However, the bad news is that the ground is made entirely of sand. After observing the beast for a few hours, I noticed it uses the sand far more effectively than the quest described.

"In fact, the reason so many people never returned was that the beast’s control over the sand is incredibly advanced to the point that this planet is a weapon it could harness. We’d better prepare for that and make sure the battle doesn’t drag on, or it’ll end badly for us.
"Apart from that, I think I know where the Sand Demons are."
Liora took a bite of the fruit Princess Lovina had given her before pointing at the ground.
"They’ve been imprisoned beneath the sand, and the Blood Sand Berserker has been feeding on them for years now.
"The only way we can save them is to kill the Blood Sand Berserker and make sure it never gets the chance to harm them during the battle. This meant it must be isolated from its natural domain."
"I’ll handle controlling the battlefield," Enzi said, and her two sisters had no doubt she would be able to do exactly that. Her affinity for the Glass Element perfectly countered the Sand Element.
Of course, with her extensive control over the element and the fact that she was now an Immortal King, she could do far more than simply use it for movement.
Their opponent was obviously a Demigod. However, even as an Immortal King, Enzi knew she would be able to keep the beast away from the sand for a while.
Liora had already reached the Immortal Monarch stage, so with her already extensive experience in controlling shadows and wielding the Darkness Element, her assassin abilities would come into play.

She had been a member of the Midnight Shadows before she became an alchemist. However, now that she had abandoned her alchemist path and had fully embraced the daggers once more, she had never stopped training.
She had already reached the Shadow Legend stage, making her someone comparable to a Sword Legend. This meant her assassin abilities had become even more refined and deadly.
However, while Liora and Enzi were indeed powerful warriors, Princess Lovina was the strongest member of the team.
She had already reached the Immortal Lord stage, and on top of that, her poison abilities had already transcended those of an ordinary Immortal Lord.
Princess Lovina now possessed a Poison Domain, so regardless of how dangerous her opponent was, as long as she could contain it within her Poison Domain, she could either kill it or weaken it.
She had also ventured into the combat aspect of her Poison Mage class, so she wouldn’t simply stand at the back and watch.
"I feel like we can win this easily if we put our minds to it," Enzi said, and her sisters nodded.
They indeed could win easily. However, to do that, they needed the element of surprise.
Three hours later, a shadow moved across the dunes of the brown desert; her destination was a forest filled with thousands of nearly dried-up plants.
Within the forest, a beast that resembled a lizard-rhino slept lazily on the sand, its body radiating a terrifying Demigod aura.

The Blood Sand Berserker was a massive, hulking creature with the body of a rhino and the scales of a lizard. Its skin was a deep burnt-orange color with darker, almost black stripes running along its back.
Its eyes burned like embers, four horns protruded from its head, and its claws ended in deadly talons. Just one deadly attack from it, and that would be all.

Liora knew she needed the element of surprise to unleash her attack, so she didn’t rush her movements. She carefully limited her speed, making sure she could approach within 200 meters of the Blood Sand Berserker without revealing herself.
Five minutes later, she was still 300 meters away. However, she paused and began observing the beast. After another thirty minutes, she resumed moving.
However, the moment Liora emerged from a certain shadow, the sand around her suddenly shifted, and a dome of crystallized sand instantly formed around her.
"I hate shadows the most."
The beast suddenly spoke as it turned its massive body toward the dome, trapping Liora.
"You think I didn’t notice you the first time you came to spy on me?"
Its enormous body lumbered toward the dome.
Within the prison, Liora attempted to break free, only to discover that it was far sturdier than she had anticipated.
However, she didn’t panic. In fact, she wanted the beast to come closer so she could do exactly what she had come to do.
Just as expected, the Blood Sand Berserker, believing it had already won, crossed the 200-meter mark and soon stood only 50 meters away from Liora. In the past, it has used this method to kill many.
At that moment, Liora smiled and activated her technique.
"Midnight Realm."
Darkness instantly engulfed the surrounding space, robbing the Blood Sand Berserker of its vision.
However, the darkness itself wasn’t Liora’s objective.
It was the momentary blindness she was counting on...
And she was right to choose this move, because the instant the Blood Sand Berserker lost its sight, Princess Lovina appeared.

With a wave of her staff, a sea of poisonous lotuses bloomed into existence. Then, as though they had been programmed to detonate one after another, the entire forest was instantly shrouded in an extremely dense, poisonous mist, so potent that the Blood Sand Berserker immediately sensed the poisonous danger.

chapters.title: Chapter 1743: Glass Domain Unleashed
paragraphs: The moment the poison spread across the battlefield, Enzi arrived before the crystallised dome and placed her hand on it. The next second, it shattered like glass, freeing Liora.
Immediately, Liora slipped back into the shadows and headed toward the Blood Sand Berserker.

Enzi, however, disappeared from the battlefield for a brief moment before taking a step forward. A few seconds later, all four combatants found themselves within an arena-like space made entirely of glass.
"Welcome to the Glass Domain," Enzi said with a smile, standing atop a platform of thick crystal glass.

The Blood Sand Berserker growled, its body burning as though it had been drenched in blazing oil. Unfortunately for it, the Poison Princess Lovina wasn’t someone who ever missed when it came to using poison in battle.
Princess Lovina had come a long way on her journey as a poison cultivator.
Now, instead of relying solely on internal effects, her poison could inflict even more devastating external injuries, the kind that made her an exceptionally deadly warrior.
Just one attack was all it took to render the Blood Sand Berserker immobile long enough for Enzi to pull it into the very place they wanted it.
Three hours earlier, Enzi had come up with the perfect attack plan...

"We can beat it if we manage to bring it into my Glass Domain. Right now, if we fight it in the desert, it could overpower us. So the only way is to lure it into my Glass Domain. Liora will distract it long enough for Princess Lovina to poison it.
If everything goes well, I’ll be able to pull it into the Glass Domain, where killing it will be much simpler."
Enzi smiled as she watched the first step of the plan succeed.
"Human, you dare attack me in my own domain?" the Blood Sand Berserker said, its body radiating an overwhelmingly powerful aura.
"Your domain? Are you insane or something?" Enzi asked with a frown. "The last time I checked, you kidnapped every last Sand Demon and have been feeding on them. Aren’t you ashamed of yourself?"
Her words came from a place of genuine anger. Learning that millions had been captured by this beast and were probably nothing more than its food had greatly infuriated her.
"Their lives are inconsequential to the bigger picture, so they should be grateful I found a use for them," the Blood Sand Berserker replied.
At once, a terrifying aura erupted from its body, threatening to devour the three women and shatter the domain.
However, when it realised the domain wasn’t going anywhere, it narrowed its eyes at Enzi. Just as it was about to issue another warning, Enzi made her move.
"Threefold Glass Domain Dimension."
The domain shifted, and a second later, the Blood Sand Berserker found itself in three different places at the same time, facing one of the three ladies in each of those spaces.
Even more horrifying, its Demigod cultivation had been reduced to the Immortal Monarch stage.
In one space, its beast form faced Enzi.
In another, its demi-human form faced Princess Lovina.
And in the third, it had become fully human as it confronted Liora.
"What... what have you done?" the Blood Sand Berserker asked, its eyes bloodshot as it stared at Enzi, who wore a smirk at the corner of her beautiful face.

"What do you think?" she replied. "I separated your existence into three, making sure you have to fight each of us in a different dimension. The only way you survive this is by killing all three of us... or by killing me."
She brushed her silver hair behind her shoulder and extended a hand, summoning a sleek crystal sword.
"But let’s be honest—you never stood a chance, even in your true Demigod form."
She moved.
The sound of shattering glass echoed throughout the domain.
In the blink of an eye, Enzi was already upon the Blood Sand Berserker, her sword unleashing deadly arcs of glass that sliced through the air.
The Blood Sand Berserker had no choice but to fight back with everything it had. Otherwise, it would die before it even realised what had happened.

In the second glass dimension, Princess Lovina floated gracefully in the air, dozens of poisonous lotuses hovering behind her as she gazed coldly at the demi-human version of the Blood Sand Berserker.
Enzi’s Glass Domain had indeed become much stronger after she advanced to the Immortal stage.
Now, she could do far more than simply trap people inside it.
She could exploit the different aspects of their existence.
Against a beast, she could separate it into three distinct forms—its true beast form, its demi-human form, and its humanoid form.
However, because every aspect of the target was divided, its cultivation was divided as well.
As a result, the Blood Sand Berserker had been reduced to the Immortal Monarch stage in each dimension, drastically lowering its combat power.
More importantly, its consciousness had also been split threefold, forcing it to perceive and react to three simultaneous battles.
Its focus had been completely divided.
The effect on its combat ability became immediately apparent the moment Princess Lovina launched her attack.
"Such a pity."
Her staff swept through the air.
Dozens of poisonous lotuses immediately rained down upon the unfortunate demi-human form of the Blood Sand Berserker, which was already being assaulted simultaneously in the other two dimensions.
Liora glided across the battlefield, her body moving as though she were made of wind itself.
She appeared directly before the humanoid form of the Blood Sand Berserker and struck, her left dagger shooting toward its neck.
The Blood Sand Berserker managed to block the attack and quickly retreated.
However, a pillar of glass suddenly rose from the ground, casting a narrow shadow.
That was all Liora needed.
Before the Blood Sand Berserker could track her again, she had already emerged from the new shadow behind it, launching another deadly slash aimed at its neck.
It twisted its body aside, narrowly avoiding a fatal wound, but Liora’s dagger still carved a deep gash across its shoulder.
Without giving it a moment to recover, she thrust her right dagger toward its chest.
Seeing that it had no chance of dodging, the Blood Sand Berserker made a desperate decision and blocked the attack with its hand.
The dagger pierced straight through its palm, drawing blood.
Liora, an experienced assassin, twisted the blade, aiming to inflict pain.
As expected, a surge of unbearable pain coursed through the Blood Sand Berserker’s body.
However, because its existence had been split into three, the pain was instantly transferred to its other two forms as well.
The sudden agony disrupted the beast-form version long enough for Enzi to carve a deep slash across its body.
That injury, in turn, was also transmitted to the remaining two forms.
However, while the beast and humanoid forms had already suffered considerable injuries, the greatest danger lay in the demi-human form.
Princess Lovina’s poison had already taken hold.
It was steadily spreading throughout its body, continuously slowing its movements.
Because all three forms remained connected, the poison’s effects were shared among them as well.
As a result, every one of its forms became noticeably slower.
This wasn’t good news for the Blood Sand Berserker. The longer the battle stretched on, the more danger it would find itself in.
However, even after enduring simultaneous assaults from three dimensions and forcing itself into a heightened state of awareness, it realised it had truly fallen into a deadly trap.
"ROAR!"
So it unleashed a thunderous roar and activated its last trump card.
Then, all of a sudden, a black berserker aura erupted from its body.
"Lovina, do it," Enzi commanded the instant the beast entered its berserker state.
Inside the second glass dimension, Princess Lovina smiled.
She waved her staff before activating one of her deadliest abilities.
In an instant, the entire dimension turned crimson.
Then, from within the sea of blood-red poison, a heart-wrenching scream erupted from the Blood Sand Berserker.

Now, she could do far more than simply trap people inside it.
She could exploit the different aspects of their existence.
Against a beast, she could separate it into three distinct forms—its true beast form, its demi-human form, and its humanoid form.
However, because every aspect of the target was divided, its cultivation was divided as well.
As a result, the Blood Sand Berserker had been reduced to the Immortal Monarch stage in each dimension, drastically lowering its combat power.
More importantly, its consciousness had also been split threefold, forcing it to perceive and react to three simultaneous battles.
Its focus had been completely divided.
The effect on its combat ability became immediately apparent the moment Princess Lovina launched her attack.
"Such a pity."
Her staff swept through the air.
Dozens of poisonous lotuses immediately rained down upon the unfortunate demi-human form of the Blood Sand Berserker, which was already being assaulted simultaneously in the other two dimensions.
Liora glided across the battlefield, her body moving as though she were made of wind itself.
She appeared directly before the humanoid form of the Blood Sand Berserker and struck, her left dagger shooting toward its neck.
The Blood Sand Berserker managed to block the attack and quickly retreated.
However, a pillar of glass suddenly rose from the ground, casting a narrow shadow.
That was all Liora needed.
Before the Blood Sand Berserker could track her again, she had already emerged from the new shadow behind it, launching another deadly slash aimed at its neck.
It twisted its body aside, narrowly avoiding a fatal wound, but Liora’s dagger still carved a deep gash across its shoulder.
Without giving it a moment to recover, she thrust her right dagger toward its chest.
Seeing that it had no chance of dodging, the Blood Sand Berserker made a desperate decision and blocked the attack with its hand.
The dagger pierced straight through its palm, drawing blood.
Liora, an experienced assassin, twisted the blade, aiming to inflict pain.
As expected, a surge of unbearable pain coursed through the Blood Sand Berserker’s body.
However, because its existence had been split into three, the pain was instantly transferred to its other two forms as well.
The sudden agony disrupted the beast-form version long enough for Enzi to carve a deep slash across its body.
That injury, in turn, was also transmitted to the remaining two forms.
However, while the beast and humanoid forms had already suffered considerable injuries, the greatest danger lay in the demi-human form.
Princess Lovina’s poison had already taken hold.
It was steadily spreading throughout its body, continuously slowing its movements.
Because all three forms remained connected, the poison’s effects were shared among them as well.
As a result, every one of its forms became noticeably slower.
This wasn’t good news for the Blood Sand Berserker.
The longer the battle stretched on, the more danger it would find itself in.
However, even after enduring simultaneous assaults from three dimensions and forcing itself into a heightened state of awareness, it realised it had truly fallen into a deadly trap.
"ROAR!"
So it unleashed a thunderous roar and activated its last trump card.
Then, all of a sudden, a black berserker aura erupted from its body.
"Lovina, do it," Enzi commanded the instant the beast entered its berserker state.
Inside the second glass dimension, Princess Lovina smiled.
She waved her staff before activating one of her deadliest abilities.
In an instant, the entire dimension turned crimson.
Then, from within the sea of blood-red poison, a heart-wrenching scream erupted from the Blood Sand Berserker.

chapters.title: Chapter 1744: Poison Domain
paragraphs: The blood-red poison surged like an endless tide, swallowing every inch of the second glass dimension. With the signal given, Princess Lovina wasted no time activating her poison domain.
This opened a domain filled with nothing but poison.
In fact, this domain was wielded by Princess Lovina in her past life. She wasn’t supposed to awaken it this early in her current life. However, one thing led to another, and now she was using it.
While it isn’t even 10% as powerful as the true Poison Domain, it was enough to kill even a god.
The moment it activated, the Blood Sand Berserker’s demi-human form let out another agonising scream as its flesh rapidly blackened.
Crimson veins spread across its body while poisonous lotus petals clung to its skin like parasites, each one injecting a different toxin into its bloodstream.
"What... is... this poison?"
Its voice trembled with disbelief, terror, and pain.
Princess Lovina floated calmly in the air, her blue robes fluttering gently despite the violent storm of poison surrounding her.
She knew the battle was as good as over. After all, within the poison domain, even non-living things wouldn’t survive.
And with the demi-human version of the Blood Sand Berserker now poisoned, both the main beast form and the humanoid form were subjected to the excruciating pain of their skin melting away.

It took just a few minutes for the demi-human version to die. The moment it did, the human and beast forms followed. In no time, all three versions died, and that was the end of the battle between the three ladies and the Blood Sand Berserker.
The Glass Domain came undone, and the body of the Blood Sand Berserker fell out.

Now that the battle was over and the domain had been deactivated, the other versions were no more. However, because all three versions had died before the domain was deactivated, the beast’s main body died as well.
Perhaps if one of the three versions had survived, it wouldn’t have died.
But it died before it even knew how it had happened. As they say, sometimes winning is all about having the best strategy and perfect execution.
The battle would have been brutal had they not isolated the Blood Sand Berserker within the Glass Domain. They gambled, and it worked.
The three ladies sighed upon seeing their target dead.
"Good job, everyone," Princess Lovina said as she walked toward the body of the dead beast.

"Now, we have to find a way to retrieve the trapped sand demons despite our mission stating that we are only to kill the sand demons." She turned to her sisters and saw that they already had plans to free the sand demons.

Thankfully, glass is formed from the Earth Element, and sand is a component of it, so Enzi could free the people by turning the sand into glass. In fact, she had already started preparing from the very moment they attacked the Blood Sand Berserker.
They all wanted the sand demons to be freed, so making sure it happened safely was their priority now.
Enzi had anticipated the possibility of the Blood Sand Berserker breaking free from the Glass Domain and attacking the sand demons, so she had created many contingencies just in case.
"Let me begin."
She placed her palm on the ground and started transforming the sand into glass.
Meanwhile, deep underground, inside a city built from nothing but stone and earth, thousands of sand demons sat with pale expressions.
Looking up at what could be considered the clouds, they saw that thousands of cracks had formed across them. Under normal circumstances, they wouldn’t have had to worry.
However, they were aware that they had been imprisoned several meters underground, so these cracks weren’t a good sign for any of them.
They knew it would end in deaths, so they started to panic.
Those proficient in the Sand Element stood guard, hoping to prevent thousands from dying. At the very least, if this place collapsed, they planned to save a few thousand sand demons.

However, as the cracks continued to spread, their panic reached a new level. The children cried their hearts out while their mothers did everything they could to calm them, only to give them false hope.
They knew it was over for them, but they wouldn’t tell their children that—not beneath a collapsing mountain of earth.

Suddenly, the cracks stopped. Then, to everyone’s bewilderment, the clouds began turning into glass. In fact, those who had been panicking allowed themselves to be mesmerised for a few moments as the sky transformed into glass.
"What is happening?" some wondered, looking up at the sky that had almost completely turned to glass.
Soon, their questions were answered when the glass shattered. However, instead of falling on them, it began converging toward a single point before breaking into countless tiny fragments.
In no time, a large dark hole appeared in the sky, while the shattered glass had already reformed into several spheres of glass. Then the glass spheres floated upward and vanished from sight.
A few seconds later, three ladies appeared in the air and gazed down at the thousands of stunned sand demons.
"Hello, everyone. We hope we didn’t scare you too much," Liora said, prompting some of the elder sand demons to take flight and appear a few meters away from the ladies.
Seeing their hostile expressions, the three ladies smiled, and Enzi spoke.
"Relax. We have already killed the Blood Sand Berserker, so you are free to leave this place."
Hearing what Enzi said, they all widened their eyes.
"Really?" one of the sand demon elders asked, and the three ladies nodded.
"You can go and check if you’re in doubt. We received your distress signal, so we came to your aid. That said, with your homes destroyed, where do you intend to go now?"

The elders were grateful, but the three ladies could tell from the looks on their faces that they had no idea what to do. Before the Blood Sand Berserker came and imprisoned them, there had been about thirteen million sand demons in their tribe.
However, now they had fewer than ten million left, a clear indication of how many sand demons had been devoured by the Blood Sand Berserker.
So while they were sand demons and would have loved to remain in the desert, their last five years of suffering had traumatised them to the point that they no longer had the will to live here.
What if another Blood Sand Berserker appeared?
That question made them all hesitate.
"You know, we have a place where we can take your people to live in peace and harmony for the rest of their lives. If you wish, we can bring you there—that is, if you are willing."
The elder sand demons turned to look at their people before making a decision.
"We will discuss it with them first, and if they are willing, we will tell you our decision."

Enzi and her sisters had no problem with that. To them, if these sand demons chose to go with them, it would simply mean adding more souls to the tower, thereby further increasing their man’s growing strength.
At the end of the day, the tower was free for anyone to live in, and everything was run using Tower Points.
Of course, with the growing population living there now, Gaia had introduced Spirit Stones to facilitate buying and selling among the various races.
So, regardless of the circumstances they found themselves in, they would be welcomed and given the chance to live in peace for years to come.
