chapters.title: Chapter 1745: World Core Crystal
paragraphs: It took the sand demon elders some time to convince everyone to accept the offer Enzi and her sisters had made. They knew that living in the desert was no longer an option.
They had been through so much that many of them were traumatized. So if there was a place where they could live out the rest of their lives without danger, they would gladly accept it.

Still, some were skeptical, which was only natural. They had just escaped from the Blood Sand Berserker, so what if the place they were being taken to was just another prison where they would become food for another hungry beast?
The three ladies addressed their concerns by taking ten representatives into the tower and showing them around the city where they would be living.
It wasn’t a desert city but one built from bricks and pure earth. Gaia and her subordinates had worked tirelessly over the past few years, so there were already three cities waiting to be occupied.
Gaia’s vision of a [erfect world inside the tower was slowly being built by her, and one of the spaces would be for the Sand demons.

Of course, given the kind of lives the sand demons had endured over the years, Enzi promised them that within less than five months, they would have a desert-inspired city ready if they wished for such a setting.
For now, however, they could stay in this one.
The ten representatives were overjoyed. So when they returned to the outside world, they had nothing but praise for what they had seen. In the end, the entire tribe agreed to the relocation.
Enzi and her sisters immediately began moving the sand demons into the tower city.
But while that was happening, the auction had entered its final rounds. Already, over twenty items had been sold, leaving only four more to go.

Over the past couple of hours, one treasure after another had been auctioned. None had caught Kent’s attention. However, Flura placed bids on a few herbs and successfully won the ones she truly needed.
Aside from that, despite a few ores being put up for auction, Kent left them to the blacksmiths, especially Lady Khronisia.
Of course, every last item auctioned would be good materials for upgrading the Lost Knights.
However, Kent had no intention of using ordinary materials to upgrade his knights. He only wanted the best, so he let the likes of Lady Khronisia win those bids instead.
Right now, another armor set from the Chaos Era was up for bidding, and considering its value and usefulness, everyone wanted it.

The price had already reached 50 trillion, yet none of them was willing to back down. They all wanted it, so the bidding continued for another forty minutes before the final bid of 135 trillion was placed.

In the end, the armor found its new owner, and with that, the twenty-second item was brought onto the stage. The moment the glass chamber housing the item was revealed, everyone shifted in their seats.
"A World Core Crystal," Kent muttered, his eyes sparkling.
And he wasn’t the only one. Everyone present had their gaze locked onto the crystal.
"This is the World Core Crystal, which I believe all of you have already recognized," the auctioneer said.
Everyone nodded.

"Kent, what is this World Core Crystal?" Elina asked, resting her head on Vexthra’s shoulder. The rest of her sisters were still playing with the Dragon Rod, but she chose to remain by her big sister’s side for now.
Kent looked at her and smiled.
"It is a Crystal formed when a world experiences a natural death. Some worlds, both inhabited and uninhabited, perish for various reasons.
Some die due to harsh conditions, while others die due to intense battles that have happened on it in the past.

However, before they die, they condense their essence and laws into what you are looking at. Contained within this World Core Crystal are the very laws of nature that the planet had comprehended—the Laws of Creation, Life, Death, and many more.
When used to refine weapons, the likelihood of the weapon inheriting the laws contained within the crystal is extremely high. In fact, most law-infused weapons were forged using World Core Crystals."
"Then it sounds like it would be perfect for what you have in mind," Elina said, and Kent nodded.
"It would indeed be perfect. After all, refining battle dolls is no different from refining weapons, and I happen to be one of the greatest blacksmiths to ever walk the face of the universe."
The girls laughed, knowing that while many would dismiss it as bragging, he truly was the legendary Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith who had once dominated the world of blacksmithing.
"I suppose you will be buying it," Pandora asked.
Yet again, Kent nodded.
"It is a perfect addition to the Heaven’s Breath Crystal. Those two alone will do for now... Of course, if another one appears, I’ll bid for it as well. But these two are enough for the time being."
The ladies knew he had to focus, so they pulled away, allowing him to prepare for the bidding war that was about to unfold.
"Since we all know how valuable World Core Crystals are, you should also know that this one came from a God World. This also means it contains traces of divine essence."
The VIP rooms immediately became lively. Everyone wanted it even more than they had wanted the Heaven’s Breath Crystal.

"The starting bid is set at 10 trillion Spirit Stones, with a minimum increment of 2 trillion Spirit Stones per bid. I will reiterate that this is an auction, so refrain from using your background to threaten anyone."
Everyone nodded.
"The bidding starts now."
"20 trillion!"
"30 trillion!"
"35 trillion!"
In an instant, the price soared as everyone rushed to place their bids. In fact, over sixty percent of the thousands of attendees were actively bidding.
Kent remained seated, as none of this concerned him. He was simply waiting for the small fries to exhaust their funds before making his move.

Inside the various VIP rooms, those he had already identified as truly wealthy also remained silent for now. The bidding war had only just begun, and with three more items still left to be auctioned, many knew this was their best opportunity to secure at least one treasure.
Auctions could never satisfy everyone.
Some were destined to come, try their best, and leave without winning a single bid, while others would walk away with multiple treasures and leave with satisfied hearts.

So while the big dogs remained silent, the chatterboxes were having the time of their lives, making sure that after today, they would at least be able to brag that they had once come close to winning the bid for a World Core Crystal.
The bidding continued relentlessly for another thirty minutes before many people finally started backing out.
Just then, the fatty inside VIP Room 79 made his move—or rather, had the slave lady place the bid on his behalf.
"250 trillion."
It was a massive leap from the previous bid of 170 trillion.
The moment his bid echoed throughout the auction hall, Kent could hear people gritting their teeth even from the VIP rooms he had been monitoring.
Perhaps many who had watched the fatty purchase one treasure after another had assumed he had finally run out of money, and so he wouldn’t bid on this.
However, that wasn’t the case at all.
The bastard was still loaded.
But there was someone even wealthier than he was, and that person had already marked him for death.
"300 trillion."
Kent finally placed his first bid.

chapters.title: Chapter 1746: Threat Wrapped in a Beautiful Compliment
paragraphs: "320 trillion."
The lady increased the bid again, causing Kent to furrow his brow.
"350 trillion."
He increased it as well, hoping the fatty would finally back down. However, he was clearly determined to have the World Core Crystal for himself.
This made Kent wonder just who the man was and why he needed something that perhaps only an alchemist or a blacksmith would have any proper use for.
Looking at his stature, it was plain as day that he was neither an alchemist nor a blacksmith, so why did he need it?
Most of the people who fought over it had a tangible use for it, so Kent had no reason to wonder why they were bidding. However, this one clearly didn’t fit either role.

Of course, Kent knew the universe was vast, and what worked for one person might not work for another. He also knew the World Core Crystal could be used for other purposes, so he had no reason to doubt the man.
In that case, since the man clearly had a use for the World Core Crystal, Kent wasn’t about to concern himself with what others needed it for.
The bid continued to climb for a few minutes before Kent finally had enough and decided to use one of his trump cards—his extensive wealth.
"500 trillion."
He raised the bid from 350 trillion to 500 trillion, and everyone in the auction hall gasped at once.

The increase was massive, something many hadn’t expected to see in this year’s auction, at least not for the twenty-second item. The previous Mega Auction had ended with the final item selling for 400 trillion.

Even then, many had wondered why someone would spend that much on a piece of fabric. However, the fabric auctioned off for the last item in that auction was woven from the reverse scale of the infamous Primordial Chaos Dragon.

Its sentimental value far surpassed that of most treasures, so a price of 400 trillion was understandable. However, while World Core Crystals weren’t that common, they weren’t exactly impossible to obtain.
After all, it was common knowledge that wherever a massive battle broke out, the world involved usually died much faster.
So, obtaining a World Core Crystal was far more likely than getting a piece of fabric made from the scales of the Chaos Dragon.
In their opinion, Kent had gone too far, and even Lady Wu couldn’t help but nod.
She knew Kent had the money to pay, but she hadn’t expected him to go that far.
But it worked.
The fatty didn’t place another bid after Kent raised it to 500 trillion. However, a lazy voice came from his room a few seconds later.
"Young man, you really are something, huh?" he laughed before adding, "It is your win this time, young man. I’m sure the next one will be mine."
He had already won five items, so saying that sounded shameless. However, Kent simply smiled and replied,

"At the end of the day, it’s all about who ends up owning the items they bid for. But I will commend your interest in treasures of great value. I can tell you’re someone who appreciates priceless things."
"That I am. I have quite a collection of them. I am sure I will add even more after this auction."
Many gritted their teeth when they heard what the man said. Clearly, he was a collector, and to most people, that was the worst kind of profession to pursue.
Those people bought items of great value and importance only to place them in display cases for their own amusement.
Strangely, most collectors are extremely rich—so rich, in fact, that they could dominate auctions from start to finish.
Kent smiled and gave him a rather insightful reply.

"You know what they say—the journey of a man ends when he no longer has the willpower to hold on to his dignity. Sometimes, they cross over to the next plane before they even realize it. You, sir, are someone who knows how to carry yourself, and you even conceded to a youngster such as myself. I will repay you thirteenfold when the time comes."
"I will take you up on that, Kent Madson."
Kent grinned and replied, "Trust me, I don’t break my promises."
His wives shook their heads, knowing the man was as good as dead. To them, everything Kent had just said was a threat wrapped in a beautiful compliment.
He intended to kill the man who had dared take the feisty wife from his past incarnation as a slave.

Had it not been for his wives sitting him down and making sure he thought things through before attacking, he would have already killed the man. However, he managed to keep his anger just beneath the surface.

Right now, he had merely told the man what he intended to do to him. In essence, the man clearly didn’t know he had offended a very dangerous barbarian who was also a dragon, as well as a Blood and Evil Cultivator.
"He is dead," Yukiko muttered, shaking her head.
Meanwhile, on the stage, seeing that there were no more bids coming in, Lady Wu announced Kent as the winner. Yet again, Kent said he would be paying after the auction.
Before introducing the twenty-third item, Lady Wu addressed everyone first.
"We are finally down to the last three items. At the last Brown Maple Mega Auction, the final three items were all wearables. We fought over the Grim Reaper Hood, a relic from the Primordial Era.

We also fought over the Six-Eyed Water Demon King’s Necklace, a relic from the Dark Era, and finally, we witnessed the intense bidding war for the breastplate made from the reverse scales of the Primordial Chaos Dragon.
It was a wild ride. However, the event ended on a good note for everyone.
I am happy to announce that this auction will witness the sale of three legendary elemental techniques, each estimated to be at the rank of Pseudo-Primordial."
Gasps.
Everyone, including Kent, gasped. He clearly hadn’t expected this, and his previous assumption that the auction was essentially over had just been thrown out the window.
’I need to win one of these techniques and merge it with Divine Flame Armament.’

His eyes sparkled as he thought about the technique he planned to use in his next mission. It was something he had created by merging several flame techniques he had learned during the Flame Tower trial back on Sonox.
Back then, he hadn’t possessed enough flame essence to wield the Primordial-grade Finger of Destruction, so he had created Divine Flame Armament as his go-to technique.
However, after recovering most of his memories, he realized that Divine Flame Armament had tremendous potential. He even speculated that it could be pushed to the Primordial rank.
However, improving it would require many techniques. Thankfully, he was about to see what the auction had in store for him.
Soon, the next item was brought out—an ice technique meant for mages. Kent asked his wives if they wanted it, but they declined, so he didn’t place a bid.
Someone won it for a staggering 350 trillion spirit stones.
The second was an earth-element technique that sold for 370 trillion. He didn’t bid on that either, since it wasn’t something he wanted.
Then the final item was brought out, and the moment its name was announced, his eyes widened.
"Up next is the second form of the infamous Finger of Destruction technique."

chapters.title: Chapter 1747: Finger of Destruction Second Form
paragraphs: Kent would be lying if he said he wasn’t surprised by the appearance of the second form of the [Finger of Destruction] technique in this auction.
He had received the first form from Flame Lord Agni, one of the legendary Flame Lords of the Immortal Realm.
From what Agni had told him before handing over the technique, the Finger of Destruction first appeared in a ruin said to date back to the Primordial Era.

Back then, all seven forms of the technique were revealed on a single tome, meant for one person. However, since everyone wanted it, an extremely chaotic battle erupted, and thousands lost their lives.
In the end, the tome containing the technique shattered into seven pieces, each falling into the hands of a different person.
Agni was one of the fortunate few to obtain a fragment. Fortunately for him, he escaped with his life, but in the end, he wasn’t able to cultivate it.

Even so, he became the most wanted man in the entire Immortal Realm and beyond. After the ruin closed, it was soon discovered that he possessed the first form of the technique, leaving those who had obtained the remaining forms unable to cultivate theirs.
Of course, despite lacking the ability to cultivate the original technique, they were still able to create legendary techniques based on it.
In fact, many Celestials alive today have created terrifying techniques inspired by the nature of the remaining forms of the [Finger of Destruction].
Kent possessed the first form, and he had always planned to obtain the second.
The last he had heard, the second form of the [Finger of Destruction] was in the possession of the Flame Demon Clan.
Their ancestor, already a Celestial, was present when the original tome shattered. He had obtained the second form, and ever since then, the clan had guarded it as one of their greatest treasures.
They had benefited immensely from it, and after years of countless experts trying to seize the technique, those attempts eventually stopped.
Every decade, new talents were born within the Flame Demon Clan, each exceptionally proficient in the Flame Element.
It reached the point where many people resorted to currying favor with the Flame Demon Clan just for the chance to catch a glimpse of the technique.

Unlike Agni, who had no backing—especially considering that even his fellow Flame Lords had hunted him relentlessly—the Flame Demon Clan had thousands of powerful warriors standing behind them. As a result, no one dared stir up trouble.
So for them to put such a precious technique up for auction...
Kent, in all his expectations, never expected them to do such a thing, and he certainly hadn’t expected it to appear at this auction.
But it was here now, and as someone whose next mission would take him to one of the most dangerous places in the universe, he knew obtaining it would greatly increase his chances of survival.
"I need to get this technique no matter what," he muttered, clenching his fist.

The mission he would soon undertake would lead him to a unique world known as Flame Paradise. The name sounded peaceful, but the horrors hidden within were far more terrifying than words could describe.

Ironically, Agni—the very man who had given Kent the first form of the Finger of Destruction—had found himself trapped there after being hunted down by numerous clans and the Flame Temple itself, the very organization to which he had once sworn eternal allegiance to protect the Flame Dao.
He needed to rescue him, and Kent also needed to form his third Flame Core and recover one of the Nirvana Flames he possessed.
While inside, he would only be able to use flame-type techniques, so his plan was to strengthen [Divine Flame Armament], since he was likely to encounter Gods, Supremes, and even Celestials there.
Now, it appeared he would be getting his hands on the second form of the [Finger of Destruction], which, in his opinion, would be more than enough for what he had planned.
"Sounds like this technique is impressive," Yukiko said as she looked at Kent.
"It is one of the greatest flame-type techniques in the universe. I already have the first form. Now, if I win the bid for this one, I’ll be getting my hands on the second."
"Go ahead, then. If you don’t have enough money, we’ll sponsor you," Vexthra assured him.
Kent merely smiled and nodded. He had already taken all of his previous purchases into account, and even after that, he was still incredibly wealthy.
’Tower, do you think we can go all out this time around?’

[Master clearly has no idea how much a 2% stake in an empire like the Brown Maple Auction House is worth after more than 370,000 years have passed. You possess so many spirit stones that you could buy dozens of the items you’ve already purchased without even noticing a dent in your wealth.]
Kent grinned.
To him, it had only been a few years since he had last seen his friends from the Pill World. However, his shares in the Brown Maple Auction House had been maturing for over 370,000 years.
The Brown Maple Auction House had long since reached its golden age, causing the value of his shares to soar to an unprecedented level.
’Then let’s go all out,’ Kent said before turning his attention back to the auction.

"The Flame Demon Clan has held on to the second form of the Finger of Destruction technique for countless years. However, after benefiting from it for so long, they have decided to auction it off so that the next fortunate person—or people—may also enjoy it."
Lady Wu smiled as she repeated exactly what she had been instructed to say when the technique was entrusted to her to be auctioned.
She knew those words sounded extremely shameless. However, she had nothing better to say than the script she had been given.
As expected, many people sneered, yet they remained determined to win the technique.

As for Kent, he knew the Flame Demon Clan had already made several copies of the technique before putting the original up for auction. After all, while replicating such a technique could take thousands of years, it wasn’t impossible.
So, the fact that they were willing to sell it meant they no longer had any real need for it and simply wanted to cash out.
"The starting bid is 50 trillion, with a minimum increment of 5 trillion."
She paused and slowly scanned the room, allowing the anticipation in the air to build.
"May the highest bidder win."
And so, the bidding war began.

Everyone jumped in immediately. Kent, however, held back and began observing the various VIP rooms. He was well aware that several influential figures hadn’t participated in the auction at all since it began, so he wasn’t about to reveal himself just yet.
Time passed, and before long, the bid had reached 300 trillion.
Just then, for the first time since the auction had begun, the occupant of VIP Room 99 placed a bid—and it was a shocking one.
"400 trillion."
The entire auction hall fell silent the moment the bid was announced.

Perhaps Kent, who had no idea who this person was, would be the only one to go against her. However, the thousands of people gathered in the hall recognized the voice immediately, and almost all of them backed down.
Even the fatty in VIP Room 79 did the same.
"This voice..." Vexthra muttered, narrowing her eyes.
A few seconds later, her eyes widened, and for the briefest moment, an icy aura escaped from her body.

chapters.title: Chapter 1748: A Primal God
paragraphs: Vexthra’s expression made Kent wonder why she looked so stunned and a bit shaken. The Vexthra he knew didn’t scare easily, so seeing her with that expression told him something wasn’t right.
"Vexthra, is everything alright?" he asked, holding back his bid for now.
"Not sure just yet, but I think the person who placed that bid may be from the Primal Temple," she replied, narrowing her gaze further at VIP room 99.
"The Primal Temple?" Kent asked, his brow furrowing. This was the first time he had heard such a name, leaving him slightly stunned.
In response, Vexthra revealed what she knew.

"From what I know, the Primal Temple is a secret organization that dates back to the Primordial Era. They are said to be beings who have crossed the 100th layer in every ascension. They possess unfathomable power, and the person who spoke sounded like the Mystery Shadow Assassin Primal God"

Kent frowned, stunned by what he had just heard. He had never heard of the Primal Temple before, but he had heard of the Arcane Order. From what he knew, they too were beings who had crossed the undisputed 100th layer.
In fact, he had fought many of them during both the Primordial and Divine Eras, and he is sure he fought them in some of his other incarnations.

During those eras, they had been traitors—beings who sought the end of the universe. They were the beings who opened the Void Gate and unleashed the Void Beasts upon the universe, leading to the Great War.
He didn’t know whether the Arcane Order and the Primal Temple were one and the same, but he didn’t like anything he had just heard. In fact, his killing intent began to leak, startling his wives.
"What is wrong, Kent?" Pandora asked.
Instead of replying, Kent turned toward the auction stage and raised the bid.
"420 trillion."
HMMM
From VIP room 99, the person who had placed the 400-trillion bid let out a low growl but said nothing. Throughout the auction hall, many had gone pale.
"Is Kent Madson insane? How does he dare go against someone from the Primal Temple?"
The few who recognized the lady in VIP room 99 began whispering among themselves, making Kent, already enraged by past memories, narrow his eyes.
"Kent, dear, you do know that Primal Gods aren’t affected by the world’s limitations. This means this person still possesses her god-level strength even in the Immortal Realm," Vexthra cautioned.
Kent merely smirked.
"Is that supposed to make me afraid?" he asked, clenching his fist as his teeth ground together.
"I don’t know if they’re the same people I’ve been hunting down throughout all my incarnations, but if she happens to be one of them, then she isn’t leaving the Immortal Realm today."
The ladies could tell he was furious, so none of them tried to stop him.
Instead, they all went on high alert because for someone to make Kent this angry meant they had done something unforgivable—something that had crossed his bottom line.
"The bid stands at 420 trillion. Are there any higher bids?" Lady Wu announced.
Nobody made a sound.
A few moments later, she sighed and declared the winner.
"Since there are no further bids, the item goes to the gentleman in VIP room 13."
Almost instantly, a suffocating killing intent filled the auction hall, followed by an icy voice that sent a chill down everyone’s spine.

"Kent Madson, I have heard a lot about you, but I have to say, meeting you has been a disappointment. Refusing to give face to a senior such as myself is an insult to me and to everything I represent."
Suddenly, a powerful finger materialized above the auction hall and hovered in the air.
"Which is why I will be killing you today."
Kent smirked and was about to move when Pandora and the rest of her sisters held him back.
"Think this through, Kent. She has already crossed the 100th layer and possesses true Dao Essence."
Kent narrowed his eyes at the ladies before smiling.
"Relax, ladies. I just want to check something first. As long as she isn’t the person I’m looking for, I’ll let her live."
"Huh? We meant you should be scared for your life," Vexthra and her sisters said, clearly never expecting Kent to claim he would spare a Primal God when he was the one in danger.
Vexthra had reached the 65th layer during her god ascension, yet even that alone made her one of the most dangerous Domain Gods in the universe.
Someone who had crossed the 100th layer was not to be underestimated.
Kent merely smiled before vanishing from the VIP room, reappearing above the auction hall. It was there that he finally came face-to-face with the person who had threatened to kill him.
She was a Universal God with dark eyes and long pink hair. Her lean body was clad in form-fitting leather armor that hugged every curve, revealing her to be an assassin-type god.
A single glance was all Kent needed to realize that recklessness would only get him killed.
Yet instead of attacking, he smiled and asked a question that instantly changed everything.

"The Hall of Primordial Gods recorded that during the golden age of the Primordial Era, a group of gods who had seen beyond the 99th layer decided to rule the universe, so they made contact with a Doomsday Lord.
"Their request was granted, giving rise to the Forsaken Race. They called themselves the Arcane Order, and they became the true enemies of the universe."
His eyes narrowed.
"What is the difference between the Arcane Order and the Primal Temple?"
The Universal God’s eyes narrowed as well, and waves of killing intent poured from her body.
Seeing that reaction, Kent smiled.
His cloak transformed into golden, crimson, and black dragon armor. He extended his hand, and his jagged broadsword, Gaap, materialized within his grasp.

"So that is how it is, huh? You evil fiends infected the universe, created the Soul Temple, and corrupted the Universe Order and Council from the shadows. Then, after gathering enough strength, you dared to rebrand yourselves into... what exactly?"
A talon-like dragon tail emerged behind him, radiating deadly intent.
"You... who are you, and how do you know all this?" the Universal God asked as she summoned two daggers. "You know what? Don’t tell me. I’ll kill you before you even get the chance to answer."
Seated in VIP room 13, Pandora smiled and snapped her fingers, creating a transparent barrier enclosing Kent and the Universal God assassin.
Kent smiled before his expression turned ice-cold.
"If I can’t kill you within ten minutes, I’ll offer you my head for free."
The moment those words left his mouth, golden-crimson lightning erupted from his body.
Then he vanished.
The next instant, he appeared behind the assassin, who went by the name Xylarahi. She sidestepped before Kent’s sword could reach her.
However, just as she thought she had seized the movement to attack, Kent’s dragon tail whipped behind him like a razor-sharp blade and lashed toward her.
Her right dagger shot up to intercept it.
BOOM!!
The collision blasted her backward, sending her crashing through countless buildings.
"Die!"
Kent roared as he moved once more, his lightning element fueling both his speed and power. Although he was only an Immortal Monarch, he was actually overwhelming a Universal God.
Pandora had already prepared a battlefield for them.
By creating a perfect replica of the city and overlaying it onto reality, she made it appear as though buildings were being destroyed, when in truth, the real city remained completely untouched.

sentences.text: Vexthra’s expression made Kent wonder why she looked so stunned and a bit shaken.
The Vexthra he knew didn’t scare easily, so seeing her with that expression told him something wasn’t right.
"Vexthra, is everything alright?" he asked, holding back his bid for now.
"Not sure just yet, but I think the person who placed that bid may be from the Primal Temple," she replied, narrowing her gaze further at VIP room 99.
"The Primal Temple?" Kent asked, his brow furrowing.
This was the first time he had heard such a name, leaving him slightly stunned.
In response, Vexthra revealed what she knew.
"From what I know, the Primal Temple is a secret organization that dates back to the Primordial Era.
They are said to be beings who have crossed the 100th layer in every ascension.
They possess unfathomable power, and the person who spoke sounded like the Mystery Shadow Assassin Primal God"
Kent frowned, stunned by what he had just heard.
He had never heard of the Primal Temple before, but he had heard of the Arcane Order.
From what he knew, they too were beings who had crossed the undisputed 100th layer.
In fact, he had fought many of them during both the Primordial and Divine Eras, and he is sure he fought them in some of his other incarnations.
During those eras, they had been traitors—beings who sought the end of the universe.
They were the beings who opened the Void Gate and unleashed the Void Beasts upon the universe, leading to the Great War.
He didn’t know whether the Arcane Order and the Primal Temple were one and the same, but he didn’t like anything he had just heard.
In fact, his killing intent began to leak, startling his wives.
"What is wrong, Kent?" Pandora asked.
Instead of replying, Kent turned toward the auction stage and raised the bid.
"420 trillion."
HMMM
From VIP room 99, the person who had placed the 400-trillion bid let out a low growl but said nothing.
Throughout the auction hall, many had gone pale.
"Is Kent Madson insane?
How does he dare go against someone from the Primal Temple?"
The few who recognized the lady in VIP room 99 began whispering among themselves, making Kent, already enraged by past memories, narrow his eyes.
"Kent, dear, you do know that Primal Gods aren’t affected by the world’s limitations.
This means this person still possesses her god-level strength even in the Immortal Realm," Vexthra cautioned.
Kent merely smirked.
"Is that supposed to make me afraid?" he asked, clenching his fist as his teeth ground together.
"I don’t know if they’re the same people I’ve been hunting down throughout all my incarnations, but if she happens to be one of them, then she isn’t leaving the Immortal Realm today."
The ladies could tell he was furious, so none of them tried to stop him.
Instead, they all went on high alert because for someone to make Kent this angry meant they had done something unforgivable—something that had crossed his bottom line.
"The bid stands at 420 trillion.
Are there any higher bids?" Lady Wu announced.
Nobody made a sound.
A few moments later, she sighed and declared the winner.
"Since there are no further bids, the item goes to the gentleman in VIP room 13."
Almost instantly, a suffocating killing intent filled the auction hall, followed by an icy voice that sent a chill down everyone’s spine.
"Kent Madson, I have heard a lot about you, but I have to say, meeting you has been a disappointment.
Refusing to give face to a senior such as myself is an insult to me and to everything I represent."
Suddenly, a powerful finger materialized above the auction hall and hovered in the air.
"Which is why I will be killing you today."
Kent smirked and was about to move when Pandora and the rest of her sisters held him back.
"Think this through, Kent.
She has already crossed the 100th layer and possesses true Dao Essence."
Kent narrowed his eyes at the ladies before smiling.
"Relax, ladies.
I just want to check something first.
As long as she isn’t the person I’m looking for, I’ll let her live."
"Huh?
We meant you should be scared for your life," Vexthra and her sisters said, clearly never expecting Kent to claim he would spare a Primal God when he was the one in danger.
Vexthra had reached the 65th layer during her god ascension, yet even that alone made her one of the most dangerous Domain Gods in the universe.
Someone who had crossed the 100th layer was not to be underestimated.
Kent merely smiled before vanishing from the VIP room, reappearing above the auction hall.
It was there that he finally came face-to-face with the person who had threatened to kill him.
She was a Universal God with dark eyes and long pink hair.
Her lean body was clad in form-fitting leather armor that hugged every curve, revealing her to be an assassin-type god.
A single glance was all Kent needed to realize that recklessness would only get him killed.
Yet instead of attacking, he smiled and asked a question that instantly changed everything.

"The Hall of Primordial Gods recorded that during the golden age of the Primordial Era, a group of gods who had seen beyond the 99th layer decided to rule the universe, so they made contact with a Doomsday Lord.
"Their request was granted, giving rise to the Forsaken Race.
They called themselves the Arcane Order, and they became the true enemies of the universe."
His eyes narrowed.
"What is the difference between the Arcane Order and the Primal Temple?"

Seeing that reaction, Kent smiled.

chapters.title: Chapter 1749: Killing A Primal God
paragraphs: Xylarahi steadied herself before the last building could collapse on top of her. With a flick of both daggers, countless crimson slashes erupted outward, reducing the surrounding structures to dust.
Her expression turned grave. She had not expected a mere Immortal Monarch to wield such overwhelming strength.
"This strength..."

She stared at Kent, no longer looking at him as an Immortal Monarch but as a monster capable of threatening her life. She had reached the 105th layer during her God Ascension Trial, so being sent crashing through buildings was a blatant insult.
"No wonder you dared provoke the Primal Temple."
Kent rested Gaap on his shoulder and smirked.
"I didn’t provoke you," Kent muttered coldly.
His purple-red eyes gleamed with murderous intent. He was now certain that the Primal Temple was, or once had been, the Arcane Order. The realization only fueled his anger.

The Forsaken Race had always been his number one enemy during the primordial era. However, after learning that the ones responsible for their arrival and rise throughout the universe were the Arcane Order, he abandoned his pursuit of the Forsaken Race and turned his attention to hunting down the Arcane Order instead.
It was then that Adina’s incarnation stepped in, sealing the Forsaken Race on thousands of planets and casting them into the space-time continuum.
"You people have been on my kill list for a very, very long time."
BOOOM!
Without another word, Xylarahi disappeared.

The world around Kent suddenly fell silent. It was as if he were the only person left in existence. Then, the space around him warped, and thousands of killing intents, each fashioned into a tiny dagger, materialized and attacked.
Kent glanced around and snorted.
He waited for the daggers to close in. Then, with a single step, he vanished, leaving behind only a blurry afterimage and crackling bolts of lightning.
"ARCH!"
The next second, his sword pierced through Xylarahi’s shoulder.

She coughed up blood and instantly retreated, pushing her speed to its absolute limit. She had both seen and felt what had happened, and she knew Kent had been aiming for her heart had she not reacted in the last second.
However, what truly baffled her was how Kent had escaped her Dagger Intent.
She had used that skill thousands of times, and every opponent who faced it had fallen—not because they were weak, but because they instinctively tried to defend against the daggers.
Attempting to defend against the daggers was the true attack.
The daggers were formed from killing intent, and the only way to defend against them was with another killing intent.

The moment the daggers surrounded Kent, the entire space around him had been sealed, locking him inside. The only way to escape the encirclement was to possess killing intent that vastly surpassed her own.
Despite it all, Kent had walked out of it as though it didn’t exist.
That was even more shocking than the wound in her shoulder.
"H-How..."
Disbelief filled her face.
"How do you possess more killing intent than a god?"
Kent lowered his sword and replied calmly,
"Lady, I was slaughtering demons and dragons long before your ancestors were born."
Kent released only 5% of his killing intent.
At once, the protective bubble Pandora had created began to crack.
Inside the VIP room, Pandora narrowed her eyes in disbelief. Forming a hand seal, she immediately reinforced the barrier, sealing every fracture before it could spread.
"Interesting."

By all standards, she is a Primordial, so the Immortal World’s suppression did not affect her like it did the rest of her sisters. Even so, she was baffled to see her containment crack after Kent released just a fraction of his killing intent.
To everyone watching, a dark, cloaked figure holding a crimson scythe now stood behind Kent.
The sight filled everyone with fear deep within their bones.
"Now die."

Kent moved, and the overwhelming killing intent radiating from him moved with him. The moment he arrived before Xylarahi, she tried to evade, but Kent was already upon her. His tail pierced her other shoulder while his sword swept toward her left hand.
She raised her dagger to block, but it was as though nothing stood in the sword’s path. The dagger was severed in half, and the blade continued into her shoulder, carving a deep wound.
Kent’s tail lashed out, sending Xylarahi flying.
Before she could even land, Kent’s foot slammed into her spine.
BANG!

The kick sent her hurtling away once more, blood pouring from her mouth. Kent then raised his sword and slashed downward, causing bolts of crimson lightning to descend violently and strike Xylarahi squarely in the chest.
The impact buried her into the ground, a hissing sound escaping from her mouth and nose.

"Just because you climbed a few hundred layers, you think you’ve earned the right to brag while standing before me?" he sneered, calmly walking toward the broken woman who had clearly overestimated her own strength.
In her opinion, a place like the Immortal Realm could never pose a threat to her. After all, as a Universal God, even hundreds of Demigods would struggle to face her.
However, she had now realized the error of her thinking.
The one who claimed to be the strongest in the universe had today encountered someone even stronger.

In truth, the so-called layer hierarchy of the Primal Temple—the very achievement they constantly flaunted as proof of their superiority—were something Chaos had already conquered during his own ascension to godhood.
Once a cultivator reached the 100th layer, they became aware of hidden truths about cultivation and were bestowed a unique cultivation technique by the Dao.
It is mostly focused on the path they walked.
Chaos had witnessed the path beyond the Dao, the path that led to the Origin.
That single encounter had changed his life forever, transforming him into one of the greatest warriors to ever exist.
So, in his eyes, the path beyond the 100th layer was indeed extraordinary.
But those standing before him were insignificant.

The memories of his past lives had already begun shaping him into someone truly worthy to be fear. Had he not yet recovered the memories of the Nine Underworld Flame Blacksmith, perhaps he might have struggled a little.

Instead, he had relived his life in Hell and witnessed the thousands of battles he had fought within the Damnation Arena. He had experienced firsthand how completely Fjorge had immersed himself in killing intent and the martial arts.
Combined with the memories of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, Lord Genesis, the Ruthless Bandit, and several other incarnations, Kent had become someone who was nearly untouchable.

"Your arrogance was your downfall, lady. A true Universal God with refined battle arts would have pushed me much harder. But choosing to fight me using nothing but killing intent was your greatest mistake.
"Now I get to kill you and rid this universe of one less traitor."
Kent struck without the slightest hesitation.
Xylarahi’s head separated cleanly from her body.
Just like that, a Universal God had fallen.
Everyone present could only gasp in horror.
Kent had killed a Primal God in less than three minutes.
As shocking as that was, what terrified them even more was that he had done so knowing exactly where she came from.
Panic began to spread through the crowd. The Primal Temple will respond, and it would be devastating to watch...
Kent, however, simply stored away her corpse before returning to VIP Room 13 to answer the questions his wives had for him.

chapters.title: Chapter 1750: End Of the Auction
paragraphs: "So why did you kill her?" Veth asked the moment Kent returned to the VIP room.
"She is a member of my old enemies," Kent replied, taking a seat.
"During the Primordial Era, when I was waging war against the Forsaken Race, I discovered that the Forsaken Race didn’t appear on their own.
Somebody or some group of people brought them to this universe with the intention of using them to dominate and rule everything.

Later, when I researched further, I discovered that this group of people all came from an organization called the Arcane Order. Upon further investigation, I discovered they were beings who had surpassed the 100th layer during their god ascension and glimpsed the Dao.
At first, I held back my assault on them since I had no concrete justification to attack them. However, it soon became clear to me that they were far worse than I had thought.
After they failed with the Forsaken Race, they contacted the Void Race and even helped some of them cross over. That led me to abandon my assault on the Forsaken Race and focus on them instead.
I tried to rid the universe of them, but I guess here I am, still facing a much more evolved and bolder version of them. I have to purge them before they infest this universe on a much larger scale."
Vexthra sighed and smiled a little. "I am afraid you may be late on this one."

She looked at Kent critically and added, "The Primal Temple is one of the grandest organizations in the universe now. They have control over the God Realm, the Supreme Realm, and even the Celestial Realm."
"Hmmm," Kent hummed, his expression becoming even colder.

"You know, it took me a great deal of time to find out the true purpose behind their mission and vision. When I did, I was shaken to the core. However, even after spending years fighting them, I still failed. Now, it appears they have become much bigger."
He clenched his fist and sighed. "I have to become stronger."
His wives, knowing that all they could do at the moment was stand beside him, hugged him from all sides, making sure he felt their love.
Kent appreciated their kind gesture and allowed himself to calm down a bit.
However, his mind continued to consider the possibility that the events leading up to this auction weren’t a coincidence but an encounter arranged by fate.

Everything that had happened from the start of the auction to the end had been arranged. The minerals he had won would be used to upgrade the Lost Knights, who had actually fallen at the hands of the Arcane Order.

That battle had been a terrible one, and Kent, who knew how hard the Fourteen Lost Knights had fought, could tell from the very beginning that this auction had been arranged to make him aware of his past enemies and what must be done to rid this universe of their evil intent.
’The danger surrounding this universe now is just too great. I’d better start making moves to deal with some of it before it overwhelms me.’

He didn’t know what would happen next, but he could tell that he would soon have to go above and beyond just to keep his promise to all those who had lost their lives fighting in the Great War and every other war that had plagued the universe.
A few minutes later, Lady Wu’s voice spread throughout the auction hall, causing everyone who had been talking to fall silent.
"It appears this year’s auction has ended with a bang." A smile formed on her face, knowing that this event would spread far and wide and that the Brown Maple Auction House’s name would accompany it.
"While it didn’t end on the lightest note, I hope and trust that we all enjoyed ourselves, and I believe that 10,000 years from today, we will meet again for another mega auction event."
Everyone nodded.

"Then, on that note, I declare the end of this year’s Brown Maple Mega Auction. Thank you all for coming. Those who have bids to clear are invited to proceed to the various procurement sections to make their payments and collect their items."
The auction finally came to an end, and everyone started to leave.
"Ladies, time to head back," Kent said, and his wives nodded.
While they would have loved to stay by his side a little longer, they now understood that, with the auction over, they had to return to what they had been doing before coming to the auction with him.
They shared a round of kisses before leaving. Afterward, Kent, Veth, and Flura left their room and headed to the place where they would pay for the items they had won during the auction.
Meanwhile, inside VIP Room 79, the fatty, who had already paid for everything, stood up, still munching on some snacks, and lazily walked out of the room, followed by the slave girl.

The moment they stepped out of the room, a shadow moved and merged with the slave girl’s shadow. Kent didn’t know how many life-saving treasures the fatty possessed, so he instructed his shadow fiend to slip into the slave girl’s shadow instead.
Since they would be traveling together, it didn’t matter whose shadow had been infiltrated.
After walking for a few minutes, they arrived at a section of the auction house where a sleek-looking ship, built like a carriage house, was waiting.
This wasn’t a normal ship. It was connected to hundreds of universe channels, each of which this fatty was the owner and manager.
They boarded the ship, which looked much smaller from the outside but was as vast as a mansion on the inside. It even had a garden, along with chefs, maids, and guards working around the clock.

The fatty walked into a large dining hall where a lavish feast awaited him on a massive table, with maids standing by to replace his plates and refill his drink. Meanwhile, the slave girl walked into another building, entered a room, and let out a deep sigh.
After entering, she sat down and took another deep breath. She then began replaying the scenes from the auction in her mind.
After a while, she murmured a name.
"Kent Madson, huh?"

The image of Kent killing the Primal God flashed through her mind. However, as quickly as it appeared, it vanished. She knew that entertaining any thoughts concerning her master was nothing more than wishful thinking.
So she sighed and decided to focus on their next destination.

Then again, if she had paid closer attention to her shadow, she would have noticed another shadow slipping out of it and gliding silently across the vast mansion before passing through a window and making its way into the dining hall.
Meanwhile, outside, the ship slowly rose into the air. Before long, it disappeared into a universe channel and began traveling at a terrifying speed.

Nobody aboard the ship realized they had been infiltrated. Well, none of them expected a shadow fiend to exist in the universe when, according to everything they knew, all shadow fiends had long ago been sealed within the Shadow Realm.
Meanwhile, outside, Kent, Veth, and Flura were led straight to Lady Wu’s office, where she had been pacing back and forth before they arrived.
"Kent!"
She beam with joy and practically jumped into his arms the moment she saw him enter the room.

’The danger surrounding this universe now is just too great.
I’d better start making moves to deal with some of it before it overwhelms me.’

He didn’t know what would happen next, but he could tell that he would soon have to go above and beyond just to keep his promise to all those who had lost their lives fighting in the Great War and every other war that had plagued the universe.
A few minutes later, Lady Wu’s voice spread throughout the auction hall, causing everyone who had been talking to fall silent.
"It appears this year’s auction has ended with a bang." A smile formed on her face, knowing that this event would spread far and wide and that the Brown Maple Auction House’s name would accompany it.
"While it didn’t end on the lightest note, I hope and trust that we all enjoyed ourselves, and I believe that 10,000 years from today, we will meet again for another mega auction event."
Everyone nodded.
"Then, on that note, I declare the end of this year’s Brown Maple Mega Auction.
Thank you all for coming.
Those who have bids to clear are invited to proceed to the various procurement sections to make their payments and collect their items."
The auction finally came to an end, and everyone started to leave.
"Ladies, time to head back," Kent said, and his wives nodded.
While they would have loved to stay by his side a little longer, they now understood that, with the auction over, they had to return to what they had been doing before coming to the auction with him.
They shared a round of kisses before leaving.
Afterward, Kent, Veth, and Flura left their room and headed to the place where they would pay for the items they had won during the auction.
Meanwhile, inside VIP Room 79, the fatty, who had already paid for everything, stood up, still munching on some snacks, and lazily walked out of the room, followed by the slave girl.
The moment they stepped out of the room, a shadow moved and merged with the slave girl’s shadow.
Kent didn’t know how many life-saving treasures the fatty possessed, so he instructed his shadow fiend to slip into the slave girl’s shadow instead.
Since they would be traveling together, it didn’t matter whose shadow had been infiltrated.
After walking for a few minutes, they arrived at a section of the auction house where a sleek-looking ship, built like a carriage house, was waiting.
This wasn’t a normal ship.
It was connected to hundreds of universe channels, each of which this fatty was the owner and manager.
They boarded the ship, which looked much smaller from the outside but was as vast as a mansion on the inside.
It even had a garden, along with chefs, maids, and guards working around the clock.
The fatty walked into a large dining hall where a lavish feast awaited him on a massive table, with maids standing by to replace his plates and refill his drink.
Meanwhile, the slave girl walked into another building, entered a room, and let out a deep sigh.
After entering, she sat down and took another deep breath.
She then began replaying the scenes from the auction in her mind.
After a while, she murmured a name.
"Kent Madson, huh?"
The image of Kent killing the Primal God flashed through her mind.
However, as quickly as it appeared, it vanished.
She knew that entertaining any thoughts concerning her master was nothing more than wishful thinking.
So she sighed and decided to focus on their next destination.

Then again, if she had paid closer attention to her shadow, she would have noticed another shadow slipping out of it and gliding silently across the vast mansion before passing through a window and making its way into the dining hall.
Meanwhile, outside, the ship slowly rose into the air.
Before long, it disappeared into a universe channel and began traveling at a terrifying speed.
Nobody aboard the ship realized they had been infiltrated.
Well, none of them expected a shadow fiend to exist in the universe when, according to everything they knew, all shadow fiends had long ago been sealed within the Shadow Realm.
Meanwhile, outside, Kent, Veth, and Flura were led straight to Lady Wu’s office, where she had been pacing back and forth before they arrived.
"Kent!"
She beam with joy and practically jumped into his arms the moment she saw him enter the room.
